info.title: Kindgi Platform API
info.description: REST + SSE API for Kindgi: runs, agents, flows, human-in-the-loop approvals and the admin control plane. Generated from the route and schema registrations in `@kindgi/api` and drift-checked against the mounted routes. `info["x-kindgi-capabilities"]` names what this API does that an earlier one didn't: an open list of strings, which a client checks before a request an earlier runtime would take differently, and whose names it doesn't know it ignores.

servers.description: Same-origin — path relative to the deployment root.

tags.name: system
tags.description: Health + spec discovery.

tags.name: runs
tags.description: Run lifecycle (start, list, get, cancel, resume, journal, stream).

tags.name: signing-keys
tags.description: The deployment trust list: the public keys whose signatures `POST /v1/deployments` accepts. Revoked keys stay readable for audit.

tags.name: tokens
tags.description: API token administration (mint + revoke), and public run tokens: short-lived, read-only tokens a browser uses to follow specific runs.

tags.name: system-keys
tags.description: The operator's system keys (`kgi_sy_…`), on a runtime serving many tenants: each acts in no tenant, with the least system scope its service needs (sign-up, the orchestrator, billing, the license renewal), and only the full system capability mints them. A runtime serving one tenant has none.

tags.name: system-tenants
tags.description: The operator's tenants on a runtime serving many: create, list, read, close and suspend them (a project too), and what the control plane sets on each (production, limits, the image prefix), plus the admins' contacts for service notices. System keys only, each route under its own scope.

tags.name: system-usage
tags.description: Usage across tenants, aggregated (counts, sums, first and last times): the control plane's pull for statements. System keys only.

tags.name: usage
tags.description: Your workspace's usage, aggregated: runs, approvals, model calls and projects put in production, counted and summed by project, agent, kind, class, state or day, over the projects you may read. Model-call cost is on `cost`.

tags.name: system-deployments
tags.description: Per-deployment routing, on a runtime serving many tenants: whatever runs each deployment's own pack service (an orchestrator) lists the deployments that need one or should lose theirs, and records where each runs, under `system:deployments`. Support suspends a pack under `system:suspend`. No tenant input ever names a pack's URL.

tags.name: approvals
tags.description: Human-in-the-loop review queue (role-scoped).

tags.name: agents
tags.description: Agent catalog (list, get, publish, unregister — caller-plugged registry).

tags.name: gate-policies
tags.description: What a promotion of an agent must show before a version goes live for a scope (evals step 4b).

tags.name: flows
tags.description: Flow catalog (list, get, publish, unregister — caller-plugged registry). Enables non-agent workflows via HTTP — publish once, execute many via `POST /v1/runs`.

tags.name: tools
tags.description: Tool catalog (list, get, register, unregister — caller-plugged registry, metadata-only).

tags.name: guardrails
tags.description: Guardrail catalog (list, get, register, unregister — caller-plugged registry, metadata-only).

tags.name: conversations
tags.description: Durable multi-turn threads (open, list, get, close, read messages).

tags.name: memory
tags.description: Fact catalog + retrieval (list, get, write, supersede, retrieve — caller-plugged binding wraps the memory subsystem).

tags.name: proposals
tags.description: Supervisor fix-proposal lifecycle (draft, dry-run, submit-review, apply, rollback, withdraw — caller-plugged binding wraps the supervisor).

tags.name: provenance
tags.description: Causal DAG readback + signed exports (list, get, export), signed with the deployment's export key.

tags.name: export-signing-keys
tags.description: The public keys this deployment signs its exports with (audit bundles, provenance, compliance evidence): what a verifier pins.

tags.name: artifacts
tags.description: Blob storage (list metadata, multipart upload, streaming download, HEAD, delete). Caller-plugged via `BlobStorageBinding` (from `@kindgi/blob-binding`).

tags.name: observations
tags.description: Supervisor readback of run outcomes.

tags.name: capabilities
tags.description: Capability catalog (list + get) — part of the admin control plane. Read-only over HTTP. Capabilities are framework-declared (`FEATURES` enum + `@kindgi/specs/capability.schema.json`) and deployment-extended at boot time via `CapabilityRegistryBinding`; tenants do NOT author capabilities via the API.

tags.name: providers
tags.description: Model-provider catalog (list, get, register, unregister, capabilities sub-resource) — part of the admin control plane. Full CRUD. `ProviderMetadata` is the wire shape; secrets never cross the wire (they live inside `ProviderRegistryBinding`). The capability router picks a best-fit provider from this set per capability requirement at run time.

tags.name: judgments
tags.description: Judgments: yes or no, with an optional reason, about one item of a finished run's output, optionally recorded under a judge class (list, get, create, unregister). Each judgment keeps copies of what was judged (the run's input and output, and the item) so they outlive the run's own retention. Who judged comes from the authenticated caller, never the body; an app judging for one of its users passes that user's opaque id as `participantId`. One live judgment per run, item key, caller and participant: judging again supersedes the earlier one, which stays as history. Caller-plugged via `JudgmentRegistryBinding`.

tags.name: judge-classes
tags.description: Judge classes (list, get, create, update, unregister): the deployment's named kinds of judge ("expert", "user", ...), each with a weight, scoped to the tenant, a project, or an agent in a project. A judgment may name a class; an unclassified judgment counts with weight 1. Caller-plugged via `JudgmentRegistryBinding`.

tags.name: mcp
tags.description: MCP-endpoint catalog (list, get, register, unregister). Tenants declare the remote MCP servers (`stdio` / `http-sse` / `streamable-http`) they want the runtime to consume. The runtime discovers each endpoint's tools and registers them into `ToolRegistryBinding` under the same tenant — remote MCP tools become native Kindgi tools without a recompile. Secrets never cross the wire: `secretRef` names a secret in the deployment's store, resolved at the endpoint's tenant scope. A deployment refuses `stdio` endpoints unless `KINDGI_TENANT_HOST_ACCESS=local`. Caller-plugged via `MCPEndpointRegistryBinding`.

tags.name: cost
tags.description: Cost readback (list records, get record, aggregate across a required time window) — part of the admin control plane. Read-only over HTTP; records are written by the runtime usage instrumentation (agents, tools, sandboxes). Caller-plugged via `CostBinding`. Budgets are not enforced through this surface.

tags.name: adapters
tags.description: Unified adapter catalog (list, get, test) — part of the admin control plane. Covers every adapter kind the deployment wired: model providers, embedding providers, blob storage, sandbox providers, eval judges. Read-only + smoke-test-only over HTTP; adapter lifecycle (register / unregister / reconfigure) is a deployment concern — the runtime learns about adapters at `CreateAppInput` time. Caller-plugged via `AdapterRegistryBinding`. Config is REDACTED on the wire — no secrets crossing.

tags.name: policies
tags.description: Tenant policy catalog (list, get, versions, publish, unregister) — part of the admin control plane. Full versioned CRUD, mirrors `flows` 1:1. Registry-only: enforcement is out of scope. `policyKind` selects the shape of `spec` — closed enum, extended additively (`access-control`, `model-routing`, `adapter-allowlist`, `rate-limit`, `retention`, `compliance`). Runtime consumers (e.g. model routing for `model-routing`, retention sweeps for `retention`) read policies from this store and apply them at their own boundary. Caller-plugged via `PolicyRegistryBinding`.

tags.name: retention
tags.description: Deleted rows' retention (scheduled, sweep) — part of the admin control plane. Deleting most things is a tombstone; a `retention` policy per domain (see `policies`) sets how long tombstones stay before a sweep purges them for good. `scheduled` lists what's due and when; `sweep` purges what's past its grace. Nothing sweeps on its own: call `sweep` from a schedule. Caller-plugged via `RetentionBinding`.

tags.name: eval-suites
tags.description: Evaluation suite catalog (list, get, versions, publish, unregister) — part of the admin control plane. Full versioned CRUD, mirrors `policies` 1:1. Registry-only: eval-run execution + per-kind grader dispatch live on the `eval-runs` tag. `evalKind` selects the shape of `spec` — closed enum, extended additively (`accuracy`, `pairwise`, `regression`, `human-review`, `benchmark`, `custom`, `judged`). The cases of a `judged` suite are copies of judged runs built from judgments (`POST .../versions/from-judgments`, listed at `GET .../versions/{version}/cases`; `EvalCaseStoreBinding`). Runs against these suites are started through the `eval-runs` tag. Caller-plugged via `EvalSuiteRegistryBinding`.

tags.name: blocks
tags.description: Data blocks: versioned prompts and settings an agent version pins when it's published (list, get, versions, publish, unregister, reinstate). A version never changes, nor does a block's kind; a settings block's values satisfy its schema and the latest version's. A block belongs to one project and is authorized through it: `read` on the project to read, `write` to publish, unregister or reinstate. Caller-plugged via `BlockRegistryBinding`.

tags.name: eval-runs
tags.description: Eval-run data plane (start, list, get, cancel, events SSE). Dispatches an eval run against a registered suite. Dispatch is per-`EvalKind`; kinds without a registered dispatcher return `422 dispatcher-not-registered`. `result` is kind-specific opaque JSON on the wire — for `accuracy` it is `{ passCount, totalCount, meanScore, perCase[] }`. SSE events mirror run streaming: per-case progress followed by a terminal frame carrying the aggregate. Caller-plugged via `EvalRunBinding`.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: OIDC and SAML identity providers + session lifecycle. Layers browser-based auth on top of the static bearer-token surface: bearer tokens continue to work byte-shape-identical; session tokens use the `kgi_sk_*` prefix so the same middleware routes both flavors. Providers are caller-plugged via `IdentityProviderBinding` (no baked-in list); sign-in runs in the deployment, which reads them. Sessions persist via `SessionStoreBinding`. `clientSecretRef` is a REFERENCE — the plaintext secret never crosses the wire.

tags.name: identity
tags.description: Tenant-scoped identity directory (list, get, list-active-sessions, revoke-sessions, whoami) — part of the admin control plane. Caller-plugged via `IdentityDirectoryBinding` — deployments plug in their own user store (LDAP, SCIM, or bespoke). Registry-only over HTTP: the framework does NOT own user persistence. The directory is flat; groups, roles, invitations, directory sync and impersonation are not part of this surface. `primaryEmail` may be redacted per tenant policy — the routes treat it as opaque. Provider access-token / refresh-token NEVER cross the wire, even to admins.

tags.name: deployments
tags.description: Signed pack deployments (register, list, get). The single wire surface that lands a signed OCI image + index.json into the platform. Register runs a six-step atomic transaction: Ed25519 signature verify over the canonical `{imageDigest, artifactVersion, indexHash, tenantId, publishedAt}` envelope, tenant-scoped trust-list check via `SigningKeyRegistryBinding`, image pullability + `/app/index.json` sha256 match via `ImageRegistryBinding`, per-primitive manifest validation, registry upserts (tools + guardrails + agents + flows), append-only deployment ledger row via `DeploymentBinding`. All-or-nothing rollback on any failure; digest-based idempotency (redeploying the same image returns the existing record). Records are immutable — rollback = re-register the previous digest.

tags.name: compliance
tags.description: Compliance-evidence readback + signed exports (list, get, export). Reads are a classification lens over `AuditEventBinding`; only classifier-marked `exportable` kinds appear on the wire. A signed export is signed with the export signing key of the deployment (`exportSigning`); a deployment without one answers `404 signing-not-configured`. It is the same envelope as the audit-bundle and provenance exports, so one verifier reads all three. Redaction happens when evidence is generated, not at the export boundary — records are stored already redacted.

tags.name: audit
tags.description: PDP decision audit stream (list). Every route-level authz `check()` emits one `AuditEvent` (kind `authz-decision`) via the `AuditEventBinding`; this route pages through them, tenant-scoped, with `?actorSubject=` / `?onBehalfOf=` / `?action=` / `?resource=` / `?outcome=` / `?runId=` / `?from=` / `?to=` filters. Admin@tenant only. This view is a filtered projection of the tenant audit events.

tags.name: orgs
tags.description: Multi-tenant hierarchy — Org CRUD (list, create, get, patch, delete). Optional structural subdivision within a tenant; small tenants ignore Orgs entirely. Caller-plugged via `OrgBinding` from `@kindgi/platform`.

tags.name: teams
tags.description: Multi-tenant hierarchy — Team CRUD (list, create, get, patch, delete) + `TeamMembership` sub-resource (list, add, updateRole, remove). People-groups that work together on projects; users belong to many teams. Team memberships are framework-owned (no external directory sync). Membership add is idempotent on `(teamId, userId)` — role mutation goes through PATCH.

tags.name: projects
tags.description: Multi-tenant hierarchy — Project CRUD (list, create, get, patch, delete) + `/projects/default` shortcut + `ProjectMembership` sub-resource (list, add, updateRole, remove). Primary content scope: every content resource belongs to exactly one project. The Default project (`isDefault: true`) is auto-created per tenant at inception — exactly one per tenant, enforced at the storage layer.

tags.name: judging
tags.description: A project's judging rules (which runs to queue for a person's judgment when they end) and the queue they fill. Rules only list runs; nothing here starts a model.

tags.name: tenant
tags.description: Sovereignty boundary readback + tenant-scoped config (get tenant; list + upsert entries routed to the env / secrets bindings). There is no `/v1/tenants` collection — the caller's tenant is implicit from the bearer token. `PATCH /config` routes writes to `SecretBinding` when `sensitive: true` OR `kind: "secret"`; else to `EnvBinding`. `GET /config` merges both bindings at tenant scope; secret values are ALWAYS redacted here. The `/config` sub-routes mount when at least one of `envBinding` / `secretsBinding` is wired. Prefer `/v1/env/*` + `/v1/secrets/*` for new callers.

tags.name: env
tags.description: Non-sensitive per-env values (`/v1/env/*`). Every route requires `envName` + `scopeKind` (+ `scopeId` for org / project); `value` is present on every read path (env is non-sensitive by definition). Writes require the `env:write` capability. Caller-plugged via `EnvBinding` (`@kindgi/env-inmemory` is an in-memory implementation for development and tests).

tags.name: secrets
tags.description: Sensitive per-env values (`/v1/secrets/*`). The ONLY endpoint that accepts plaintext is `POST /v1/secrets`; every other route is metadata-only (`value` NEVER returns on list / get / listVersions / getVersion — structural redaction). Rotation is discriminated: sync providers return 201 inline, async providers return 202 with a status URL + SSE events URL. A hard revoke erases the value, which can't be undone; backups, and a secret manager's own retention, may keep copies for a time. Every mutating route is capability-gated (`secrets:write`, `secrets:rotate`, `secrets:revoke`, `secrets:revoke:hard`).

tags.name: schedules
tags.description: Run an agent or a flow on a schedule: a cron expression in a timezone. Each occurrence is one fire, which starts one run as the schedule's owner (re-checked at every fire), through the same path as `POST /v1/runs`; a run a schedule started names it (`Run.trigger`). After a gap, `catchUp` runs once for the latest missed occurrence (or skips them), never once per missed one; `overlap` skips an occurrence while the previous run is still going. `GET …/fires` is the schedule's history; `run-now` fires it outside the schedule. Mounted when the deployment fires schedules.

tags.name: mail-triggers
tags.description: Mail triggers: each new mail in a mailbox's folder starts a run of an agent or a flow, as the trigger's owner. A thread's mail runs one at a time, and each run continues the thread's conversation.

tags.name: webhook-endpoints
tags.description: Outbound webhooks: endpoints the platform sends signed events to (`run.finished` when a top-level run completes, fails or is cancelled), their delivery log, redelivery and a test event. Signed in the Standard Webhooks format with a secret the endpoint references by name (`secretRef`); delivered at least once, so receivers deduplicate on `webhook-id`. Event bodies are under `webhooks`. Not to be confused with `/v1/webhooks`, which are inbound triggers. Caller-plugged via `WebhookEndpointBinding`.

tags.name: connections
tags.description: Accounts at other apps (a member's Google account, the company's GitHub App) that tools act with. `connection-entries` lists the apps this server can connect to; `connection-apps` is the tenant's own registration of its client at an app (a tenant admin's, secrets by reference); `connections` are the accounts connected through them, with the connect that makes one (`requests`, `start`, `finish`). A connection is a member's own or the company's, and its token never leaves the server. `POST /v1/connection-notices/{tenantId}/{appId}` is where an app reports a removal, signed its own way. Caller-plugged via `ConnectionBinding`.

tags.name: sites
tags.description: Sites that sign their own people in to one project: a site (a WordPress admin, say) vouches for whoever is signed in there, so they ask the project's agents and decide its approvals as themselves. A site holds its own Ed25519 key; Kindgi only ever has the public half.

code.description: Stable machine-readable discriminant. Values match domain error codes (see `docs/API-ROUTE-CONVENTIONS.md` §4.3).

requestId.description: Server-assigned request id; also echoed via `X-Request-Id` header.

RunAgent.description: Set on an agent's turn (an agent run, or the turn a flow's agent step started): the agent, the version that ran and the conversation. Absent on other runs, and on turns that ran before Kindgi 0.1.3.

version.description: The agent version that ran (semver).

via.description: Why this version ran: named by the caller (`explicit`); held by the flow version a flow's agent step runs in (`flow-pin`: the node's `config.version`, else the version the flow version pinned when it was published); the conversation's own (`conversation`); the version live for the run's scope (`live`); or the latest, nothing being live (`latest`). Absent on runs from before Kindgi 0.1.4.

liveScope.description: The pin that chose the version, when `via` is `live`.

RunWaitingFor.description: Set on a suspended run by `GET /v1/runs/{runId}` (not the list): what it waits for, its journal's open waits. `approvals`: those still to be decided, linked to the waits. `connections`: the connects it waits for. `tokens`: its waits for another system's answer. `other`: the rest. Absent from a runtime before Kindgi 0.1.6, or when the journal can't be read; `kindgi runs resume` then works it out itself.

connections.description: The connects the run waits for. Left out when there are none.

tokens.description: Its waits for another system's answer (a pausing tool's calls). Absent on a runtime that pauses no run, or when they can't be read: those waits are then `unattributed`.

items.description: `child-run` (`childRunId`, `childStatus`, `timesOutAt`): a child run must finish. `decided-approval` (`approvalId`, `approvalStatus`): decided, the runtime continues. `unattributed` (`tokenId`, `timesOutAt`): a wait no approval is linked to. `no-open-wait`: the journal shows none; the runtime picks the run up again.

RunWaitingApproval.description: An approval the run waits for, as a run reader sees it: its identity and state. Its subject's details, description, context and decision stay on `GET /v1/approvals/{approvalId}`, behind the reviewer gate.

requiredRole.description: The reviewer role that may decide it, or above.

subjectKind.description: What waits: e.g. `tool-call:pending` (a tool call held for review).

tool.description: For a tool call held for review: which tool and which call. Never the call's arguments.

callId.description: The model's id for the call.

RunWaitingToken.description: A wait for another system's answer: a pack tool that declares `pauses` handed its wait token's link on. Answer it through the link, or with `POST /v1/runs/{runId}/resume` and this `tokenId`. Never the link itself.

name.description: What the run waits for, as the tool named it.

callId.description: The model's id for the call, for an agent's call.

nodeId.description: The flow step that waits, for a flow's tool step.

timesOutAt.description: When the wait times out, and the call fails with `wait-token-timed-out`.

RunTrigger.description: Set on a run a trigger started: the trigger and the fire that started it. Absent on other runs. `kind` is the trigger's kind: `schedule`, `event`, `webhook` (an inbound webhook) or `mail` (new mail in a mailbox).

fireId.description: The fire that started the run: one entry of the trigger's fire history.

scheduledFor.description: A schedule's fire: the occurrence the run is for.

LiveScopeTenant.description: The agent's default for the whole tenant.

LiveScopeSegment.description: A segment path within a project: it covers every run whose path starts with it.

LiveScope.description: Where a live version is pinned, from least to most specific: tenant, org, project, segment path. A run takes the most specific pin that covers it.

version.description: The version a run would use (semver).

via.description: A live pin chose it, or nothing is live on the way up and it is the latest.

data.description: Its first project first, then the others, each once.

Promotion.description: One change of a scope's live version, kept for good: what was live before, what is after, who asked and why.

fromVersion.description: The scope's own pin before; null when it had none.

toVersion.description: The scope's own pin after; null after an unpin.

evalRunId.description: The comparison the change was judged on.

status.description: A `promote` row's state: it changes once, from `pending-approval` to its final state. Absent on rollback and unpin rows, and on promotions made before gates (`promoted`).

policy.description: The gate policy that applied; null when none did. Absent before gates.

approvalId.description: The approval a `pending-approval` promotion waits on (kept once decided).

resolvedAt.description: When a `pending-approval` promotion reached its final state.

GateCheck.description: One of a gate's checks, as the promotion records it.

message.description: A plain sentence: what was found against what the policy asks.

GateApproval.description: The approval a passing promotion waits for.

separateApprover.description: Whoever asked for the promotion may not approve it.

GatePolicySpec.description: What a promotion must show. Every part is optional; an empty spec checks nothing. A promotion must name a comparison (`evalRunId`) exactly when the spec has `comparison`, `evidence`, `metrics`, `replay` or `onlyRestrictedClasses`. Unknown keys are refused.

evidence.description: The judged evidence behind each gated metric; for a metric with `maxDrop`, the baseline's too.

k.description: `weightedPrecisionAtK` only: the summary's `k` must be this.

maxDrop.description: How far the candidate may fall below the baseline (the live version).

replay.description: Each knob left out of the block is 0. No block: no replay checks.

maxRefusedWrites.description: At most this many tool calls the replay refused (the comparison summary's `refusedWrites`). Reads count too, despite the name.

approvals.description: A passing promotion waits for a reviewer.

onlyRestrictedClasses.description: Only restricted judge classes count: the comparison must be weighted `restricted-only`, so a class anyone may assert can't move the gate.

policy.description: The policy that gates a promotion for the scope; null when none does.

PromotionCheck.description: What the gate would say about a promotion. Nothing is recorded.

policy.description: The policy that applies; null when none does.

version.description: The agent version to make live (registered, active).

evalRunId.description: The comparison this promotion was judged on.

toVersion.description: An earlier version to go back to; omit → the scope's previous live version.

failureMessage.description: The failure as the runtime recorded it. Read `failure` instead: an agent turn records its typed error here in an internal form.

output.description: The run's output once it completed. Present on single-run responses; on lists only with `?include=output`.

contentErasedAt.description: When an erasure cleared the run's content (its input, output, failure message and journal payloads): a person's words were erased. Structure (status, times, ids) stays.

parentRunId.description: Set on a child run (a sub-flow run, or the agent turn an agent step started): the run that started it.

parentNodeId.description: Set on a child run: the node in the parent run that started it.

startedBy.description: How the run started, recorded when it was created and never changed: `person` (a person, signed in or with their own API key), `key` (a service account's key), or the kind of trigger that fired it: `schedule`, `webhook`, `event` or `mail`. A child run has its parent's. Only `person` counts as attended: in any other run, or one without this field (runs from before runs recorded it), a tool that declares `needsApprovalWhenUnattended` waits for a person's yes.

actsFor.description: Whom the run acts for, whose access it has, recorded when it was created and never changed: `user:<id>` (a person) or `service_account:<id>` (a service account), the same strings as an approval's `requestedBy`, a conversation's `openedBy` and `whoami`'s `actor`. A person who starts a run, signed in or with their own API key, is whom it acts for, and so is a service account whose key starts one. A run a schedule, a webhook or a mail trigger fired (`startedBy` `schedule`, `webhook` or `mail`) acts for the trigger's owner when it fired; a child run for its parent's; an agent acting for someone for that someone. An approval or a resume doesn't change it. An id, never a name: show the caller's own as `you`, and a name only where the caller may read that person or service account. Absent on a run that acts for no one (a system job, an agent on its own, an eval run's replay run) and on runs from before runs recorded it. Never on a public run token's progress view or its stream, nor on the `run.finished` webhook's run.

toolsAllowedUnattended.description: The tools, by id, whose calls in this run don't wait for a person's yes though no person started it: the list of the webhook or schedule that fired it, as it was when the run started, and never changed after. A child run has its parent's. Absent: none.

replayOf.description: Set on a replay run (an eval run re-running a past run): the run it replays.

evalRunId.description: Set on a replay run: the eval run that started it.

segments.description: The segment path the run was started with (coarse to fine), which picks live agent versions. A child run has its parent's. Absent when there was none.

traceId.description: The W3C trace id of the request that started the run: the caller's (from its `traceparent`) or one the API minted. The runtime's records about the run carry it; `GET` responses answer `traceresponse` with each request's own. Absent for a run no request started, and on runs from before runs recorded it.

publicAccessToken.description: Only in the response to `POST /v1/runs`, when the deployment issues public run tokens: a read-only token for this run (and its descendants) to hand to a browser, for `GET /v1/runs/{runId}/progress` and its stream.

RunFailure.description: Why a failed run failed; present only on a `failed` run. An agent turn's failure carries its own code (`budget-exceeded`, `capability-routing-failed`, `model-invocation-failed`, …; `rate-limit-exceeded` when a budget kept per tenant refused work the turn needed, with `details` naming the budget); any other failure is `run-failed`, with the run's failure message.

cause.description: What the error came from, when it says: e.g. for `capability-routing-failed`, the router's `capability-unsatisfiable` with its reasons, by provider.

reason.description: The error's own reason, when it gives one: for a turn that ended at its approval (`hitl-cancelled`), `timeout` when nobody decided in time. Absent from an older runtime and from errors without one; read `code` then.

details.description: The error's own facts, for a code that has them: for `rate-limit-exceeded`, `limit` (the budget that refused: `schema-compile-time` or `template-render-time`) and `budgetMs`, the names the API's `429` uses. Never the wait: read back later, it's stale. Absent for any other code, and from an older runtime.

FailureSubject.description: Whose runs a failure group counts: an agent's turns, or a flow's runs.

FailureGroup.description: One group of failed runs: the same cause, subject and version.

code.description: The failure's code (`Run.failure.code`). Absent when not grouped by code, and in `unrecorded`.

reason.description: The failure's reason (`Run.failure.reason`), when it gives one: a `hitl-*` outcome's, e.g. `timeout`.

version.description: The agent's or flow's version. Absent when not grouped by version, or not recorded for the run.

firstSeen.description: When the first of them failed, in the window.

lastSeen.description: When the latest of them failed, in the window.

outcomes.description: People's decisions, never errors: `hitl-*` codes (an approval rejected, cancelled or timed out), the most first.

unrecorded.description: Runs that failed before their cause was recorded (a runtime from before this): by subject and version only, never by code.

total.description: Every failed run in the window, across the three lists.

dryRun.description: When true, the run executes with side-effects mocked; the row is marked `dryRun: true`.

wait.description: When false, respond `202` as soon as the run exists and finish it in the background; poll `GET /v1/runs/{runId}` for its status and output. Default true: respond `201` once the run completes, fails or suspends.

agentVersion.description: Semver. Omit → the conversation's own version for a follow-up turn, else the version live for the run's scope, else the latest.

projectId.description: Project to run under; omit → the tenant's Default project.

segments.description: The run's segment path below its project, coarse to fine (an app-defined finer scope, e.g. company then role). A version live on a prefix of it serves the run.

waitpointId.description: Token id of the pending waitpoint to complete: a `pause:` id, from the run's `waitingFor.tokens`. Ids starting with `child:` and `pause:` are reserved for the runtime: a handler never waits on one of its own. Resuming without a waitpoint id returns `400 bad-input`.

value.description: The answer: the paused tool's output, checked against its output schema. Absent: `{}`.

failureMessage.description: The failure as the runtime recorded it. Read `failure` instead: an agent turn records its typed error here in an internal form.

output.description: The run's output once it completed. Present on single-run responses; on lists only with `?include=output`.

contentErasedAt.description: When an erasure cleared the run's content (its input, output, failure message and journal payloads): a person's words were erased. Structure (status, times, ids) stays.

parentRunId.description: Set on a child run (a sub-flow run, or the agent turn an agent step started): the run that started it.

parentNodeId.description: Set on a child run: the node in the parent run that started it.

startedBy.description: How the run started, recorded when it was created and never changed: `person` (a person, signed in or with their own API key), `key` (a service account's key), or the kind of trigger that fired it: `schedule`, `webhook`, `event` or `mail`. A child run has its parent's. Only `person` counts as attended: in any other run, or one without this field (runs from before runs recorded it), a tool that declares `needsApprovalWhenUnattended` waits for a person's yes.

actsFor.description: Whom the run acts for, whose access it has, recorded when it was created and never changed: `user:<id>` (a person) or `service_account:<id>` (a service account), the same strings as an approval's `requestedBy`, a conversation's `openedBy` and `whoami`'s `actor`. A person who starts a run, signed in or with their own API key, is whom it acts for, and so is a service account whose key starts one. A run a schedule, a webhook or a mail trigger fired (`startedBy` `schedule`, `webhook` or `mail`) acts for the trigger's owner when it fired; a child run for its parent's; an agent acting for someone for that someone. An approval or a resume doesn't change it. An id, never a name: show the caller's own as `you`, and a name only where the caller may read that person or service account. Absent on a run that acts for no one (a system job, an agent on its own, an eval run's replay run) and on runs from before runs recorded it. Never on a public run token's progress view or its stream, nor on the `run.finished` webhook's run.

toolsAllowedUnattended.description: The tools, by id, whose calls in this run don't wait for a person's yes though no person started it: the list of the webhook or schedule that fired it, as it was when the run started, and never changed after. A child run has its parent's. Absent: none.

replayOf.description: Set on a replay run (an eval run re-running a past run): the run it replays.

evalRunId.description: Set on a replay run: the eval run that started it.

segments.description: The segment path the run was started with (coarse to fine), which picks live agent versions. A child run has its parent's. Absent when there was none.

traceId.description: The W3C trace id of the request that started the run: the caller's (from its `traceparent`) or one the API minted. The runtime's records about the run carry it; `GET` responses answer `traceresponse` with each request's own. Absent for a run no request started, and on runs from before runs recorded it.

publicAccessToken.description: Only in the response to `POST /v1/runs`, when the deployment issues public run tokens: a read-only token for this run (and its descendants) to hand to a browser, for `GET /v1/runs/{runId}/progress` and its stream.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent when `hasMore: false`. See `docs/API-ROUTE-CONVENTIONS.md` §5.

JournalKind.description: Runtime journal kind (bare — distinct from the SSE-only `run.*-*` wire enum in `@kindgi/specs/run-event.schema.json`).

kind.description: Runtime journal kind (bare — distinct from the SSE-only `run.*-*` wire enum in `@kindgi/specs/run-event.schema.json`).
Runtime journal kind (bare — distinct from the SSE-only `run.*-*` wire enum in `@kindgi/specs/run-event.schema.json`).

eventId.description: Monotonic event id within the run. Sent as the SSE `id:` line and echoed back via `Last-Event-Id` on reconnect.

RunProgress.description: A run's progress: status and timing, without its input, output, failure message or tenant. Safe to show in a browser.

RunProgressEvent.description: A run event without its payload: what happened, on which node, when.

eventId.description: Sent as the SSE `id:` line; echo it back in `Last-Event-Id` to resume.

MintTokenBody.description: A new API key. `for` is whom it acts for: the caller by default; only a tenant admin mints for someone else.

role.description: The most the key may do, under its principal's grants: an `admin` key may administer the tenant when its principal is a tenant admin; a `member` key takes no admin action on the tenant, whoever it's for; below it, its principal's roles hold (a project admin's member key administers that project). Default `member`; `admin` needs a tenant admin minting it.

capabilities.description: Framework capabilities the key carries (`env:write`, `secrets:write`, …). A caller can only grant capabilities it holds. Default none.

expiresAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp. Absent: the key never expires. When the minting key expires (or the key a token sign-in session was opened with), it's required and no later than that key's (`token-expiry-exceeds-minter`).

projectId.description: Limit the key to this project: a request naming another project is refused (`key-project-mismatch`). A key limited to a project mints only keys limited to it.

revokedAt.description: Set once revoked; a revoked key never authenticates again.

lastUsedAt.description: When the key last authenticated a request (updated at most once a minute).

token.description: Plaintext bearer token. Returned exactly once at mint time.

SystemKey.description: A system key (`kgi_sy_…`): the operator's, acting in no tenant. Never its secret.

mintedBy.description: Who minted it: a system key's id, or `boot` for the deployment's own token.

RevokeSystemKeyResult.description: The revoked system key, and the keys revoked with it because they were minted from it.
