SystemDeploymentEntry.description: A deployment as whatever runs its pack service needs it: ids and the image, nothing of the tenant beyond its id. Name the service `packServiceName(tenantId, deploymentId)` (`@kindgi/api`). In the `retire` list, `reason` says why the service should go.

packId.description: The pack it deploys (the image index's `packId`).

projectId.description: The deployment's project, as a call routes in it: the one it named, else the tenant's Default. Absent only when the tenant has no Default project.

imageRef.description: Digest-pinned, as registered: the pack service is created from exactly this.

reason.description: In the `retire` list only. `superseded`: newer deployments ship every tool version and check it does, so no new call reaches it. A tool call a step made on it still goes back to it when the step runs again, and fails closed (`pack-endpoint-cleared`) once its endpoint is cleared. `tenant-closing`, `tenant-suspended`: every deployment of the tenant, routed or not. `project-suspended`, `pack-suspended`: every deployment of the project, or this one.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent when `hasMore: false`.

url.description: `https://<host>`: no user info, path, query or fragment. Its host must be on the operator's allowlist (`KINDGI_PACK_ENDPOINT_HOSTS`) and begin with the deployment's own service name (`packServiceName`), then `-` or `.`.

auth.description: How the server calls it: `google-id-token` adds an ID token for the URL (Cloud Run's invoker check) to the pack token; `token` sends the pack token only.

token.description: The pack service's token (`KINDGI_PACK_SERVICE_TOKEN`), printable ASCII without spaces. Stored wrapped; never returned, logged or recorded.

packEnvRevision.description: The `revision` from `GET …/pack-env` whose values the service was made with, when its pack declares an environment. Kept as the one it runs, so `GET /v1/system/pack-env` lists it once they change.

PackEnvDeclaration.description: The names the pack service reads from its process environment, as the image's `index.json` declares them (`env`), each list in name order. Names only, never a value. On a deployment: absent when it declares none, and from older servers.

required.description: Names the pack service needs, set and non-empty, to be ready.

optional.description: Names the pack reads when present.

PackEnvScope.description: Where a value is set: the deployment's project, the project's org, or the tenant.

id.description: The project's or the org's id. Absent for the tenant.

PackEnvNameStatus.description: One name the deployment's pack declares: where it's set, and why it can't be given to the pack service, if it can't (`secretScope`, for `ambiguous` only, names the secret's scope). Each name is looked for at the deployment's project, then its org, then the tenant (most specific wins); a tenant-wide deployment's, at the tenant's Default project. Never a value.

kind.description: What it is set as: a plain value (`env`) or a secret. `null` when it is set nowhere.

scope.description: Where it is set: the plain value's scope when `ambiguous`. `null` when it is set nowhere.

missing.description: Set nowhere, as a plain value or a secret (optional names too).

problem.description: Why it can't be given to the pack service. `ambiguous`: set both as a secret and as a plain value (`secretScope` names the secret's scope). `secret-not-yet`: set only as a secret, and the orchestrator didn't ask for secret values (`secrets=values`); a tool reads it per call (`ctx.secrets`). `missing`: a required name set nowhere. `unreadable`: set as a secret, and it can't be read for a reason the platform fixes, not the owner. Absent when it can be given, and for an optional name set nowhere. The owner's check (`GET /v1/deployments/{deploymentId}/pack-env`) lists a name set only as a secret as `kind: 'secret'`, with no problem.

PackEnvProblemCode.description: Why a deployment's pack service can't be given its declared environment, the first in this order: `pack-env-ambiguous` (a name is set both as a secret and as a plain value), `pack-env-secret-not-yet` (a name is set only as a secret, and its value wasn't asked for), `pack-env-missing` (a required name is set nowhere), `pack-env-secret-unreadable` (a name's secret is set, but it can't be read for a reason the platform fixes, not the owner; only a read with `secrets=values` finds it, and only when there's no other problem). A later runtime may add codes, so treat an unknown one as a reason not yet named.

PackEnvHeldCode.description: Why a `ready` pack service runs on the values it was last given: a `PackEnvProblemCode`, so the newest can't be given to it; `pack-env-update-failed`: they were given, and its new revision with them didn't start, so the last ready one serves. That revision is tried again for an hour after it's first recorded; setting the values again is a new revision, tried again too. The orchestrator couldn't give it its secrets: `pack-env-secrets-unaudited` (the runtime has nowhere to audit a secret it gives out, so it gives none; the platform fixes it), `pack-env-secret-too-large` (a secret's value is over 32768 bytes, the most a pack service can be given), `pack-env-secret-redeploy` (a name is now set only as a secret, and this pack service was made where no secret can be given to it; a new deployment's can be, from a new build of the pack). A service held as `pack-env-secret-unreadable` or `pack-env-secrets-unaudited` is listed by `GET /v1/system/pack-env` every time, with its `held`, as the revision doesn't move when the platform fixes it. A later runtime may add codes, so treat an unknown one as a reason not yet named.

SystemPackEnv.description: What the deployment's pack service is to be given: where each declared name is set, and the values when nothing stands in the way, plain ones in `env` and, when asked for (`secrets=values`), secrets in `secrets`. Each value given out is on the audit record: `env-resolved` as the deployment's system read, and `secret-resolved` (caller `pack-env`, with the request id as its `correlationId` and the system key's id), written before the answer.

revision.description: Changes whenever what would be given changes: a value written or removed, a secret set or revoked. Made from scopes, row ids, revisions and update times, never from a value. Send it back with the endpoint (`packEnvRevision`) or `PUT …/pack-env`.

names.description: Every declared name, required ones first, each list in name order.

env.description: Each declared name that is set, by name, as plain values. Absent while there is a `problem`: then nothing is given, and the service keeps what it runs.

secrets.description: With `secrets=values` only: each declared name that is set only as a secret, by name (`{}` when there's none). Never put one into a plain env. Absent while there is a `problem`, and when it wasn't asked for.

PackEnvSecretValue.description: A secret given to the deployment's pack service: its value, read at the version `revision` names, and audited before the answer.

revision.description: `ps1-…`: the same for the same value under the same name, and changes whenever what's given for the name does (a new version, another scope, a revoke or a delete). Made from the name's part of the deployment's `revision`, never from the value.

SystemPackEnvEntry.description: A deployment whose pack service runs on declared env values that changed since: ids, the image, and the revision it runs. Never a value. Name the service `packServiceName(tenantId, deploymentId)` (`@kindgi/api`).

packId.description: The pack it deploys (the image index's `packId`).

projectId.description: The deployment's project, as a call routes in it: the one it named, else the tenant's Default. Absent only when the tenant has no Default project.

imageRef.description: Digest-pinned, as registered: the pack service is created from exactly this.

appliedRevision.description: The revision its service runs: given with its endpoint, or recorded since. Absent: none was. Send it back as `appliedRevision` with `PUT …/pack-env`.

SystemPackEnvHold.description: Only when it's held at its current revision for a cause the platform fixes, not the owner: it's listed every time, as the revision doesn't move when that's fixed. Read its values again when your back-off says. Absent otherwise.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent when `hasMore: false`.

revision.description: The `revision` from `GET …/pack-env`. Without `held`: the service now runs its values. With `held`: they weren't given, and the service keeps what it runs.

appliedRevision.description: The revision the service was found running, as `GET /v1/system/pack-env` listed it. Absent: none was recorded. Another revision recorded since is a conflict (`pack-env-conflict`).

PackEnvNames.description: Where each name the deployment's pack declares is set, at the env the server serves. Never a value.

envName.description: The env the values are read at (`KINDGI_ENV`).

data.description: Every declared name, required ones first, each list in name order.

code.description: Why the pack service couldn't be created, or was refused: one of `DEPLOYMENT_ENDPOINT_PROBLEM_CODES`. The tenant sees the code, never more.

SystemTenant.description: A tenant, as the operator sees it: never its content.

state.description: `closing`: readable and exportable with its own keys for its window, nothing runs. `suspended`: the same, reversibly. `closing` wins over `suspended`.

test.description: A test tenant: left out of usage, invoices and counts.

imagePrefix.description: The repository its deployments' images must sit at or under, `<host>/<path>`.

slug.description: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens; generated when absent.

productionAllowed.description: Whether it may put projects in production. Absent: blocked, until the operator allows it; `true` takes `system:tenants:production`.

test.description: A test tenant. The full system capability only.

imagePrefix.description: The repository its deployments' images must sit in, `<host>/<path>` with no trailing slash; takes `system:tenants:image-prefix`. On a runtime serving many tenants, a tenant without one can't register a deployment.

firstAdmin.description: The person made the tenant's admin and member, by email: the runtime's own sign-in finds them. The runtime gives them every capability but `secrets:reveal`, to put on the keys they make. Absent: the answer carries an admin key instead, which takes the full system capability.

adminKey.description: The tenant's first admin key, without `firstAdmin`: shown once.

nextCursor.description: Opaque; absent when `hasMore` is false.

confirm.description: The tenant's slug, a second check on the id.

TenantTableRows.description: A tenant's rows in one table: the table's name and a count.

complete.description: `true`: nothing of the tenant is left, its purge record is written, and it's marked purged. `false`: `left` and `objectsLeft` say what is; run it again.

alreadyPurged.description: It was marked purged before this run: what this run deleted was written after its mark. Its mark and its record stay as they were.

purgedAt.description: When it was marked purged. Absent while something of it from before the mark is left.

deleted.description: Rows this run deleted, per table with any: table names and counts, never the rows' content.

objectsDeleted.description: Objects this run deleted from the artifacts' store.

authzStoreDeleted.description: Whether this run deleted its authorization store.

left.description: Rows of it still there afterwards, per table; empty when none are. A table the purge doesn't delete from is named too: report it.

objectsLeft.description: Objects still under its prefix in the artifacts' store.

leftBecause.description: Why what's left wasn't deleted, when it's a setting the runtime lacks.

keyId.description: The system key's id, or `boot` for the deployment's own token.

ApiToken.description: An API key. Never includes the secret. `principal` is whom it acts for; absent on a key that is a service account of its own (`service_account:<tokenId>`), as keys minted before principals are.

role.description: The most the key may do, under its principal's grants: an `admin` key may administer the tenant when its principal is a tenant admin; a `member` key takes no admin action on the tenant, whoever it's for; below it, its principal's roles hold (a project admin's member key administers that project).

capabilities.description: Framework capabilities the key carries (`env:write`, `secrets:write`, …). A caller can only grant capabilities it holds.

projectId.description: The project the key is limited to.

revokedAt.description: Set once revoked; a revoked key never authenticates again.

lastUsedAt.description: When the key last authenticated a request (updated at most once a minute).

items.description: An API key. Never includes the secret. `principal` is whom it acts for; absent on a key that is a service account of its own (`service_account:<tokenId>`), as keys minted before principals are.

role.description: The most the key may do, under its principal's grants: an `admin` key may administer the tenant when its principal is a tenant admin; a `member` key takes no admin action on the tenant, whoever it's for; below it, its principal's roles hold (a project admin's member key administers that project).

capabilities.description: Framework capabilities the key carries (`env:write`, `secrets:write`, …). A caller can only grant capabilities it holds.

projectId.description: The project the key is limited to.

revokedAt.description: Set once revoked; a revoked key never authenticates again.

lastUsedAt.description: When the key last authenticated a request (updated at most once a minute).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent when `hasMore: false`.

ApiKeyPrincipal.description: Whom an API key acts for: a person, or a service account.

id.description: The user id, or the service account id.

ServiceAccountGrantTenantMember.description: Tenant member: read the tenant's settings (providers, policies, adapters, signing keys, deployments), not its projects. A service account has it only when granted; a person has it from being added.

ServiceAccountGrantProject.description: A role on one project; it replaces the account's role there.

ServiceAccountGrantProjectBody.description: A role to give on one project; it replaces the account's role there.

ServiceAccountGrant.description: What a service account may do: tenant admin, tenant member (read the tenant's settings), or a role on one project.

ServiceAccountGrantBody.description: The grant to add: tenant admin, tenant member, or a role on one project.

ServiceAccountUngrantProject.description: Whatever role the account has on one project.

ServiceAccountUngrantBody.description: The grant to remove: tenant admin, tenant member, or the role on a project.

ServiceAccount.description: A named, non-human principal (`service_account:<id>`) for an app, a pipeline or a schedule. It acts through API keys minted for it.

name.description: Unique among the tenant's active accounts.

unregisteredAt.description: Set once unregistered: it has no grants, and its keys no longer work.

projectId.description: Set on a project's own account: made by the first trigger that runs as the project (`runAsProject`), with the `editor` role on it. It runs only the triggers with `runAsProject`, not the project's other shared triggers. It has no keys, and its grant is fixed. Unregistering it stops those triggers until an admin takes each over; deleting the project unregisters it.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, e.g. `acme-ci`.

items.description: The grant to add: tenant admin, tenant member, or a role on one project.

grants.description: Written before the account is returned, so its first key works at once.

TrustedSigningKey.description: A public key the tenant trusts to sign deployments (`POST /v1/deployments`). A revoked key stays readable, with `revokedAt`, so the deployments it signed can be audited; it verifies no new ones.

keyId.description: The signer key id a deployment envelope names.

publicKey.description: Base64 of the raw public-key bytes (32 for Ed25519).

keyId.description: The id deployment envelopes name as `signerKeyId`. Bound to `publicKey` for good: rotate by trusting a new id.

publicKey.description: Base64 of the 32 raw bytes of the Ed25519 public key.

revoked.description: `false` when the key was unknown or already revoked.

runIds.description: The runs the token may read; their descendants are readable too.

expiresInSeconds.description: Lifetime; the deployment default (15 minutes) when absent.

ReviewerRole.description: Reviewer role class. Hierarchy: standard < senior < admin.

requiredRole.description: Reviewer role class. Hierarchy: standard < senior < admin.

decision.description: The reviewer's decision, once one is recorded. Absent while the approval is open, and when it ended without one (it expired, a timeout escalated it, or its run's end withdrew it).

requestedBy.description: Who asked for it, when recorded: `user:<id>`, `service_account:<id>` or `system:<what>`.

separateApprover.description: Whether the person who asked may not approve it (four eyes). A runtime that knows it always sends it, `false` included.

withdrawnBecause.description: Why it was withdrawn, when its run's end withdrew it (a reviewer's withdrawal has its `decision` instead).

escalatedFrom.description: The approval this one was escalated from.

escalatedTo.description: The approval this one was escalated to.

decidedBy.description: Who decided, as an actor: `user:<userId>`, the reviewer's user. The run's journal and provenance name the decider the same way. The Kindgi runtime always records it; a deployment whose HITL binding doesn't leaves it out.

reviewerRoleAtDecision.description: Reviewer role class. Hierarchy: standard < senior < admin.

sessionProvider.description: The provider of the session the reviewer decided with: `site:<id>` for a site's sign-in, an identity provider's id for a single sign-on session. Absent for an API key, and on decisions an older runtime recorded.

deciderName.description: The reviewer's display name when they decided: a person renamed since still shows as they were. Absent on decisions an older runtime recorded.

reviewerRoleAtDecision.description: Reviewer role class. Hierarchy: standard < senior < admin.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, in the same order; treat as opaque on the client.

order.description: The order the page is in: `asc` (oldest first) or `desc` (newest first). Absent from a runtime before Kindgi 0.1.6, which lists newest first and ignores `order`.

decidedBy.description: `me` on every page of a list asked for with `?decidedBy=me`, an empty one too: it holds only the approvals the caller decided. Absent from a runtime before Kindgi 0.1.9, which ignores `decidedBy` and lists them all.

value.description: Payload passed to the run waitpoint (`RunBinding.completeToken`) when the approval is linked to a suspended run and the decision is `approve` or `reject`. Refused (400 `bad-input`) for an agent's tool-call or session gate (`tool-call:pending`, `agent-turn:session-hitl-gate`): those resume on the decision alone.

CompleteApprovalResult.description: A recorded decision, and what it did to the run waiting on the approval. `runStatus` is the run's status when the decision couldn't resolve its waitpoint because the run had already ended (e.g. `cancelled` after the decision was recorded); the decision stands.

waitpointResolved.description: True when the approval had a `waitTokenId` and this call resolved the run's waitpoint: approve and reject complete it; withdraw cancels it, so the run ends (`failed`, `hitl-withdrawn`).

resume.description: How the run went on, when this call resumed it (the runtime resumes inline): `ok`, or `failed` with the run's error, e.g. `tool-version-unresolvable` when a tool version the turn started with is gone, or `rate-limit-exceeded` when a budget kept per tenant refused work the turn needed. The decision stands either way.

Reviewer.description: Reviewer roster row. Deactivation is soft (audit trail survives offboarding). `deactivatedAt` present → reviewer no longer receives approvals.

role.description: Reviewer role class. Hierarchy: standard < senior < admin.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent when `hasMore: false`.

RegisterReviewerBody.description: Register a reviewer for the caller's tenant. Idempotent w.r.t. `(tenantId, userId)` — re-registering rotates role/displayName rather than inserting a duplicate.

role.description: Reviewer role class. Hierarchy: standard < senior < admin.

ExportSigningKey.description: A public key this deployment signs exports with.

keyId.description: Derived from the public key (`ex_` and 16 base64url characters), so the same key keeps its id.

algorithm.description: An Ed25519 key signs `ed25519`; an EC P-256 key (a KMS without Ed25519) signs `ecdsa-p256-sha256`.

fingerprint.description: `sha256:` and the hex SHA-256 of the raw public key: to pin it, or compare by eye.

active.description: Whether new exports are signed with it.

data.description: Active first. Empty when the deployment doesn't sign exports.

mode.description: `development`: no key needed (`KINDGI_DEV`); the key's fields are absent, and `preview` may be present.

name.description: Whose key: the name the banner prints.

startsUntil.description: Until when the runtime starts with this key: `expiresAt` plus the 14-day grace.

daysLeft.description: Whole days until it expires; negative once it has.

standing.description: `expiring`: 30 days or fewer left. `grace`: expired, and the runtime still starts with it (for 14 days). `expired`: past the grace too: this server runs on, but won't start with it again.

renewBy.description: Which way to the next key applies: `command`, a key this deployment renews itself (`kindgi license renew`); `contact`, a key Kindgi issued (write to Kindgi).

renew.description: How to get the next key, as the banner says it, with where the deployment keeps its key and renewer. Present from 30 days before the key expires, and only to the deployment's own token.

UsageGroup.description: One group: the dimensions it's grouped by (only those), then its count, the sum of its quantities, and its first and last times.

tenantId.description: The tenant, on the operator's read across tenants.

projectId.description: Absent for a record with no project; a tenant admin's read includes those, and the CLI shows them as `(none)`.

agentId.description: Absent for a record with no agent; the CLI shows those as `(none)`.

kind.description: What was counted: `run.started`, `run.ended`, `approval.requested`, `approval.decided`, `llm.inference`, `llm.embedding`, `project.production`. A runtime may count more kinds later: show one you don't know as it is.

class.description: The class of the run a record counts or belongs to, fixed when the run was created: `production`, `staging`, `dry-run`, `replay`, `eval`, `child`. A record with no counted run has none. A runtime may add classes later: show one you don't know as it is.

state.description: The record's state, by kind: `on`, `off` (`project.production`); `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled` (`run.ended`); `escalation` (`approval.requested`, an escalation's next tier); `approved`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`, `escalated`, `expired` (`approval.decided`). Other kinds have none.

quantity.description: The sum of their quantities: milliseconds for `run.ended`, tokens for model calls, and 1 for every other record, so a group of those has a quantity equal to its count.

watermark.description: Every record at or before this time is in the answer; a later one may not be yet. Re-read a window until its watermark is past the window's end. Every page of one read carries the same watermark.

nextCursor.description: More groups: pass it as `cursor`. Absent on the last page.

runs.description: Runs started in the period: not dry runs, replays, evals or child runs.

people.description: Distinct people who started runs or decided approvals in the period, counted in each tenant and summed.

projectsInProduction.description: Projects in production at `until`; absent when the runtime has no such setting.

ExportAuditBundleBody.description: Body for `POST /v1/approvals/{approvalId}/audit-bundle`, optional: no body signs with the active key. `includeMessages` adds the conversation messages of the approval's run.

signingKeyId.description: Optional: sign with this key, one of `GET /v1/export-signing-keys`. Leave it out to sign with the deployment's active key. A key the deployment doesn't sign with is `404 signing-key-not-found`.

includeMessages.description: When true, hydrates conversation messages tied to the approval's run (agent turns pin `runId === conversationId`). Empty array for non-agent runs — field always present when requested.

ExportAuditBundleResult.description: A decided approval's signed audit bundle. Body: `{ bundleSchemaVersion, approvalId, tenantId, subjectKind, subjectRef, requiredRole, status, createdAt, decidedAt?, decision, evidence: { guardrailResults?, messages? }, exportedAt }`.

kind.description: Which export this is: `audit-bundle`, `provenance` or `compliance`. Absent from older servers.

bundle.description: Base64 of the exact bytes that were signed: the body, as sorted-key JSON with no whitespace. Verify these bytes; nothing needs re-serializing.

bundleSchemaVersion.description: The body's version, semver. `2.0.0`: a string like the other exports' (it was the integer `1`), named `bundleSchemaVersion` in the body too, with `exportedAt` signed once.

algorithm.description: The signing key's algorithm. `ecdsa-p256-sha256` signatures are IEEE P1363 `r‖s`. A verifier refuses an algorithm it doesn't know.

signingKeyId.description: The key that signed it: one of `GET /v1/export-signing-keys`.

signature.description: Base64 of the 64-byte signature over the `bundle` bytes: Ed25519's, or ECDSA P-256's as IEEE P1363 `r‖s`.

publicKey.description: The signing key's public half, PEM SPKI. On its own it only proves the bytes weren't changed; check it against `GET /v1/export-signing-keys` (or a key you pinned) to know who signed them.

exportedAt.description: When it was signed: the same instant as the signed body's `exportedAt`.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; treat as opaque on the client.

JudgeClassScope.description: Where a judge class applies: the whole tenant, one project, or one agent in a project.

name.description: The deployment's own word for the class: "expert", "user", "arbitrator".

weight.description: How much a judgment of this class counts, relative to the others.

unregisteredAt.description: Set when the class was retired.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor. Treat as opaque on the client.

assertableBy.description: Who may assert the class; `null` lifts the restriction.

JudgedSubject.description: What a judged run ran: an agent at a version, or a flow at a version.

JudgedItem.description: The judged item of a run's output.

key.description: The caller's stable id for the item. `kindgi:correction` is reserved: a judgment on it is accepted only when it carries a correction at pointer `""`.

pointer.description: Where the item is in the run's output, as a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901), e.g. `/matches/2`. `""` is the whole output.

rank.description: The item's position in a ranked list (0 = first).

args.description: The partial set of top-level argument fields to compare, by value. Fields left out are not compared; an empty object asks only that the tool was called. At most 4000 characters in canonical JSON.

Correction.description: An expert's correction of a run's decisions: the tool calls the agent should have made, and the tools it should not have called at all. Graded deterministically on a replay. A tool can't be in both `calls` and `notCalled`, and one of them must be non-empty (both empty is a 400).

calls.description: The calls the agent should have made.

notCalled.description: Tools that should not have been called at all.

JudgmentAssertedBy.description: Who asserted a judgment: the authenticated caller, never a typed name.

id.description: A user id, or for a service token its token or session id.

correction.description: The expert's correction of the run's decisions, when they gave one.

judgeClassId.description: The judge class the judgment is recorded under. Absent when unclassified (counts with weight 1).

restricted.description: Present (true) when the judge class was restricted (`assertableBy`) when the judgment was recorded, so the judge was checked against it. A restriction added or lifted later doesn't change it.

participantId.description: The app's opaque id for its end user who judged, when an app judged on their behalf.

unregisteredAt.description: Set when the judgment was removed or superseded.

supersededBy.description: The judgment that replaced this one.

JudgedRunContext.description: What a judged run needs besides its input to be replayed, captured when it was first judged. For an agent turn: the conversation before it, what its retrievals returned, and the decision at its session approval gate. For a flow run: its tool calls with their results. For both: the env values its tools were sent.

history.description: The conversation's messages before the turn, oldest first (at most the last 200).

historyTruncated.description: Whether older messages were left out of `history`.

recalled.description: Messages of earlier conversations the turn recalled (intents over conversations), as quoted to the model.

sessionApproval.description: The reviewer's decision at the turn's session approval gate, when the turn waited on one. A replay of the turn follows it.

rationale.description: The reviewer's reason for a rejection.

flow.description: For a flow run: what it did, kept at its first judgment so it can be replayed. Every tool call it made with its result (at its tool nodes, in its agent steps' turns and in its sub-flows), at most 500, and its agent steps.

runId.description: The run that made it: the flow run, a sub-flow's, or an agent step's turn.

nodeId.description: The tool node that made it, or the agent step whose turn did.

scope.description: The loop iteration, in a loop body.

fromEvent.description: An agent step's turn kept the result as outside data: another system's answer to a paused call, or a result its tool says is outside data. A replay hands it to the model as data, as the turn did. Absent for a tool node's call, and for a run judged before the mark was kept.

recalled.description: Messages of earlier conversations the step's turn recalled.

truncated.description: More calls were made than were kept.

toolEnv.description: The env values each tool's calls were sent (`needsSpec.env`), by tool id: its first call's, as the run recorded them. A replay sends them to a read-only tool it runs live, so the tool reads the config the run saw, not today's. Absent for a run from before env was recorded.

replayOf.description: When the judged run is a comparison's replay: the run it re-ran, stamped at its first judgment. A test set built from judgments leaves replays out.

JudgedRunCopy.description: The stored copy of a judged run's input and output, taken when it was first judged.

segments.description: The segment path the run was started with (empty: none). Absent for runs judged before it was recorded.

JudgmentWithCopies.description: A judgment with the stored copies of what was judged.

itemValue.description: The judged item's value, when the judgment pointed at it.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor. Treat as opaque on the client.

judgeClassId.description: Optional. When given it must exist and apply to the run.

participantId.description: An app's opaque id for its end user, when judging on their behalf.

correction.description: Optional. The tool calls the agent should have made, graded on a replay. A correction judges the run's whole output, so it is recorded under one reserved item (`item.key` `"kindgi:correction"`, `item.pointer` `""`): a correction on any other item is a 400, and a second correction of the run by the same expert replaces the first, so it counts once.

JudgedItemSummary.description: The judgments of one item of a case's output, summed up.

yesWeight.description: The weight behind "yes" (an unclassified judgment counts 1).

totalWeight.description: The weight behind all judgments of the item.

restricted.description: The same weights, counting only judgments recorded while their class was restricted (`Judgment.restricted`), for a comparison weighted `restricted-only`. Absent from a test set built before restrictions.

judgmentIds.description: The judgments behind these two. Absent from a test set built before judgment ids.
The judgments summed into the item, by id: what a comparison on this case counts. Absent from a test set built before judgment ids.

judgeClassId.description: The judgment's class, when it had one.

restricted.description: Set when the judgment was recorded while its class was restricted (`Judgment.restricted`).

JudgeClassAssertableBy.description: Who may assert the class: every part that is set must hold. A class with one is restricted: a judgment recorded while it is carries `restricted`, and a comparison weighted `restricted-only` counts only those.

minReviewerRole.description: The caller's reviewer role is at least this (its token's, or the roster's).

principalIds.description: Only these principals: user ids, or service token ids.

JudgeClassAssertableByView.description: Who may assert the class, as the caller sees it: every part that is set must hold. `principalIds` is sent only to an admin on the class's scope; `principalCount` to everyone who reads it.

minReviewerRole.description: The caller's reviewer role is at least this (its token's, or the roster's).

principalIds.description: Only these principals: user ids, or service token ids. Sent only to an admin on the class's scope.

principalCount.description: How many principals the class is restricted to (`principalIds`), for every reader. Absent when it names none.

JudgedEvalCase.description: One case of a `judged` eval suite: a copy of a judged run with its items' judgments summed up.

corrections.description: Experts' corrections carried onto this case from its judgments, each graded on the replay. Empty or absent when none. `restricted-only` keeps only the entries whose judgment was restricted.

judgmentId.description: The judgment the correction was recorded on.

judgeClassId.description: The judgment's class, when it had one.

restricted.description: Set when the judgment was recorded while its class was restricted (`Judgment.restricted`).

calls.description: The calls the agent should have made.

notCalled.description: Tools that should not have been called at all.

erased.description: An erasure cleared this case (a person's words were erased): `input` and `output` are null, `items` empty, `corrections` empty, and eval runs leave it out (counted as `erased`).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor. Treat as opaque on the client.

BuildJudgedSuiteBody.description: Name the agent (`agentId`) or the flow (`flowId`) whose judged runs to use.

version.description: Semver version to publish, e.g. `1.0.0`.

since.description: Runs first judged at or after this time.

until.description: Runs first judged before this time.

judgeClassIds.description: Count only judgments recorded under these judge classes.

minJudgments.description: Leave out runs with fewer counted judgments. Default 1.

segments.description: Only runs started in this segment path or below it, coarse to fine (e.g. `company=acme`). A run judged before its segments were recorded with its judgments is in no segment, so it's left out.

truncated.description: Whether more judged runs matched than the 1000 cases a set holds.

default.description: Default value used when the caller omits this parameter.

source.description: What it reads: facts (the default), or messages of this agent's earlier conversations, quoted in the turn's `<memory>` block as earlier conversation, never as turns.

types.description: The fact types it retrieves: required for facts; not used for conversations.

roles.description: For conversations: whose messages it recalls. Default `['user']`, the people's own words. Adding `agent` recalls the agent's earlier answers too, which can carry its mistakes: they are quoted as unverified earlier answers, and publishing warns `recall-agent-answers`.

scope.description: What the intent selects within what the run may see. Facts: this conversation's; the run's end user's only (`same-user`: none when the run names no `participantId`); the run's project's (none without a project); or every fact of the type it may see (`tenant`). Conversations: this end user's other conversations with the agent (`same-user`: none when the run names no `participantId`); this conversation's messages older than the history window (`same-conversation`); conversations in the run's segment path (`same-segment`) or its project (`same-project`), whoever had them: those two quote other people's conversations, so publishing warns and their messages are marked as another person's. `same-segment` is for conversations only, `tenant` for facts only.

mode.description: With the user's message as the query: full-text, by meaning (fails the turn with `semantic-unavailable` on a runtime without embeddings), or both fused by rank (without embeddings, the keyword half). Absent: the newest facts.

AgentMemoryPolicy.description: How the agent uses what it retrieves.

instructionTypes.description: Fact types that are instructions for this agent: a retrieved, verified fact of one of these types goes into the system message under 'Policies (verified)'. Default: none.

remember.description: Lets the agent remember: its turns offer the built-in tool `kindgi_remember` (built-in tools are `kindgi_<verb>`; an agent cannot list one in `tools`, and a published tool cannot use the prefix). The model picks the type, the text (up to 2,000 characters), an optional slot `key` and when it stops being true; the scope comes from here and the run. Every remembered fact is `unverified`, attributed to the agent version and the call that wrote it, and expires after `keepDays` unless a person verifies it. A person approves it before any read sees it when the scope is wider than one person (`same-project`, `tenant`) or the text reads like an instruction.

types.description: The fact types it may write.

scope.description: Where its facts go: the conversation's end user (else the user the run acts for), the conversation, the run's project, or the tenant. Each but `tenant` includes the run's project.

keepDays.description: Days an unverified fact is kept. Default 30.

Capability.description: Capability declaration — see `@kindgi/capabilities`. Additional properties are permitted so new capability kinds do not require a wire change.

ToolRef.description: Typed tool reference. `version` is a semver **range** (npm-style: `1.2.3` exact pin, `^1.2.3` compatible-updates, `~1.2.3` patch-updates-only, `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0` explicit range). Dispatch resolves the range to a concrete active version via `semver.maxSatisfying` at run start. No implicit "latest" — every tool ref names both id and range.

schema.description: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) the final answer must match.

name.description: A name for the output, shown to the model and in errors. Default `output`.

maxRepairs.description: How many times the model is asked to repair an invalid answer. Default 1.

maxRetries.description: Failed calls sent back to the model per turn. Default 1.

retryOn.description: Which failures are sent back: arguments that don't fit the input schema (`invalid-arguments`), a tool the agent doesn't have (`unknown-tool`), a tool that ran and failed (`tool-error`). Default `invalid-arguments`, `unknown-tool`.

version.description: Semver.

projectId.description: The agent's project: every version of an agent is in the one project. Absent when the runtime doesn't record it: a pack `kindgi dev` serves from disk, or a runtime before Kindgi 0.1.6.

instructions.description: The system prompt (a Liquid template), or a prompt block by range whose template and parameters are used instead (pinned at publish, `pins.prompts`).

settings.description: Settings blocks the agent reads, by range: tools read them as `ToolContext.settings['<id>']`, templates as `settings["<id>"]`. Pinned at publish (`pins.settings`).

modelSettings.description: A model-settings block by range: its `temperature` and `maxOutputTokens` go into the turn's model calls. Pinned at publish.

preferredProvider.description: Soft hint — the router prefers this provider by id (e.g. `anthropic`) when at least one of its models satisfies `capabilities.needs` + tenant policy. Combine with `preferredModel` to pin the exact (provider, model) tuple. Falls back to capability-based ranking when the pinned provider is unregistered or filtered out.

preferredModel.description: Soft hint at the model level (`ModelInfo.name`, e.g. `claude-sonnet-5-5`). Combined with `preferredProvider`: both set → promote the exact tuple; only `preferredModel` → promote any provider exposing that model; only `preferredProvider` → promote every model of that provider.

unregisteredAt.description: Present only on an unregistered version (`GET …/versions/{version}` reads those too). Unregister stops a version being chosen, not the pins that hold it: a new run naming it is refused, while a resumed run and a published version that pins it still run it.

pinsDigest.description: Set by the runtime with `pins`: `sha256:<hex>` of the pins' canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace). Two agent versions with the same digest run the same blocks.

AgentPins.description: The exact block versions an agent version runs: its lockfile. Set by the runtime when the version is published, never in the publish body: each tool range resolves once to the version every run of that agent version uses, so a new tool version reaches the agent only through a new agent version. Absent on a version published before pins existed (its ranges resolve per run).

PromptRef.description: A prompt block an agent's instructions come from, by id and semver range.

BlockRef.description: A settings block an agent reads, by id and semver range.

PinChange.description: One pin that differs between two versions of an agent or a flow.

from.description: The earlier version's pin; absent when it had none.

to.description: The later version's pin; absent when it has none.

VersionDerivation.description: Set by the runtime on an agent or flow version a deploy registered in place of the definition's version, which was registered already with other pins or content (versions never change). Never in the publish body.

version.description: The version the definition names.

reason.description: `pins-changed`: a block it uses has a new version; `unpinned`: the definition's version was published before pins existed; `version-taken`: the definition's version holds another definition; `edited`: derived from `version` with some data-block pins swapped (`POST /v1/agents/{agentId}/versions`).

label.description: For `edited`: a short label for the version.

proposalId.description: For `edited`: the improvement proposal it was derived for. Such a version serves no scope until a promotion makes it live.

DeriveAgentVersionBody.description: Derive a new agent version from a pinned one with some data-block pins swapped: an expert's edit reaching an agent with no code change.

from.description: The version to derive from (it must be pinned).

label.description: A short label for the new version.

projectId.description: The agent's project, when the runtime doesn't record it on the version.

AgentPinSwaps.description: The data-block pins to swap, by block id → exact version. Only blocks the version already references; tool pins come from code.

FlowPins.description: The exact tool and agent versions a flow version runs: its lockfile. Set by the runtime when the version is published, never in the publish body: each tool the flow runs, and each agent it runs at no named version, resolves once to its latest version then, which every run of that flow version uses. Absent on a version published before pins existed (it binds the latest versions per run).

agents.description: Agent id → exact version, for agent nodes that name no version.

FlowVersionOverrides.description: Agents and tools a flow runs at other exact versions than the flow version's pins ("this flow, with `acme.scorer` at 0.4.0"), without publishing a new flow version: a comparison's flow candidate (`versions` on the start body and the run's `comparison`), and the flow runs that replay it (a run's `versions`). Each id must be an agent or tool the flow uses.

agents.description: Agent id → exact version, for agent nodes with or without a version of their own.

PublishAgentBody.description: Full `defineAgent` spec. Validated server-side via `@kindgi/agents.defineAgent` — validation failures return `400 validation-failed` with the issue list under `details.issues`.

projectId.description: Project this belongs to (its content scope). Required: missing, or not a project in the caller's tenant → `400 bad-input`.

instructions.description: The system prompt (a Liquid template), or a prompt block by range whose template and parameters are used instead (pinned at publish, `pins.prompts`).

settings.description: Settings blocks the agent reads, by range: tools read them as `ToolContext.settings['<id>']`, templates as `settings["<id>"]`. Pinned at publish (`pins.settings`).

modelSettings.description: A model-settings block by range: its `temperature` and `maxOutputTokens` go into the turn's model calls. Pinned at publish.

preferredProvider.description: Soft hint — the router prefers this provider by id (e.g. `anthropic`) when at least one of its models satisfies `capabilities.needs` + tenant policy. Combine with `preferredModel` to pin the exact (provider, model) tuple.

preferredModel.description: Soft hint at the model level (`ModelInfo.name`). Combined with `preferredProvider` to pin an exact tuple; alone to select a model across every provider that exposes it.

warnings.description: What the agent should know about this deployment before its first turn, e.g. `semantic-unavailable` (a retrieval intent searches by meaning and the deployment has no embeddings), `remember-unavailable` (the agent remembers and the deployment cannot store agent memories), `recall-other-people` (an intent recalls conversations in the run's segment or project, whoever had them) or `recall-unavailable` (the deployment cannot recall earlier conversations).

wasTombstoned.description: `true` when this call un-tombstoned the version; `false` when it was already active (idempotent no-op).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent when `hasMore: false`.

when.description: Optional predicate expression evaluated at edge dispatch time (see `@kindgi/flow`).

version.description: Semver.

projectId.description: The flow's project: every version of a flow is in the one project. Absent when the runtime doesn't record it: a pack `kindgi dev` serves from disk, or a runtime before Kindgi 0.1.6.

pinsDigest.description: Set by the runtime with `pins`: `sha256:<hex>` of the pins' canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace).

unregisteredAt.description: Present only on an unregistered version (`GET …/versions/{version}` reads those too). Unregister stops a version being chosen, not the pins that hold it: a new run naming it is refused, while a resumed run and a published version that pins it still run it.

PublishFlowBody.description: Full flow definition. Validated server-side via `@kindgi/flow.loadFlow` — validation failures return `400 validation-failed` with the issue list under `details.issues`.

projectId.description: Project this belongs to (its content scope). Required: missing, or not a project in the caller's tenant → `400 bad-input`.

wasTombstoned.description: `true` when this call un-tombstoned the version; `false` when it was already active (idempotent no-op).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent when `hasMore: false`.

oneOf.description: A connection the tool declares in `needsSpec.connections`, by its name there: sent as `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`.

permissions.description: The entry's permission keys the call needs: `gmail.send`.

as.description: Whose connection: `person`, the run's person (the one it acts for, who started it or owns its trigger); `company`, the tenant's.

HttpToolSpec.description: Declarative HTTP-invocation spec. Attached to `ToolManifest.spec` under the discriminant `kind: 'http'`. The runtime `Tool.handler` is synthesized by the 'http' spec synthesizer to perform URL-template substitution, secret-ref resolution via `ToolContext.resolveSecret`, and the outbound fetch. All fields serialize cleanly to JSON.

urlTemplate.description: URL template with `{param}` placeholders substituted from the tool's input at invoke time.

parseJson.description: When true (default), the response body is parsed as JSON before returning to the invoker.

SandboxMode.description: Isolation posture the runtime enforces around the handler. Optional additive field.

RuntimeLimits.description: Sandbox-enforced resource caps at dispatch. Optional additive field.

NetworkPolicy.description: Network egress policy. Optional additive field. Discriminated on `kind`.

TypedNeeds.description: Typed discriminated needs (env / secrets / config / capabilities / bindings / connections). Optional additive field.

connections.description: Accounts at other apps the tool acts with, by the tool's own name for each (`mail`). The runtime resolves them per call into the context's `connections`.

CodeArtifactRef.description: Handler-artifact pointer. Discriminated on `kind`: `oci` is the deploy-pipeline shape (image + module path + artifactVersion); `filesystem` is the local-development shape — absolute host path at the pack's on-disk handler file. Production servers SHOULD reject `filesystem`.

ToolSpec.description: Declarative handler spec. Discriminated on `kind`; the framework's synthesizer registry maps kind → runtime handler. Mutually exclusive with an imperative handler at author time.

projectId.description: The tool's project: every version of a tool is in the one project. Absent when the runtime doesn't record it: a pack `kindgi dev` serves from disk, or a runtime before Kindgi 0.1.6.

input.description: JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) for the tool input.

output.description: JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) for the tool output.

mutating.description: Semantic marker: `true` when this tool causes observable side effects (writes state, calls external APIs with mutations, sends messages). Read-only tools set `false`. Absent defaults to `true`. Consumed by the HITL default classifier — a read-only tool passes straight through, a mutating tool asks on first use.

needsApprovalWhenUnattended.description: `true`: in a run no person started (one whose `startedBy` isn't `person`), every call of this tool waits for a person's yes, whatever the agent's approval rules say, and a flow's tool step that calls it is refused. A webhook trigger, a schedule or a mail trigger whose `toolsAllowedUnattended` names the tool (a project admin's to set) lifts that, in its own runs only. A tool that uses a person's connection, reads included, counts as declaring it. In a run a mail started, so does a tool that isn't `mutating: false`, and one that uses the run's own mailbox. Absent means `false`.

pauses.description: `true` when the tool may make its run wait for another system's answer: each call gets a wait token, hands its link to that system, and answers `pause`; the system's answer, valid against `output`, becomes the call's result. The run waits at most 24 days (24 hours by default) and fails the call when the time passes. Only a pack tool with a handler can pause: not one with a declarative `spec`, nor an MCP tool. Absent means `false`.

resultIsOutsideData.description: `true` when the tool's results are text from outside that nobody checked, such as a mail someone sent: an agent reads each result as data, not instructions, in that turn and in every later turn's history. Absent means `false`.

unregisteredAt.description: Present only on an unregistered version: a retired tool (every version unregistered) as `GET /v1/tools?includeRetired=true` lists it.

secretScopes.description: Where each secret it names is read, by name: recorded by the server when it was registered, never sent by a caller. `null`: none usable (the registrant administers no scope the secret could be read at), until an admin records it again: a tool by publishing a new version, an MCP endpoint by unregistering it and registering it again. Absent on items registered before it was recorded, or on a runtime without a secrets store.

RegisterToolBody.description: ToolManifest — Tool minus its runtime `handler`. Validated server-side via `@kindgi/tools.validateToolManifest`. Metadata-only registration: the handler is not uploaded and must already be available to the runtime.

projectId.description: Project this belongs to (its content scope). Required: missing, or not a project in the caller's tenant → `400 bad-input`.

input.description: JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) for the tool input.

output.description: JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) for the tool output.

mutating.description: Semantic marker: `true` when this tool causes observable side effects (writes state, calls external APIs with mutations, sends messages). Read-only tools set `false`. Absent defaults to `true`. Consumed by the HITL default classifier — a read-only tool passes straight through, a mutating tool asks on first use.

needsApprovalWhenUnattended.description: `true`: in a run no person started (one whose `startedBy` isn't `person`), every call of this tool waits for a person's yes, whatever the agent's approval rules say, and a flow's tool step that calls it is refused. A webhook trigger, a schedule or a mail trigger whose `toolsAllowedUnattended` names the tool (a project admin's to set) lifts that, in its own runs only. A tool that uses a person's connection, reads included, counts as declaring it. In a run a mail started, so does a tool that isn't `mutating: false`, and one that uses the run's own mailbox. Absent means `false`.

The run waits at most 24 days (24 hours by default) and fails the call when the time passes. Only a pack tool with a handler can pause: not one with a declarative `spec`, nor an MCP tool. Absent means `false`.

wasTombstoned.description: `true` when this call un-tombstoned the version; `false` when it was already active (idempotent no-op).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent when `hasMore: false`.

projectId.description: The tool's project: every version of a tool is in the one project. Absent when the runtime doesn't record it: a pack `kindgi dev` serves from disk, or a runtime before Kindgi 0.1.6.

output.description: JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) for the tool output.

Absent defaults to `true`. Consumed by the HITL default classifier — a read-only tool passes straight through, a mutating tool asks on first use.

Absent means `false`.

The run waits at most 24 days (24 hours by default) and fails the call when the time passes. Only a pack tool with a handler can pause: not one with a declarative `spec`, nor an MCP tool. Absent means `false`.
