unregisteredAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp — present iff this version has been soft-tombstoned via `POST /versions/:v/unregister`. Absent on active versions.

secretScopes.description: Where each secret it names is read, by name: recorded by the server when it was registered, never sent by a caller. `null`: none usable (the registrant administers no scope the secret could be read at), until an admin records it again: a tool by publishing a new version, an MCP endpoint by unregistering it and registering it again. Absent on items registered before it was recorded, or on a runtime without a secrets store.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent when `hasMore: false`.

on-violation.description: What a failed check does to the agent turn. Open string: the built-in actions are listed in `examples`, and any other non-empty name is accepted. In 0.1 the runtime acts only on `halt`: the turn fails with `guardrail-violation` and its response is not stored. Any other value is recorded as a violation, as `log-only` is, and the turn completes: nothing runs the turn again, escalates or calls a compensating tool.

retry.description: The attempts a `retry` asks for. In 0.1 nothing acts on it: there's no second attempt.

escalateTo.description: Where an `escalate` goes. In 0.1 nothing escalates.

compensateWith.description: The tool id a `compensate` names. In 0.1 that tool isn't called.

projectId.description: The guardrail's project. Absent when the runtime doesn't record it: a pack `kindgi dev` serves from disk, or a runtime before Kindgi 0.1.6.

kind.description: How the guardrail is checked. Open string: the built-in kinds are listed in `examples`; adapters register strategies for their own kinds.

check.description: Reference to the concrete check implementation registered server-side.

RegisterGuardrailBody.description: Guardrail spec. Validated server-side via `@kindgi/guardrails.validateGuardrailSpec`. Metadata-only registration: the `check` id must reference an implementation already available to the runtime.

projectId.description: Project this belongs to (its content scope). Required: missing, or not a project in the caller's tenant → `400 bad-input`.

kind.description: How the guardrail is checked. Open string: the built-in kinds are listed in `examples`; adapters register strategies for their own kinds.

check.description: Reference to the concrete check implementation registered server-side.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent when `hasMore: false`.

GuardrailOutcomeCounts.description: How many of a guardrail's checks came to each outcome.

passed.description: The check ran and found nothing.

violated.description: The check found something and the answer went through (`log-only`, `noop`, or an action handed back).

blocked.description: The check found something and its `halt` failed the turn.

errored.description: The check couldn't run (no such check, a bad configuration, a judge that couldn't be routed).

GuardrailOutcomesByAgentVersion.description: The counts on one agent version's turns.

passed.description: The check ran and found nothing.

violated.description: The check found something and the answer went through (`log-only`, `noop`, or an action handed back).

blocked.description: The check found something and its `halt` failed the turn.

errored.description: The check couldn't run (no such check, a bad configuration, a judge that couldn't be routed).

GuardrailBlockedRun.description: A turn the guardrail blocked: its run, never its answer.

byAgentVersion.description: The same counts per agent version, the most checked first, at most 100.

recentBlocked.description: The window's latest blocked turns, newest first, at most `recent`.

recordedSince.description: The earliest outcome kept for this guardrail in this project, in any window: nothing before it is counted. Outcomes were first recorded in 0.1.6, and they go with their run's retention. Absent when none is kept.

ConversationStatus.description: Lifecycle status derived from `closedAt`: `open` when null, `closed` otherwise.

projectId.description: The project the conversation is in: the project of the run that opened it, or `projectId` on open (when omitted, the agent's own project, or the tenant's Default project for an agent filed under none). Absent on conversations from before Kindgi 0.1.3; those are listed only without a scope.

openedBy.description: Who opened it: the caller's principal (`user:<id>`, `service_account:<id>`), or, for one a turn opened, whoever the run acts for. Set by the server, never from a request's body. Absent on conversations an older runtime opened, and when the caller had no principal; those aren't listed by `?openedBy=me`.

scope.description: Free-form scope object (currently `{ tenantId }` in tests; enterprises extend with `matterId`, `engagementId`, etc.).

status.description: Lifecycle status derived from `closedAt`: `open` when null, `closed` otherwise.

unregisteredAt.description: When it was unregistered (`POST /v1/conversations/{conversationId}/unregister`). Only the unregister call returns it: reads no longer do.

sequence.description: Monotonic index within the conversation. Sort order for the list endpoint.

content.description: Free-form string OR a structured object (tool results, multi-modal payloads).

title.description: Optional. Defaults to `"Untitled conversation"` when omitted.

projectId.description: The project the conversation is in; `GET /v1/conversations?scopeKind=project&scopeId=…` lists it. A project of the caller's tenant, else `400 bad-input`, that reaches the agent, else `400 reference-out-of-scope`. Omitted: the agent's own project, as for a run (the tenant's Default project for an agent filed under none).

scope.description: Structural scope (project id, matter id, etc.). Treated opaquely by the runtime.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent when `hasMore: false`.

openedBy.description: `me` on every page of a list asked for with `?openedBy=me`, an empty one too: it holds only the conversations the caller opened. Absent from a runtime before Kindgi 0.1.9, which ignores `openedBy` and lists everyone's.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent when `hasMore: false`. Sort is `sequence asc`.

FactScope.description: Fact scope object. `tenantId` is required; every optional key narrows the fact (`userId`, `orgId`, `projectId`, `threadId`, `sessionId`, `participantId`). A fact is readable by whoever has every container it names. Additional keys accepted for forward compatibility.

participantId.description: An app's end user, by the app's own id: a fact private to that participant's runs. Needs `projectId`.

FactSubject.description: Whom a fact is about: what access and erasure requests by person find.

FactAttribution.description: Who asserted a fact, set by the server from the writer.

FactGeneratedBy.description: The run step that wrote a fact, for one an agent wrote.

id.description: The fact id, kept across revisions (for a fact never superseded, also its one revision id).

revisionId.description: This revision's own id; absent where it equals `id`.

type.description: Fact type identifier (pack-defined; a few are framework-standard).

version.description: The revision number within the fact: 1, then one more per supersede or verify.

contentRef.description: `blob://<provider>/<bucket>/<key>` when the payload is stored externally.

trust.description: `verified`: a person with the right checked it. `asserted`: an app or a person wrote it. `unverified`: an agent remembered it during a conversation. Absent on facts from before trust was recorded: `asserted`.

validFrom.description: When the fact starts being true in the world; absent: always.

validUntil.description: When the fact stops being true in the world; absent: still true.

observedAt.description: When it was said or seen.

invalidatedAt.description: When this revision stopped being current; absent: it is current.

review.description: `pending` while a person must approve it: a pending fact is never retrieved.

expiresAt.description: When this revision stops being readable: from its retention (`keepUntil`, or `keepDays` from the fact's first write), or an agent-remembered fact's unverified window. No read returns it after; absent: it doesn't expire.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent when `hasMore: false`.

WriteFactBody.description: Write a fact. `type` selects the retrieval-policy (which indexes populate); `scope.tenantId` MUST match the caller's tenant. Optional `retention` overrides tenant defaults; optional `contentHash` is a caller-supplied idempotence hint (runtime computes its own hash regardless). `subjects` names whom it is about; `validFrom`/`validUntil` when it is true in the world; `observedAt` when it was said or seen.

SupersedeFactBody.description: The fact's next revision: new `content`, and optionally new `retention`, `subjects` and times (absent ones keep their current values). Its scope and type stay. `expectVersion`: only if the current revision is still this one.

RetrieveIntent.description: Retrieval intent — mirrors `RetrievalIntent` from `@kindgi/agents`, widened for direct-HTTP use. `mode: "list"` returns a plain scoped list (no query), newest first. `mode: "keyword"` runs full-text search. `mode: "semantic"` searches by meaning — it needs embeddings on the deployment; without them the route answers `422 semantic-unavailable`. `mode: "both"` runs both and fuses them by rank (reciprocal rank fusion), as `semantic` needing embeddings.

RetrieveMemoryBody.description: Retrieval intent — mirrors `RetrievalIntent` from `@kindgi/agents`, widened for direct-HTTP use. `mode: "list"` returns a plain scoped list (no query), newest first. `mode: "keyword"` runs full-text search. `mode: "semantic"` searches by meaning — it needs embeddings on the deployment; without them the route answers `422 semantic-unavailable`. `mode: "both"` runs both and fuses them by rank (reciprocal rank fusion), as `semantic` needing embeddings.

score.description: Relevance score. Keyword mode returns an implementation-defined rank (higher = better). Semantic mode returns cosine similarity in [-1, 1] (higher = better). Both: the fused rank score, `Σ 1/(60 + rank)` (higher = better). Absent for `list` mode.

MemoryErasureSubjectSelector.description: A person: an app's end user (`participant`), or an `external` subject facts name. Erasing a Kindgi user isn't offered.

MemoryErasureSelector.description: Whose words to erase: one fact (`factId`), a person (`subject`: an app's end user `participant`, or an `external` subject facts name), or one conversation (`conversationId`).

CreateMemoryErasureBody.description: Whose words to erase: one fact (`factId`), a person (`subject`: an app's end user `participant`, or an `external` subject facts name), or one conversation (`conversationId`).

selector.description: Only while it runs: a completed or failed erasure keeps no identifier.

status.description: `waiting-on-run`: a turn of the person's sits in a flow that serves other people; the erasure waits for it (`waitingOn`) until its deadline, then cancels it.

phase.description: Where a running erasure is: `seed`, `expand`, `settle` (the person's unfinished runs end, or it waits for them, before anything is cleared), `erase`, then `done`.

matchable.description: A replay after a backup restore can find this person again: a keyed hash was kept.

counts.description: What each store cleared or deleted, by store.

lastError.description: The last failure's code, or `not-yet:<reason>` while it waits. Never content.

waitingOn.description: The run it waits (or waited) for, and until when; kept as the record of the wait.

forced.description: A tenant admin said not to wait.

settleRoundsCapped.description: Runs of the person's kept appearing, round after round: the erasure went on to erase after its last round rather than wait any longer. Absent: it didn't.

code.description: `erasure-unmatchable`: this deployment has no erasure ledger key (`KINDGI_ERASURE_LEDGER_KEY`), so a replay after a restore can't find this person.

selectorHmac.description: HMAC-SHA256 of the selector under the tenant's ledger key; absent without one.

status.description: `waiting-on-run`: a turn of the person's sits in a flow that serves other people; the erasure waits for it (`waitingOn`) until its deadline, then cancels it.

force.description: Stop waiting for a run in a flow that serves other people: it's cancelled, and the erasure goes on.

replayed.description: Found in the tenant again: run again.

restored.description: Put back in the ledger; nothing in the tenant matches.

ProposalTier.description: What a proposal changes: a settings block (new values) or a prompt block (a new template) the agent version pins.

FixProposalStatus.description: Where a proposal stands, from its comparison and its promotion (never stored). `draft`: not evaluated yet. `evaluating`: its comparison is queued or running. `evaluated`: the candidate beat the recorded outputs on the objective metric by more than the noise (the spread, with more than one repetition). Under `evaluation.rule: 'cheaper'` it means instead: no worse than the current version on the same cases and costing less, so `evaluated` doesn't always mean better. With `evaluation.decisions` (a model-settings change), it also means no correction the current version passes failed. `not-better`: it didn't. `evaluation-failed`: the comparison failed or was cancelled. `in-review`: requested; the gate passed and an approval is open. `promoted`: live for the scope (`promotion.liveNow` says whether it still serves it). `refused`: the gate refused it. `rejected`: the reviewer rejected it. `expired`: the approval expired undecided. `superseded`: approved after the scope's live version or policy changed. `rolled-back`: rolled back through the proposal. `withdrawn`: withdrawn.

blockId.description: The data block the change is to.

fromVersion.description: The block version the agent version pins: what's being changed.

content.description: The new content: `{ values }` for a settings block (its schema carries over), `{ template }` for a prompt block (its parameters carry over).

ProposalDrafter.description: Who wrote the proposal: a person, or one of the runtime's drafters.

version.description: For a drafter: the drafter's version.

model.description: For a drafter that used a model: which.

passId.description: For a drafter: the improvement pass that drafted it (`GET /v1/improvement-passes/{passId}`).

judgmentIds.description: The judgments that motivated it. An improvement pass's proposal names the judgments it learned from on the cases it searched, never the hold-out: those its comparisons counted and, for a prompt pass, those its drafter was shown. At most 100: first those its drafter was shown, then those behind items judged wrong, then the rest.

judgmentCount.description: How many judgments it rests on, when `judgmentIds` names only the first of them. Absent when `judgmentIds` names them all.

ProposalCandidate.description: The versions evaluating the proposal published. They serve no scope until a promotion makes the agent version live.

agentVersion.description: The derived agent version (its `derivedFrom.proposalId` names the proposal).

blockVersion.description: The block version published from the proposal's content.

ProposalEvaluation.description: The comparison the proposal was evaluated with, and what it found on the objective metric (the full summary is the eval run's).

suiteId.description: The test set (a judged eval suite).

runStatus.description: The eval run's status. Absent when the run can't be read.

baseline.description: The recorded outputs' score; `null` without judged evidence.

spread.description: With more than one repetition: the candidate's max − min, the noise a delta must beat.

rule.description: How the candidate is kept. `better`: it beats the recorded outputs by more than the noise. `cheaper`: it's no worse than the current version replayed on the same cases (beyond that run's spread) and costs less (beyond the cost's own spread), with no errored case; `better` may then be false while the status is `evaluated`. Absent: `better`.

ProposalCost.description: What the replays cost in model calls on the same cases, in US dollars, averaged over the repetitions: the current version's and the candidate's. Set for a change held to the current version once both comparisons finished, when both reported a cost.

ProposalDecisions.description: The corrections the current version was checked on, replayed on the same cases, against the candidate's. A model-settings change is kept only with at least one checked and none broken. Set once both comparisons finished.

held.description: The current version passed them, and so did the candidate.

broken.description: The current version passed them; the candidate didn't.

stillWrong.description: Neither passed them. The rest of `checked` the candidate fixed.

ProposalPromotion.description: The promotion the proposal's request made.

approvalId.description: The approval a request in review waits on.

liveNow.description: For a promoted proposal: whether its version still serves the scope.

FixProposal.description: An improvement proposal: a change to one data block an agent version pins, for one live scope, taken through the same comparison, gate and promotion as any other version.

fromVersion.description: The agent version the change applies to.

hypothesis.description: What the change should improve, and why.

maxCostUsd.description: The most the pass's comparisons may cost, in US dollars.

ImprovementPassOutcome.description: What a finished pass found. `proposed`: its best candidate beat the current values on the test set's hold-out part, so it wrote an improvement proposal (`proposalId`) for a reviewer to decide. `nothing-found`: no candidate beat them by more than the noise, or within the budget (`reason`; `holdOut` has the best candidate's numbers when one got that far). `failed`: `message` says why.

ImprovementPass.description: An improvement pass: the runtime looking for better values for an agent version's tunable settings (`x-kindgi-tunable`) on a test set, within a budget. Its best candidate becomes an improvement proposal.

fromVersion.description: The version whose settings it tunes.

suiteId.description: The test set it searches and proves on.

classWeights.description: Which judgments its comparisons count. Absent from older servers: `restricted-only`.

model.description: For a prompt pass: the provider and model that drafts the templates.

candidates.description: For a prompt pass: how many templates it drafts.

costUsd.description: What its comparisons have cost so far (US dollars).

cancelReason.description: Why a `cancelled` pass stopped when nobody cancelled it: a comparison's eval run was cancelled for it (that run's `cancelReason`, e.g. `project-suspended`). It wrote no proposal. Absent when it was cancelled.

comparisons.description: Its comparisons so far, each an eval run to open: `reference` (the version as it is, on the search part; for a model-settings change also on the hold-out part, what its proof is held to), each `candidate` (the block and the values it changed, on the search part), and the `proof` (the proposal, on the hold-out part). Absent from older servers.

refused.description: For a drafted template that was never compared: why the check refused it (what it reads or names that the agent doesn't have, or its size).

hypothesis.description: For a drafted template: what the drafter meant it to change.

trigger.description: The improve schedule and fire that started it (`GET /v1/schedules/{triggerId}/fires`); absent for a pass a person started.

fromVersion.description: The version whose settings it tunes. Default: the one serving `scope`.

projectId.description: The project the pass works in: `suiteId` must be a test set it reaches, the version must reach it, and the pass's eval runs run there. A `project` or `segment` scope must be in it. Default, as an improve schedule's: the scope's project, else (a `tenant` or `org` scope) the agent version's. A project other than the version's needs `write` there.

suiteId.description: The test set (a judged eval suite). The pass splits it into a search part and a hold-out part, and proves its best candidate on the hold-out part.

tiers.description: `['settings']`: values for the tunable settings keys. `['prompt']`: a model drafts templates for the prompt block (needs `model`); a template that reads or names anything the agent doesn't have is refused, and a drafted proposal always waits for a reviewer.

model.description: For a prompt pass: the tenant's provider and model that drafts the templates.

candidates.description: For a prompt pass: how many templates it drafts.

classWeights.description: Which judgments the pass learns from. Omit it for the default: everyone's (`as-recorded`) until the tenant, the project the pass reads its judgments from (its test set's project, which can differ from where the agent is made), or the agent improved in that project has a restricted judge class, then only judgments recorded under one (`restricted-only`).

ImprovementPassEstimate.description: What a pass this input would start is estimated to cost: the budget cap it's clamped to, and — when the version has cost history — the estimate itself.

estimatedCostUsd.description: The estimate (US dollars): `basis.replays` times `basis.meanRunCostUsd`, or `maxCostUsd` when that's smaller. Absent when the version has no cost history.

maxCostUsd.description: The budget cap the estimate is clamped to (`budget.maxCostUsd`, US dollars).

basis.description: What the estimate is built from.

replays.description: How many replay runs the pass's comparisons would make.

meanRunCostUsd.description: The version's mean cost over its recent completed runs (US dollars). Absent with no cost history.

CreateProposalBody.description: A hand-written proposal: new content for a data block that `fromVersion` pins, for a live scope. The same change from the same version for the same scope is one proposal (answered with `X-Proposal-Deduped: true`).

fromVersion.description: The agent version the change applies to.

blockId.description: A block `fromVersion` pins, of the tier's kind.

content.description: `{ values }` for a settings block (they must satisfy its schema), `{ template }` for a prompt block.

EvaluateProposalBody.description: Compare the proposal's candidate on a test set. The first evaluation publishes the block version and derives the agent version (both serve nowhere until promoted).

suiteId.description: The test set: a judged eval suite.

objective.description: The metric that says whether the candidate is better.

ProvenanceSignature.description: Runtime-side signature attached at emission time (if the deployment signs on write). Independent of the export-time signature returned by the export route.

ProvenanceRecordMetadata.description: Lightweight metadata row returned by list. Excludes the full DAG payload — clients fetch the DAG via `GET /v1/provenance/{runId}`.

version.description: Schema version of the record document (semver).

signed.description: True when the emission-time signature is present. Independent of whether the export route can produce a signed bundle.

projectId.description: The project of the record's run. Absent on records from before Kindgi 0.1.3; those are listed only without a scope.

ProvenanceRecord.description: Full provenance record including the DAG payload.

signature.description: Runtime-side signature attached at emission time (if the deployment signs on write). Independent of the export-time signature returned by the export route.

callUsage.description: Each model call's usage from the cost ledger, by the `callId` in its `model-call` node's attributes. Joined when read: not part of the signed DAG. A signed export includes it, as it stood when signed.

ExportProvenanceBody.description: Optional: no body signs with the active key.

signingKeyId.description: Optional: sign with this key, one of `GET /v1/export-signing-keys`. Leave it out to sign with the deployment's active key. A key the deployment doesn't sign with is `404 signing-key-not-found`.

includeMessages.description: When true, hydrates conversation messages tied to the run (agent turns pin `runId === conversationId`). Non-agent runs return an empty `messages: []` — the field is still present on the bundle for shape stability.

ExportProvenanceResult.description: A run's signed provenance. Body: `{ bundleSchemaVersion, provenanceId, runId, tenantId, version, createdAt, flowRef?, dag: { nodes, edges }, messages?, callUsage?, exportedAt }`; `callUsage` is each model call's usage from the cost ledger, as it stood when signed.

kind.description: Which export this is: `audit-bundle`, `provenance` or `compliance`. Absent from older servers.

bundle.description: Base64 of the exact bytes that were signed: the body, as sorted-key JSON with no whitespace. Verify these bytes; nothing needs re-serializing.

bundleSchemaVersion.description: The body's version, semver. `1.2.0` adds `exportedAt` to the signed body; `1.1.0` added `callUsage`.

algorithm.description: The signing key's algorithm. `ecdsa-p256-sha256` signatures are IEEE P1363 `r‖s`. A verifier refuses an algorithm it doesn't know.

signingKeyId.description: The key that signed it: one of `GET /v1/export-signing-keys`.

signature.description: Base64 of the 64-byte signature over the `bundle` bytes: Ed25519's, or ECDSA P-256's as IEEE P1363 `r‖s`.

publicKey.description: The signing key's public half, PEM SPKI. On its own it only proves the bytes weren't changed; check it against `GET /v1/export-signing-keys` (or a key you pinned) to know who signed them.

exportedAt.description: When it was signed: the same instant as the signed body's `exportedAt`.

contentType.description: MIME type as declared by the uploader. Framework does NOT sniff content-type server-side.

size.description: Byte length of the persisted body.

hash.description: sha256 of the body, hex-encoded, lowercase (64 chars).

tags.description: Free-form caller-supplied labels. Filterable on list via `?tag.<key>=<value>`.

ownerRunId.description: Optional back-ref to the RunId that produced this blob.

projectId.description: The project the artifact belongs to: its owner run's, else the upload's `projectId`, else the tenant's default project. Reading it needs `read` there; deleting it, `write`. Absent on blobs stored before projects were recorded.

bucket.description: The bucket of the blob's S3-compatible address (`/s3/{bucket}/{key}`). Present, with `key`, when the server's storage gives the blob one: an object put through `/s3` has the bucket and key it was put under, and an upload through `POST /v1/artifacts` conventionally has bucket `artifacts` and its `blobId` as the key.

key.description: The key of the blob's S3-compatible address (`/s3/{bucket}/{key}`). Present, with `bucket`, when the server's storage gives the blob one.

contentType.description: MIME type as declared by the uploader. Framework does NOT sniff content-type server-side.

size.description: Byte length of the persisted body.

hash.description: sha256 of the body, hex-encoded, lowercase (64 chars).

ownerRunId.description: Optional back-ref to the RunId that produced this blob.

key.description: The key of the blob's S3-compatible address (`/s3/{bucket}/{key}`). Present, with `bucket`, when the server's storage gives the blob one.

UploadArtifactBody.description: Multipart form. `file` is the byte stream (required). Other fields are optional metadata: `name` (defaults to file part filename), `contentType` (defaults to file part MIME), `tags` (JSON-encoded object), `ownerRunId` (RunId string), `expectedHash` (sha256 hex, framework rejects on mismatch).

tags.description: JSON-encoded `Record<string, string>` — parsed server-side.

projectId.description: The project it belongs to, when there's no `ownerRunId` (with one, the run's project, and this must agree). Default: the tenant's default project.

expectedHash.description: Caller-computed sha256, hex-encoded, lowercase. Framework verifies + rejects on mismatch with `blob-hash-mismatch` (400).

deleted.description: `true` on the first delete; `false` on subsequent calls (already gone). 404 only when the id was never known.

id.description: Stable identifier — e.g. `feature:<feature>`; deployments MAY pick other conventions for extension entries.

oneOf.description: Deployment-declared feature name outside the closed built-in enum.

paramsSchema.description: Optional JSON Schema fragment describing the parameters an agent may attach to `{ feature, params }` in a `Requirement`.

providers.description: The tenant's registered providers with a model that has the feature, and those models. Absent from servers that don't read the provider registry; `[]` when no provider of the tenant has one.

CapabilityProvider.description: A provider of the tenant with a model that has the feature.

ModelThinking.description: How the model thinks before it answers, so a call that wants as little as it allows (a judge's) gets it. Absent: it doesn't think, or nothing is known.

mode.description: `adaptive`: on unless turned down. `always`: on, and it can only be lowered.

lowest.description: The vendor's own setting for the least thinking: for Anthropic `disabled`, `between_tools` or an effort (`low`); for Gemini a thinking level (`low`, `minimal`); for OpenAI a reasoning effort (`low`, `none`).

ProviderCost.description: USD per 1K tokens. An adapter may take more rate fields (see the adapter's README).

name.description: Vendor-facing model id passed to the SDK (e.g. `claude-sonnet-5-5`).

features.description: Features this model supports (tool-use, thinking, structured-output, ...).

p95LatencyMs.description: Best-effort p95 latency estimate in milliseconds. Varies by model.

maxOutputTokens.description: Fallback cap on output tokens. Adapters that require `max_tokens` on every request (e.g. Anthropic) use this when `ModelCallInput.maxOutputTokens` is unset.

sampling.description: Whether the model takes sampling settings (`temperature`). `false`: its API rejects a non-default value, so the call goes without one and the answer's `warnings` say so (`sampling-unsupported`). Absent: it takes them.

description.description: Short per-model description surfaced in logs.

region.description: Region the connection routes to. All models on this provider share the region (the same models served from two clouds or regions are separate providers). `'unspecified'` when not region-scoped.

models.description: Models this connection exposes. Non-empty. `models[i].name` must be unique within the list.

defaultModel.description: The model to use when an agent doesn't choose: one of `models[].name`. When candidates rank equally, it comes before the provider's other models; without it, ties break by model name. A preset sets it. A runtime before 0.1.4 ignores it.

attributes.description: Soft attributes for preference-ranking (`local`, `lower-cost`, `higher-accuracy`, ...). Matched by string equality against `Preference.feature`.

description.description: Short human description of the connection.

capabilityKind.description: Kind of resource this provider fulfils. Absent = `llm-inference`. Adapters for other kinds (embedding, gpu-compute, sandbox-exec, ...) set this explicitly.

fallback.description: A fallback serves a capability only when no other provider satisfies it (e.g. `kindgi dev`'s scripted `dev-echo`); an agent turn routed to one carries a `fallback-provider` warning. Absent = `false`.

labels.description: Bookkeeping, such as who manages the provider; the router ignores labels. At most 32 keys; a key is 1-63 lowercase letters and digits, with `.`, `-`, `_` or `/` inside; a value is at most 256 characters. The convention key `kindgi.com/managed-by` names the manager (`kindgi-dev`, `kindgi-deploy:<environment>`). Out of bounds: `400 invalid-provider`, reason `invalid-labels`.

adapter_id.description: The adapter that instantiates this provider (e.g. `@kindgi/adapter-model-gemini`). Must be registered for the tenant.

secret_ref.description: The tenant secret holding the adapter's credential (an API key, a service-account key). Absent when the adapter needs none or finds its own (a cloud's default credentials).

adapter_config.description: The adapter's connection settings: flat, non-secret values (a cloud project, a base URL). Each adapter documents its keys. Credentials go in `secret_ref`, never here.

send_traceparent.description: Send each model call's W3C `traceparent` to this provider, as a request header, so its request logs can be matched to the run. Ids only, never content. Default `false`: nothing about a run's trace leaves the deployment unless a registration opts in. The runtime enforces it; an older runtime ignores the field and sends none.

path.description: The setting at fault, as a JSON pointer into the registration: `/adapter_config/<key>`, `/secret_ref`, `/metadata/region`, `/metadata/models/<i>/name`, or `/adapter_id` (an adapter this runtime does not have).

message.description: What's wrong with that setting and what it takes (e.g. `adapter_config.api must be one of responses, chat-completions.`). The error's `message` names the provider and its adapter.

checked.description: False when this runtime has no check for the provider's adapter; `issues` is then empty.

secretRef.description: The secret the provider's key resolves from, by name only, never its value. Present when the registration has one. Only a caller allowed to check the provider sees it. `kindgi dev` uses it to keep a provider's key out of the pack service's environment. A runtime before 0.1.6 leaves it out.

MCPTransport.description: MCP transport variant. `stdio` — local subprocess (spawn a command). `http-sse` — the older MCP HTTP+SSE transport (separate POST + SSE endpoints). `streamable-http` — the Streamable HTTP transport (single endpoint, session id via header).

config.description: Transport-tagged config union. Server enforces `config.transport === transport` at registration.

sseUrl.description: Optional distinct SSE endpoint if the server splits them.

headers.description: Headers sent with every request, as given. Not for a credential: a header named `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization` or `Cookie`, or with a `-`/`_`-separated part `token`, `secret`, `password`, `passwd`, `apikey`, `credential`, `credentials`, `signature`, `session`, `auth`, `authorization` or `authentication`, or the parts `api-key`, `access-key`, `private-key`, `auth-key`, `subscription-key`, `functions-key`, `application-key`, `app-key`, `master-key`, `client-key` or `partner-key` (`X-Api-Key`, `X-Auth-Token`), is refused (`invalid-mcp-endpoint`, reason `credential-in-headers`). Send it by reference: `auth` with `scheme: header`, or `secretRef` for a bearer. An endpoint registered with one before keeps working, and its value reads back as `[redacted]`.

auth.description: How the endpoint signs in when it isn't a plain bearer: `basic`, `oauth2-client-credentials` or `header`. Not with `secretRef` (`invalid-mcp-endpoint`, reason `auth-with-secret-ref`), not on a `stdio` endpoint (reason `auth-on-stdio`), and not with a header in `config.headers` that `auth` sends: `Authorization` for `basic` and `oauth2-client-credentials` (reason `auth-with-authorization-header`), a name in `auth.headers` for `header` (reason `auth-header-in-config`). An older runtime refuses the field as unknown, or the `header` scheme as `invalid-auth`.

instructions.description: Optional pass-through to the MCP client `serverInfo.instructions`.

sendTraceparent.description: Send the W3C `traceparent` of the run calling a tool to this endpoint, as a request header, so the server's logs can be matched to the run. Ids only, never content. Default `false`. HTTP transports only: `true` on a `stdio` endpoint is refused (`invalid-mcp-endpoint`, reason `invalid-send-traceparent`). An older runtime ignores it and sends none.

secretScopes.description: Where each secret it names is read, by name: recorded by the server when it was registered, never sent by a caller. `null`: none usable (the registrant administers no scope the secret could be read at), until an admin records it again: a tool by publishing a new version, an MCP endpoint by unregistering it and registering it again. Absent on items registered before it was recorded, or on a runtime without a secrets store.

RecordedSecretScope.description: Where a secret an item names is read, recorded when the item is registered: the first of the item's own scope, its project's org and the tenant that has the secret and that the registrant administers. Else, the broadest they administer; for a deployment's tools, deployed or promoted, where that deployment's secrets sync writes (`POST /v1/deployments/{deploymentId}/secrets`), when the registrant administers it: its project, or the tenant for a deploy that names none and for a promotion into the Default project, which are stored with no project. The runtime reads the secret there only: a secret removed from it is missing, never read from a broader scope, and one set later elsewhere changes nothing until it's recorded again: a tool by publishing a new version, an MCP endpoint by unregistering it and registering it again, a webhook trigger by an update that names its secret.

MCPEndpointSecretRef.description: The secret an MCP endpoint authenticates with: a name in the deployment's secrets store, resolved at the endpoint's tenant scope by the runtime (the shape webhooks and providers use). As the endpoint's own `secretRef`, it is sent as its bearer; inside `auth`, it is the scheme's password, client secret or header value. The endpoint keeps only this reference.

MCPEndpointAuth.description: How an MCP endpoint signs in when it isn't a plain bearer. Each scheme names its secret by reference; the runtime resolves it, and no value is stored or answered.

MCPBasicAuth.description: HTTP Basic: the runtime sends `Authorization: Basic base64(<username>:<secret>)`, with the secret `secretRef` names (a WordPress Application Password, for one).

username.description: The user name. Not a secret, and without `:`.

MCPOAuth2ClientCredentialsAuth.description: OAuth 2 client credentials: the runtime asks `tokenUrl` for an access token (`grant_type=client_credentials`) as `clientId`, with the client secret `secretRef` names, sends it as the endpoint's bearer, and asks for a new one before it expires (Drupal's Simple OAuth, for one). The token is never stored.

tokenUrl.description: The token endpoint: https, or http to a loopback host (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`).

scope.description: The scopes to ask for, space-separated, sent as-is. Absent: none asked for.

audience.description: An `audience` parameter, for identity providers that need one. Absent: none sent.

clientAuth.description: How the client authenticates to the token endpoint (RFC 6749 §2.3.1): `client_secret_basic` (an `Authorization: Basic` header, the default) or `client_secret_post` (`client_id` and `client_secret` in the form).

MCPHeaderAuth.description: Headers of the server's own, each with a secret: an API key in `X-Api-Key`, a key and a secret in two headers, or `Authorization` with a prefix other than `Bearer ` (`Token …`). The runtime resolves each `secretRef` when it connects, and refuses to follow a redirect with them, as it does for every `auth`.

name.description: An HTTP header name, once per `auth` (case-insensitive). Not one the MCP transport or HTTP sets itself (`Host`, `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `Accept`, `Connection`, `Mcp-Session-Id`, `Mcp-Protocol-Version`, `Last-Event-ID`, `traceparent`, `tracestate`, …): reason `invalid-auth`.

prefix.description: Text sent before the secret, such as `Token ` or `ApiKey `, without control characters. Absent: none. Not a secret: it reads back as registered.

endpointId.description: No `.`: an MCP tool's id is `<endpointId>.<tool name>`, so it splits at its first `.`. An endpoint registered with one before keeps it.

config.description: Transport-tagged config union. Server enforces `config.transport === transport` at registration.

scopeId.description: Required when `scopeKind` is `org` or `project`; absent for `tenant` (implicit from the session).

arguments.description: Argument bag for the prompt template. Every value must be a string per MCP spec.

category.description: Free-form resource category (`llm.inference`, `tool.invocation`, `storage.write`, `sandbox.exec`, …). Maps to `resourceKind` in the runtime.

callId.description: A model call's id (`category` `llm.inference`); its provenance `model-call` node carries it too.

rootRunId.description: The root of the record's run tree (a flow run, for its agent turns).

flowId.description: The flow of the run tree's root.

nodeId.description: The step that made the call.

purpose.description: What the call was for, beyond the turn's own model step: `guardrail-judge:<guardrail id>`.

servedModel.description: The exact model version the vendor reported (vendors alias).

fallback.description: The router picked a fallback provider for the turn.

status.description: `ok`: the provider answered. `failed`: the call threw.

providerRequestId.description: The vendor's id for the request.

attempts.description: HTTP attempts the call took, the client's retries included.

rawUsage.description: The vendor's own usage object, exactly as it reported it. Only with `include=rawUsage`.

ModelCallTokens.description: The call's tokens. `promptTokens` / `completionTokens` are the totals; `cacheReadTokens` / `cacheWriteTokens` are parts of `promptTokens`, `reasoningTokens` of `completionTokens`, present when the provider reports them.

ModelCallError.description: Why a model call failed (`status: failed`).

key.description: One entry per requested `groupBy` dimension. `null` = distinct "unattributed" bucket (records had no value for that dimension).

groups.description: The most expensive groups first (`totalUsd` descending, ties by key), at most `limit`.

totalGroups.description: How many groups there were before the `limit` cap. Absent from a runtime before 0.1.5.

truncated.description: `true` when there were more groups than `limit`: `groups` holds the most expensive ones, and `totalUsd` / `totalRecords` / `tokens` still cover every record. Absent from a runtime before 0.1.5.

groupBy.description: The dimensions the server actually grouped by — echoed so callers can round-trip the response without re-parsing the request URL.

name.description: Package name that owns the implementation (e.g. `@kindgi/adapter-model-in-process`).

version.description: Semver of the wired package.

capabilities.description: Kind-specific capability tags — e.g. `['context-isolated']` for a sandbox adapter, `['tool-use', 'streaming']` for a model adapter.

config.description: Redacted routing hints only. No secrets — bindings never surface API keys, endpoints, or credentials.

probe.description: Kind-specific diagnostic data. Callers should not depend on its exact shape.

version.description: Semver — publishing a modified policy produces a new version.

spec.description: Kind-specific policy body. For `access-control`, matches `@kindgi/specs/policy.schema.json` (rules + defaults). For `model-routing`, matches `TenantPolicy` from `@kindgi/capabilities` (providers.allow / providers.deny / models.allow / models.deny / regionAllow / maxCostPerCallUsd / maxTokensPerCall). For `tool-errors`, `ToolErrorsSpec` (maxRetries / retryOn). For `hitl`, `HitlSpec` from `@kindgi/policy-contract` (maxTimeoutMs / minReviewerRole / tools — per tool id a mode or `{ mode, requiredRole }`); it only tightens an agent's approvals. For `retention`, `{ v: 1, doc: RetentionSpec }` from `@kindgi/policy-contract` (domain / graceSeconds / mode, which must be `purge`); a tenant has one retention policy per domain, plus one for `*`. `tool-errors`, `hitl` and `retention` specs are validated on publish. For other kinds, the shape is defined by the runtime consumer.

version.description: Semver — publishing a modified policy produces a new version.

spec.description: Kind-specific policy body. For `access-control`, matches `@kindgi/specs/policy.schema.json` (rules + defaults). For `model-routing`, matches `TenantPolicy` from `@kindgi/capabilities` (providers.allow / providers.deny / models.allow / models.deny / regionAllow / maxCostPerCallUsd / maxTokensPerCall). For `tool-errors`, `ToolErrorsSpec` (maxRetries / retryOn). For `hitl`, `HitlSpec` from `@kindgi/policy-contract` (maxTimeoutMs / minReviewerRole / tools — per tool id a mode or `{ mode, requiredRole }`); it only tightens an agent's approvals. For `retention`, `{ v: 1, doc: RetentionSpec }` from `@kindgi/policy-contract` (domain / graceSeconds / mode, which must be `purge`); a tenant has one retention policy per domain, plus one for `*`. `tool-errors`, `hitl` and `retention` specs are validated on publish. For other kinds, the shape is defined by the runtime consumer.

unregisteredAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp — present iff this version has been soft-tombstoned via `POST /versions/:v/unregister`. Absent on active versions.

tenantId.description: Optional. When present, must match the caller tenant (server-derived from the token). Cross-tenant publish is rejected.

RetentionDomain.description: The kind of record a retention policy covers. `*` covers every domain without a policy of its own, except `memory` and `conversation`: they hold people's words, so only a policy naming them purges them.

policyIds.description: Every policy id that covers the domain, sorted.

appliedPolicyId.description: The one that applies: the policy whose latest version is highest, and on equal versions the lower policy id. Unregister the others.

id.description: The tombstoned row's id in its domain.

purgeAt.description: `unregisteredAt` plus `graceSeconds`: when a sweep purges the row.

pastGrace.description: Whether a sweep would purge the row now.

policyId.description: The retention policy that covers the domain. Absent when none does, and this server's limit decides (`limitApplied`); always present on a server with no limit.

graceSeconds.description: How long the row is kept, in seconds (`-1`: a hold, never purged): the policy's grace, or this server's limit (`limitApplied`).

limitApplied.description: Present when this server's retention limit for the domain set `graceSeconds`: no policy covers the domain, or its policy keeps rows longer than the limit, or holds them.

hasMore.description: Some domain has more scheduled rows than this page returned (`limit` is per domain). Always sent from 0.1.4; a runtime before it sends none.

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` for the next page. Absent when `hasMore: false`, or when the runtime cannot continue a page.

domainsMissingAdapter.description: Domains a retention policy covers that this deployment can't purge (no adapter is wired).

unpolicedDomains.description: Domains no retention policy covers and this server sets no retention limit for: their tombstones are kept.

conflicts.description: Domains more than one retention policy covers. Absent or empty: none.

domain.description: Sweep only this domain. Absent: every domain.

maxPerDomain.description: The most rows one call purges per domain (default 500); the rest are `remaining`.
The most rows this call purges (default 500); the rest are `remaining`.

remaining.description: Rows past grace this call left (the `maxPerDomain` cap); sweep again.

limitApplied.description: Present when this server's retention limit set the grace (see `RetentionScheduledItem.limitApplied`).

missingAdapter.description: Present when this deployment can't purge the domain (no adapter).

conflicts.description: Domains more than one retention policy covers. Absent or empty: none.

projectId.description: The test set's project: every version of a test set is in the one project. Absent when the runtime doesn't record it: a pack `kindgi dev` serves from disk, or a runtime before Kindgi 0.1.6.

version.description: Semver — publishing a modified suite produces a new version.

spec.description: Kind-specific suite body. For `accuracy`, typically `{ cases: [{ input, expectedOutput }], grader?: { adapterId, config? } }`. For `pairwise`, typically `{ prompts, variantA, variantB }`. For `regression`, typically `{ baseline, cases }`. For `human-review`, typically `{ rubric, reviewerRole }`. For `benchmark`, typically `{ benchmark: { name, version } }`. For `custom`, typically `{ handler: { modulePath, entrypointPath }, cases }`.

unregisteredAt.description: Present only on an unregistered version: one `GET …/versions?includeTombstoned=true` lists, or a retired test set (every version unregistered) as `GET /v1/eval-suites?includeRetired=true` lists it.

projectId.description: Project this belongs to (its content scope). Required: missing, or not a project in the caller's tenant → `400 bad-input`.

tenantId.description: Optional. When present, must match the caller tenant (server-derived from the token). Cross-tenant publish is rejected.

BlockKind.description: `prompt`: a Liquid template an agent renders as its instructions. `settings`: a JSON object tools and templates read.

template.description: Liquid, rendered as an agent's instructions are (same parameters and auto-injected variables).

values.description: What tools read (`ToolContext.settings[<block id>]`) and templates read (`settings.<block id>.<key>`).

schema.description: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) the values must satisfy. A later version's values must satisfy the latest version's schema too.

Block.description: A data block version: a prompt or settings, versioned like a tool (immutable versions, soft unregister). An agent version pins the block versions it uses when it is published. Belongs to one project and is authorized through it.

unregisteredAt.description: Present only on an unregistered version; agent versions that pin it still read it.

projectId.description: Project this belongs to (its content scope). Required: missing, or not a project in the caller's tenant → `400 bad-input`.

EvalBaseline.description: What a comparison compares the candidate against: `'recorded'` (each case's recorded output, what was judged), a version (`{ agentId, version }`, replayed under the same rules), or the version live in a scope (`{ live: { projectId?, segments? } }`, `segments` a path in the project, coarse to fine). Only `'recorded'` runs today; the others are refused when the run starts.

segments.description: A segment path in `projectId`, coarse to fine, as live versions resolve it. Needs `projectId`.

EvalOverrides.description: For an agent candidate: block content its replays run instead of the version's pinned content (an improvement pass's search). `settings`: values by settings block id, each a block the version pins, satisfying its schema. `prompts`: a template for the prompt block the version pins, which reads and names only what the agent has (its parameters, the variables the current template reads, the settings blocks it pins, its tools' and blocks' ids) and is at most twice as long. Anything else is `400 validation-failed`. A comparison with overrides can't gate a promotion.

EvalSample.description: Only part of the test set's cases: split once into a hold-out part (about `holdOutShare` of them) and a search part (the rest), stratified (the cases that carry a correction, then of the others the cases with a "no" and the rest, each split on its own, a stratum of two or more giving each part at least one, so both parts check a correction when two cases carry one), in the order of a hash of each case id and `seed`. The same seed always splits the same test set the same way. A promotion gate refuses a comparison on the search part (`comparison.sample`).

EvalComparison.description: A comparison eval run's settings (a `judged` suite).

reads.description: Whether replayed reads use the past run's results when it has them (`recorded`), or run live.

classWeights.description: Which judgments count: each at its class's weight (`as-recorded`, the default), or only those recorded while their class was restricted (`Judgment.restricted`), the others weighing 0 (`restricted-only`).

rescoreOf.description: Rescore that comparison eval run instead of replaying: its replays' outputs are scored again, with the judgments recorded on them since (a changed answer judged on the replay itself). Nothing runs, and the run rescored stays as it was. Set by `POST /v1/eval-runs/{runId}/rescore`.

ComparisonMetric.description: One metric, the recorded runs beside the candidate. `null` where a side had no judged evidence; `n` / `weight` are the candidate's evidence (cases with judged items, and the judgment weight behind them), `baselineN` / `baselineWeight` the recorded side's.

k.description: `weightedPrecisionAtK`: the ranked items it looked at.

spread.description: With more than one repetition: the candidate's max − min across them.

freshWeight.description: Of `weight`, the part judged on the candidate's replays themselves (a rescore, after people judged a changed answer there). Absent when none. Not on `weightedPrecisionAtK`.

ComparisonCandidate.description: What ran on the cases: an agent version, or a flow version (with any versions it swapped in).

pinsDigest.description: The version's pinsDigest: what it ran, as a promotion gate checks. Absent for a version published before pins, and from a comparison recorded before it.

overrides.description: The blocks whose content the replays replaced (`overrides`): no published version ran, so it can't gate a promotion. Absent otherwise.

JudgedComparisonSummary.description: What a comparison concluded: the candidate beside the recorded runs, the case counts, and the metrics. What a promotion gate reads.

baseline.description: What the candidate was compared with: `recorded` (the test set's recorded runs, with the versions that served them), or another version.

scope.description: Where the test set's judgments came from.

diverged.description: Cases where a read with no recording ran live under `reads: 'recorded'`.

refusedWrites.description: Tool calls the replay refused across the cases (what the candidate would have done). Reads count too, despite the name: the replay refuses a call it can't run live (a write, or a read that needs an approval or reaches outside, say) that has no recording of the same call.

errors.description: Cases none of whose repetitions ran.

erased.description: Cases an erasure cleared (a person's words were erased): left out of the run and the metrics. Absent: none.

rescoreOf.description: A rescore: the comparison eval run whose replays it scored again.

notRescored.description: A rescore: cases whose replays couldn't be read again (a retention purge, say), kept at their earlier scores. Absent: none.

stopped.description: Flow cases that stopped at a refused tool call: no output to score, so they're left out of the metrics.

classWeights.description: Which judgments counted. Absent from a comparison recorded before restricted classes: `as-recorded`.

sample.description: The part of the test set it ran. Absent: every case.

models.description: The models that answered the candidate's replays, and how many replays each.

corrections.description: Corrections graded across the cases: shown for a promotion gate, not enforced. Absent when the test set carries no corrections.

judgments.description: Each correction graded, by its judgment: whether it passed (every repetition did). What an improvement pass compares, run to run, to keep only a model-settings change that breaks none the current version passes. Absent from a comparison recorded before it.

JudgedComparisonCost.description: What the candidate's replays cost in model calls, as the runtime reported it. Absent from a summary when no case's replays reported a cost.

candidate.description: Each repetition's total over `cases`, averaged over the repetitions, in US dollars.

spread.description: With more than one repetition: the totals' max − min.

cases.description: The cases whose every repetition reported a cost: the ones totalled.

CallDifference.description: One way a run's calls differed from a correction; it can quote argument values.

refused.description: How many of the actual calls were refused on the replay. Absent when none were.
How many of the forbidden calls were refused on the replay. Absent when none were.
Present and true when the call blamed for the miss was refused on the replay.
Present and true when the call blamed for the miss was refused on the replay.

ComparisonCaseResult.description: One case of a comparison: its replay runs, the scores, the items kept, dropped and new, the tool calls, and why it didn't run when it didn't.

runIds.description: The candidate's replay runs, one per repetition.

baseline.description: An output's score: Σ yesWeight and Σ totalWeight over its judged items, and over those among the first `k` ranked items.

fresh.description: The part of these sums judged on this output itself (a replay judged after it ran). Absent when none was.

items.description: An output's score: Σ yesWeight and Σ totalWeight over its judged items, and over those among the first `k` ranked items.

fresh.description: The part of these sums judged on this output itself (a replay judged after it ran). Absent when none was.

changes.description: The first repetition's items against the judged ones.

judged.description: What people said about this item on the replay itself, once they judged it there.

tools.description: The first repetition's tool calls, and what happened to each.

recomputed.description: With `source: 'live'`: the call ran again from the same arguments because the compared version pins other settings, and the tool reads from nowhere, so it didn't diverge. Absent from older servers, and otherwise.

corrections.description: Each correction graded on this case: its verdict and how many repetitions passed. Shown, not enforced. Survives an erasure — the differences, which quote values, are in `correctionDifferences`.

pass.description: Passed only when every repetition passed.

correctionDifferences.description: The ways each correction's calls differed, by judgment: the differences from the first repetition that failed it, and that repetition's number. Quotes argument values, so an erasure clears it (the verdicts and counts stay in `corrections`).

repetition.description: Which repetition (1-based) these differences are from.

costUsd.description: What each repetition's replay cost in model calls, as the runtime reported it, in US dollars: one per repetition. Absent when a repetition reported none.

refusedWrites.description: Tool calls the replay refused in this case: the most in any one of its repetitions. Reads count too, despite the name.

stopped.description: Set when the replay stopped at a refused tool call: what it would have done.

rescored.description: Set in a rescore when this case's replays can't be read again: its scores are the run rescored's.

JudgedComparisonResult.description: A comparison's `result` (a `judged` eval run's): the summary and each case. `EvalRun.result` stays an open object, since each kind has its own; the clients read it as this (TS `comparisonOf(run)`, Python `comparison_of(run)`).

projectId.description: The project the eval run is in: the one it was started in. Absent on a runtime before Kindgi 0.1.6.

result.description: Kind-specific opaque JSON. For `accuracy`, contains `{ passCount, totalCount, meanScore, perCase[] }`. For `judged` (a comparison), `{ summary, perCase[] }`: the summary has the baseline (the versions behind the recorded runs) and the candidate (`{ kind: "agent", agentId, version }` or `{ kind: "flow", flowId, version, versions? }`), the case counts (`cases`, `diverged`, `refusedWrites`, `errors`, and `stopped`: flow cases that stopped at a refused tool call, left out of the metrics), the models that answered, and `metrics` (`weightedYesShare`, `judgedCoverage`, `weightedPrecisionAtK`, each `{ baseline, candidate, delta, n, weight, baselineN, baselineWeight, direction, k?, spread? }`); each case has its replay runs, the scores, the items kept, dropped and new, the tool calls with what happened to each, and `stopped` (what it would have done) when it stopped. Other kinds define their own shapes as their dispatchers ship.

cancelReason.description: Why a `cancelled` run stopped when nobody cancelled it: its project or tenant took no new runs when a case started (`project-suspended`, `tenant-suspended`, `tenant-closing`). The cases before it are in `result`. Absent when it was cancelled, and from a runtime that doesn't say. A plain string: a later reason doesn't break a client.

projectId.description: Project this belongs to (its content scope). Required: missing, or not a project in the caller's tenant → `400 bad-input`.

classWeights.description: Which judgments count: each at its class's weight (`as-recorded`, the default), or only those recorded while their class was restricted (`Judgment.restricted`), the others weighing 0 (`restricted-only`).

StartEvalRunBody.description: Exactly one of `agentRef` or `flowRef` MUST be supplied. `dryRun: true` returns a plan preview without invoking the subject. For a `judged` suite (a test set), the run is a comparison: `agentRef` or `flowRef` with its `version` is the candidate, replayed on each case without doing anything the past run didn't (a flow stops at a write the replay refuses); `baseline` (default `'recorded'`), `reads` (default `recorded`), `repetitions` (default 1) and `k` (default 10) set how. With `flowRef`, `versions` runs the flow with some of its agents or tools at other versions; an id the flow doesn't use, or a version that isn't published, is refused (`400 validation-failed`, each under `details.issues`).

projectId.description: The run's project, needed only from a runtime that doesn't record it on the run.

IdentityProviderKind.description: `oidc`: an OpenID Connect identity provider people sign in with (Okta, Entra ID, Google, Keycloak…); its endpoints come from its discovery document. `saml`: a SAML 2.0 identity provider people sign in with.

ClaimMappingScopesSpec.description: Claim path + optional delimiter for extracting Kindgi OAuth scopes from provider claims. When absent, scopes come from the token response `scope` field instead.

ClaimMappingSpec.description: Per-provider claim mapping. All fields optional; closer to OIDC defaults (sub/email/name) → fewer overrides needed.

IdentityProviderSignIn.description: What to give the identity provider so it can send people back: set by the deployment on what it returns, ignored on registration. OIDC: `redirectUri`. SAML: `spEntityId`, `acsUrl`, `spMetadataUrl`.

OidcIdentityProviderConfig.description: An OpenID Connect identity provider people sign in with. The endpoints come from the issuer's discovery document when absent, and are returned once the deployment has them.

displayName.description: The name a sign-in page shows ("Sign in with …"). Default: `providerId`.

domains.description: The email domains whose people sign in with this provider (lowercase, e.g. `acme.com`): how an email-first sign-in page finds it.

join.description: Who may sign in the first time: `invite` (default) only people a tenant admin added; `domain` also anyone from one of `domains`, once the deployment has verified them.

clientSecretRef.description: Opaque reference resolved server-side. Never a plaintext secret.

SamlIdentityProviderConfig.description: A SAML 2.0 identity provider people sign in with: its metadata XML, or its entity ID, single sign-on URL and signing certificates. Keys are given as references, never as keys.

displayName.description: The name a sign-in page shows ("Sign in with …"). Default: `providerId`.

domains.description: The email domains whose people sign in with this provider (lowercase, e.g. `acme.com`): how an email-first sign-in page finds it.

join.description: Who may sign in the first time: `invite` (default) only people a tenant admin added; `domain` also anyone from one of `domains`, once the deployment has verified them.

idpSsoUrl.description: The IdP's single sign-on URL (HTTP-Redirect binding).

idpCertificates.description: The IdP's signing certificates (PEM); several during a rollover.

spSigningKeyRef.description: Opaque reference to the service provider's signing key, for IdPs that require signed AuthnRequests. Never a plaintext key.

spDecryptionKeyRef.description: Opaque reference to the key that decrypts encrypted assertions. Never a plaintext key.

attributeMapping.description: Assertion attribute names. Defaults: `userId` = the NameID, `email` = `email`.

IdentityProviderConfig.description: An identity provider registered on a tenant, one shape per `kind` (narrow on `kind` before reading kind-specific fields). Secrets are always REFERENCES resolved server-side (`clientSecretRef`, `spSigningKeyRef`, `spDecryptionKeyRef`); a plaintext secret never crosses the wire, and a `clientSecret` field is refused.

RegisterIdentityProviderBody.description: The identity provider to register, one shape per `kind`: `oidc` or `saml`. Secrets by reference only (`clientSecretRef`, `spSigningKeyRef`, `spDecryptionKeyRef`); a `clientSecret` field is refused.

GetIdentityProviderResult.description: An identity provider as stored, one shape per `kind`, with `signIn` when the deployment sets it. Secrets appear only as references.

hasMore.description: Always `false`: the list comes whole. Absent from older servers.

changes.description: Who may add, change and remove the providers here: `tenant`, its admins; `operator`, only the deployment's own token, because the operator manages sign-in (`KINDGI_AUTH_TENANT_PROVIDERS=off`). The providers there sign people in either way. Absent from older servers: read it as `tenant`.

SignInOption.description: One way to sign in, as a sign-in page shows it.

signInUrl.description: Where the browser goes to start signing in with this provider.

owner.description: Whose it is: a workspace's own identity provider (`tenant`), or one the deployment offers everyone it has added ("Continue with Google", `deployment`). A sign-in page shows a workspace's own first. Absent: `tenant`.

ConsoleLink.description: One of the deployment's own links, which the console shows on every page.

url.description: An absolute https URL with no username or password.

methods.description: The ways in this deployment allows, for a sign-in page to show. Absent from older servers.

identityProviders.description: Sign-in with an organization's identity provider (email first).

apiToken.description: Sign-in to the console with an API token (`POST /v1/auth/token-sign-in`).

sessionCookie.description: The browser session cookie's kind: `secure` (`Secure` and `__Host-`, kept by browsers only over https, and by some on http://localhost), or `plain` (development on a loopback address only, so every browser keeps it there). A sign-in page can check the browser keeps that kind before offering sign-in. Absent from older servers, and where there are no browser sessions: treat as `secure`.

emailLink.description: Present when the deployment emails sign-in links: a sign-in page offers "Email me a sign-in link". With `captchaSiteKey`, the request needs a Cloudflare Turnstile token (`x-captcha-response`).

legal.description: The deployment's terms and privacy policy, for a sign-in page to link: only the ones its operator set, each an absolute https URL with no username or password. Absent when neither is set, and from older servers.

links.description: The deployment's own links (its help desk, status page, data processing terms), which the console shows on every page, the sign-in page too, in its operator's order. Absent when there are none, and from older servers.

expiresAt.description: When the session ends at the latest: its lifetime, or the key's expiry if sooner.

SignInEvent.description: One sign-in audit event, flattened: who signed in or out, how, from where, and what was refused.

kind.description: `signed-in` / `signed-out`; `sign-in-refused` (with `reason`); `sign-in-link-sent` / `sign-in-link-capped` (an emailed link, for `userId`; `reason` is the limit that held); `sessions-revoked` ("sign out everywhere", or removing a person; `byUserId` is the admin who did it, if not the person); `sessions-ended` (a changed boot token, or a session made without a second factor in a workspace that requires one: `reason` says which); `second-factor-set-up`, `second-factor-removed` (`byUserId` is the admin who removed it, if not the person) and `recovery-codes-replaced`. Never a key or a code.

userId.description: The person the event is about: who signed in or out, whose sessions ended, or whom a link was for. Absent on a refusal that names no one.

method.description: How: `api-token`, `email-link`, `google`, `microsoft`, `github`, or a workspace identity provider's id.

clientAddress.description: The client's address, as the runtime trusts it.

reason.description: Why a sign-in was refused, or which limit held.

byUserId.description: Who acted, when it isn't `userId`: the admin who ended this person's sessions.

provider.description: The provider as stored: discovered endpoints, and `signIn` (what to give the identity provider). Absent from older servers.

UpdateIdentityProviderBody.description: Changes to a registered identity provider: a field given replaces the stored one, `null` removes an optional one, and anything not given stays. The result must still be a whole provider of its `kind` (the fields `IdentityProviderConfig` requires for it), checked as a registration is. `providerId` and `kind` can't change; `signIn` is the deployment's and is ignored. A new `issuer` drops the endpoints discovered from the old one.

providerId.description: Must match the path when given.

clientSecretRef.description: Opaque reference resolved server-side. Never a plaintext secret.

provider.description: The provider as stored now; its `signIn` is unchanged.

IdentityProviderSignInUrls.description: What to give the identity provider so it can send people back, for a provider under this `providerId`: the same before it's registered, after, and after an unregister and a new registration, so the identity provider's side can be set up first. Not secrets: they're in every sign-in's browser redirects.

registered.description: Whether a provider is registered under this `providerId` now.

sessionToken.description: Opaque session token (`kgi_sk_…`), shown once: the server keeps only a hash of it. Never parse it. Send as `Authorization: Bearer <sessionToken>` on subsequent requests. The underlying provider access-token never leaves the server.

WhoamiResult.description: Introspection of the caller's current authentication context. Always carries `tenantId` and `scopes` (empty for static bearer tokens), plus `userId` when the token carries one; `principal` says whom the caller acts as, and an API key adds `tokenId`, its `role` and the `projectId` it is limited to; session-token callers additionally see `sessionId`, `providerId`, and `expiresAt`. `user` is the caller's directory record, present when the deployment wires an identity directory and it knows the `userId`. `reviewerRole` is set when the caller is a reviewer — its token carries a reviewer role, or its user is a registered reviewer — so clients can gate reviewer-only UI (the approvals surface) without a second round trip.

actor.description: The caller as approvals name a person: `user:<id>` or `service_account:<id>`, the same string as an approval's `requestedBy` and a decision's `decidedBy`.

reviewerRole.description: Reviewer role class. Hierarchy: standard < senior < admin.

tokenId.description: The caller's API key, when it is one.

role.description: The caller's API key role, when the key has one, or its session's role ceiling.

projectId.description: The project the caller's API key or session is limited to, when it is.

tenantAdmin.description: Whether the caller is a tenant admin, decided as the admin routes decide it: `admin` on the tenant when the runtime authorizes, otherwise the `tenant-admin` scope of a full key (never a `member` key or one limited to a project). A console shows its admin pages by it. Absent from older servers: read `scopes`.

servedEnv.description: The env this runtime serves (`KINDGI_ENV`): where the values its tools read are kept. With `refusesOtherEnvs`, it's the only one: a secret, env value or secret reference under another env is refused (`409 env-not-served`), so a client defaults to `envName`. Absent when the runtime serves no env, and from older servers.

refusesOtherEnvs.description: Whether values under any other env are refused.

UserRecord.description: Tenant-scoped user record (admin plane). `primaryEmail` may be redacted on the wire based on tenant policy (the routes treat it as opaque). `metadata` is free-form JSON — deployments carry IdP claims / provisioning source / roles here.

unregisteredAt.description: When they were removed from the tenant (`POST /v1/identity/users/{userId}/unregister`); absent while they are here.

invite.description: Their invitation, while they haven't signed in: absent once they have, for people added without an email, and for people added before invitations (from 0.1.9).

firstSignedInAt.description: Their first sign-in that made a session. Absent before it, and for people who last signed in before it was kept (from 0.1.9).

grants.description: The person's grants: only on `GET /v1/identity/users?include=grants`, and only from a runtime that reads grants.

UserInvite.description: An open invitation. `pending` signs in. `expired` (past `expiresAt`, 7 days after it was made or last renewed) is refused at every way of signing in until a tenant admin renews it (`POST /v1/identity/users/{userId}/invite`).

sentAt.description: When it was last emailed; absent when it never was.

InviteEmail.description: Whether the invitation was emailed, and why not: `no-email` (the person has no email, so isn't invited), `not-requested` (`sendInvite: false`), `not-configured` (the deployment sends no email), `send-failed` (the mail server refused it or didn't answer), `capped` (the workspace, or the whole deployment, has sent as many invitation emails as it may in 24 hours). An invitation not emailed is still open: tell them yourself.

UserCreated.description: The person just added, and whether their invitation was emailed (`inviteEmail`: absent from a runtime that sends no invitations).

unregisteredAt.description: When they were removed from the tenant (`POST /v1/identity/users/{userId}/unregister`); absent while they are here.

invite.description: Their invitation, while they haven't signed in: absent once they have, for people added without an email, and for people added before invitations (from 0.1.9).

firstSignedInAt.description: Their first sign-in that made a session. Absent before it, and for people who last signed in before it was kept (from 0.1.9).

InviteRenewed.description: The person, with their invitation's new expiry, and whether it was emailed.

SecondFactorProof.description: Exactly one: a code from the authenticator app, or one of the recovery codes (used up by this).

SecondFactorConfirmBody.description: A code from the new key, as the authenticator app shows it.

SecondFactorStatus.description: A person's second factor, and whether their workspace requires one. With `setUp`, `since`, `recoveryCodesLeft` and `usable` are given; without it, `started`. Never a key or a code.

started.description: A key was given to set one up, and isn't confirmed yet.

usable.description: `false`: its key can't be opened any more (the sign-in secret changed past it). A recovery code still works, as does setting it up again, or an admin removing it.

required.description: The workspace requires a second factor at sign-in.

SecondFactorKey.description: A new key to set up, shown this once: `uri` for an authenticator app (as a QR code), `key` to type in. Nothing changes until it is confirmed.

SecondFactorRecoveryCodes.description: The 10 recovery codes, shown this once. Each signs in once in place of a code from the app; any earlier ones stop working.

SecondFactorRemoved.description: `false` when there was none to remove.

required.description: Signing in by the deployment's own ways in takes a second factor. Signing in through the workspace's own identity provider is exempt: it owns MFA there. A site's people sign in through the site, which owns their second factor, so the setting doesn't apply to them. API keys aren't covered.

onPreviousSecret.description: People whose key is still kept under the deployment's previous sign-in secret: each moves to the current one at their next code. Keep the previous secret configured until this is 0.

unusable.description: People whose key opens under neither secret: they need a recovery code, or an admin to remove it.

AuthSettingsPatch.description: Require a second factor at sign-in, or stop requiring one.

UnregisterUserResult.description: A removed person, and what removing them took away (each 0 when they were already removed).

sendInvite.description: Email them the invitation (default `true`). `false` still invites them, for an admin who tells them another way. A person without an email isn't invited.

PersonGrants.description: What a person may do, as granted directly: tenant admin, a role on a project (its memberships), a role in a team, and the reviewer roster. What a team's or an org's grants imply is not expanded.

tenantAdmin.description: Whether the person is a tenant admin. Absent when the runtime has no authorization store: nothing grants it then.

tenantMember.description: Whether the person is a tenant member: they read the tenant's settings (providers, policies, adapters, signing keys, deployments), not its projects. A person is one from being added. Absent when the runtime has no authorization store, or doesn't report it.

PersonProjectRole.description: A person's direct role on a project.

PersonTeamRole.description: A person's role in a team.

PersonReviewerRole.description: A person's active entry on the reviewer roster.

PersonGrantBody.description: The grant to give or take: tenant admin. A person's project and team roles have their own membership routes.

JudgingQueueState.description: Where a queued run stands. `judged`: every rule that queued it has the judgment it wants. `erased`: the run's content is gone (erased, or the run purged); the item shows nothing of it.

JudgingRuleWhen.description: Which of a project's runs a rule matches as they end. Every field narrows; absent fields don't. `agentIds` or `flowIds`, not both. Top-level runs only (an agent's own runs, not its turns as a flow's step); replays never match.

versions.description: These versions exactly, or `live`: runs that got the agent's live version, not one the caller named. Runs from before the runtime recorded how their version was chosen never match `live`.

status.description: How the run ended. Only `completed` today: a judgment needs a completed run, so `failed` and `cancelled` are refused (400). Absent: `completed`.

includeDryRuns.description: Dry runs are left out unless `true`.

JudgingRuleSpec.description: A judging rule as written. It only lists runs: nothing here starts a model.
