sample.description: The share of matching runs queued, decided by the run and rule ids: the same every time and across the rule's versions, so raising it keeps the runs it took before. Default 1.

maxOpen.description: Queue nothing while this rule has this many open items. Absent: no cap.

judgeClassId.description: Whose judgment it wants: one of this class closes it. Absent: any judgment does.

JudgingRulePatch.description: The fields to change; `when` is replaced whole.

sample.description: The share of matching runs queued, decided by the run and rule ids: the same every time and across the rule's versions, so raising it keeps the runs it took before. Default 1.

maxOpen.description: Queue nothing while this rule has this many open items. `null` removes the cap.

judgeClassId.description: Whose judgment it wants: one of this class closes it. `null`: any judgment does.

JudgingRule.description: One version of a judging rule; the latest live one applies.

maxOpen.description: Queue nothing while this rule has this many open items. Absent: no cap.

judgeClassId.description: Whose judgment it wants: one of this class closes it. Absent: any judgment does.

JudgingProgress.description: The live judgments on the run so far, by class.

JudgingItemCan.description: What the caller may do with the item, by the check the routes make (`write` on the project, as judging the run needs).

JudgingQueueItem.description: A queued run: never its content, only what it was and where it stands.

rules.description: The rules that queued it, each at the version that did.

wantedClassIds.description: The judge classes its rules want.

anyJudgment.description: One of its rules wants any judgment.

closedBy.description: Who dismissed or reopened it last.

reason.description: Why it was dismissed, when they said.

total.description: Every item the filters match, across pages.

JudgingResultGroup.description: One rule version's runs of one agent version. `added` = `open` + `judged` + `dismissed` + `erased`.

agentVersion.description: `null`: a flow run, or one from before versions were recorded.

skippedByCap.description: Runs the rule matched and sampled but didn't queue, because `maxOpen` were waiting, even when another rule queued them. Non-zero: the queued runs lean toward quiet times. `added` + `skippedByCap` = every run the rule matched and sampled.

judgments.description: Live judgments on the queued runs: each is one person's verdict on one item of a run's output.

runsWithJudgments.description: The queued runs with at least one live judgment: the runs `judgments` and `yesShare` come from, whatever their item's state now (still `open`, closed as `judged`, or dismissed after someone judged it). Several people judging one run make several judgments but one run here. Absent from a runtime that doesn't count them.

yesShare.description: The `yes` share of those judgments, each weighted by its class (unclassified: 1). `null` with none.

byClass.description: The same judgments by class, unweighted.

groups.description: By the rule's version and the agent's, newest rule version first: two versions of a rule are two sampling designs, never pooled.

matched.description: Those the rule would have queued, with its `sample` (`maxOpen` isn't applied).

JudgingQueueRecentInput.description: Which recent runs to catch the rule up on. Give `last`, `since`, or both.

last.description: This many of the project's most recent top-level runs (newest first).

since.description: Runs completed at or after this time.

queued.description: Matching recent runs this call newly queued for the rule: a new queue item, or the rule added to one already waiting for another rule.

alreadyQueued.description: Matching recent runs this rule had already queued and that are still open (deduped per `(rule, run)`).

alreadyReviewed.description: Matching recent runs whose run was already judged or dismissed: left as they are, not re-queued. An already-erased run is no longer a match and is counted nowhere, so `queued`, `alreadyQueued` and `alreadyReviewed` together are the matches.

AccessRole.description: A project role, as the authorization model holds it: `owner` > `admin` > `editor` > `viewer` (a membership stored as `member` is `viewer`).

since.description: When the membership was added, when the runtime keeps it.

role.description: The role the team holds on the project.

since.description: When the caller joined the team, when the runtime keeps it.

AccessPathOrgAdmin.description: An admin of the org the project sits in: admin on the project.

AccessPathTenantAdmin.description: A tenant admin: admin on every project.

AccessPath.description: One way the caller holds a role on a project: a membership of its own, a team it is in, an org it administers, or tenant admin.

role.description: The highest role the caller holds on the project, whichever way.

via.description: Every way the caller holds a role on it (for "My access").

id.description: The caller's reviewer id, its row on the roster: an approval assigned to the caller names it in `assignedTo`. Absent without a roster row (then `canDecide` is false), and from a runtime before 0.1.6.

decides.description: The approvals' required roles the caller may decide: its own rank and below, lowest first.

canDecide.description: Whether the caller can decide at all: deciding also needs its user and its row on the reviewer roster. False for a token that carries a reviewer role without them.

RoleActions.description: What a project role allows on the project and on every object of each type in it, by object type.

RoleCapabilities.description: What each project role allows, worked out by the runtime from its authorization model. A client decides an action as `capabilities[project.role][type]` holding it; the server still checks every call. An object can grant more on itself (an agent's own editor), never less, so this is what the caller may do at the least.

admin.description: Tenant admin, decided as the admin routes decide it (a `member` key's never is).

member.description: Tenant member: reads the tenant's settings. Absent when the runtime doesn't report it.

MyKeyLimits.description: The caller's API key, when it is one, and what it limits.

role.description: The most the key may do, under its principal's grants: an `admin` key may administer the tenant when its principal is a tenant admin; a `member` key takes no admin action on the tenant, whoever it's for; below it, its principal's roles hold (a project admin's member key administers that project).

projectId.description: The project the key is limited to: `projects` holds it alone, and no org or team is administered through it.

MyPermissions.description: What the caller may do, with its API key's limits applied: tenant admin and member, its reviewer role, its key's limits and capabilities, the projects it may read with its role in each and how it holds it, its orgs and teams, and what each project role allows. Only what the caller may see: nothing names a project it can't read, or anyone else's role.

reviewer.description: Present when the caller is a reviewer.

tokenCapabilities.description: The framework capabilities the caller's token carries (`env:write`, `secrets:write`, `secrets:rotate`, …), which secret, env and signing-key writes require on top of admin at their scope. A sign-in session carries those its person holds: none unless the runtime gives them some, as it does a tenant's first admin. An API key carries those it was minted with (`POST /v1/tokens`, none by default).

projects.description: The projects the caller may read, by name.

orgs.description: The orgs the caller is a member or admin of, by name.

teams.description: The teams the caller is a member or admin of, by name.

readOnlyNotice.description: The line a console shows a caller who may only view a project, as a tenant admin set it in the tenant config (`kind: 'config'`, key `console.readOnlyNotice`). Plain text on one line, at most 280 characters. Absent when none is set: the console shows its own.

IdentitySessionSummary.description: Wire-safe subset of a session. Excludes provider access-token / refresh-token — those never cross the wire, even to admins.

version.description: Absent for guardrails, which have no version.
Absent for guardrails, which have no version.
The version the agent is registered as.

authoredVersion.description: The version the agent's or flow's definition names, present when it differs from `version`: that version was registered already with other pins or content, and versions never change, so the deploy registered the next free version in its line (or an earlier deploy did).

reason.description: Why `version` differs from `authoredVersion`: `pins-changed` (a tool or agent it uses has a new version), `unpinned` (`authoredVersion` was published before pins existed), `version-taken` (`authoredVersion` is registered with other content).

newVersion.description: `true`: this deploy registered `version`; `false`: an earlier deploy did.

pinChanges.description: For `pins-changed`: the pins that differ from `authoredVersion`'s.

version.description: The version the agent is registered as.

authoredVersion.description: The version the agent's or flow's definition names, present when it differs from `version`: that version was registered already with other pins or content, and versions never change, so the deploy registered the next free version in its line (or an earlier deploy did).

reason.description: Why `version` differs from `authoredVersion`: `pins-changed` (a tool or agent it uses has a new version), `unpinned` (`authoredVersion` was published before pins existed), `version-taken` (`authoredVersion` is registered with other content).

newVersion.description: `true`: this deploy registered `version`; `false`: an earlier deploy did.

pinChanges.description: For `pins-changed`: the pins that differ from `authoredVersion`'s.

DeploymentEndpointProblem.description: While the deployment waits for a pack service (`pending`, or `cleared` and `waiting`): the last reason recorded while it waited. A `ready` endpoint has none, nor a `retired` one. A fixed code, never free text.

code.description: One of a fixed list; a later runtime may add codes, so treat an unknown one as a reason not yet named. The server refused the endpoint it was given: `endpoint-url-invalid` (not `https`, or with user info or a path), `endpoint-host-not-allowed` (the host isn't on the operator's allowlist), `endpoint-name-mismatch` (the host doesn't name this deployment's service), `endpoint-unreachable` (the pack service didn't answer), `endpoint-info-mismatch` (it answered as another pack or version), `image-not-allowed` (the image is outside the tenant's repository). The pack service couldn't be created: `tenant-not-provisioned` (the tenant has nowhere to run pack services yet), `capacity-unavailable` (no room for another pack service just now), `service-start-failed` (the image was deployed but didn't start). It can't be given its declared environment (`GET /v1/deployments/{deploymentId}/pack-env` names the names): `pack-env-ambiguous`, `pack-env-secret-not-yet`, `pack-env-missing`, `pack-env-secret-unreadable` (a name's secret can't be read for a reason the platform fixes, not the owner; it's tried again). It can't be given its secrets: `pack-env-secrets-unaudited` (the runtime has nowhere to audit a secret it gives out; the platform fixes it, and it's tried again), `pack-env-secret-too-large` (a secret's value is over 32768 bytes, the most a pack service can be given), `pack-env-secret-capacity` (a name is set only as a secret, and there's no room just now for a pack service that can be given one, apart from other projects'; it's tried again).

DeploymentEndpoint.description: Its pack service's status, when the server routes each pack call to the deployment that shipped the tool (`KINDGI_PACK_ROUTING=per-deployment`). Absent otherwise, and for a deployment that ships nothing a pack service serves (no tool, and no guardrail check but built-in ones: a pack of agents and flows only), which needs none. `pending`: no pack service yet, and calls to its tools fail (`pack-endpoint-pending`) rather than go to another deployment. `ready`: calls go to its own pack service. `cleared`: its pack service was taken down, and calls fail (`pack-endpoint-cleared`); it carries `waiting` or `retired` to say whether it comes back. Carries no URL and no token.

waiting.description: `cleared` only: a pack service is wanted for it again, as once a suspension that took its service down is lifted, and it lists as needing one; `problem` says why it isn't back yet. A `cleared` endpoint carries this or `retired`, never both. Absent from older servers, which send neither.

retired.description: `cleared` only: why no pack service is wanted for it now. `superseded` is for good: newer deployments ship every tool version and check it does, so no new call reaches it; a tool call a step made on it still goes back to it when the step runs again, and fails closed (`pack-endpoint-cleared`). `tenant-closing`, `tenant-suspended`, `project-suspended` and `pack-suspended` last until the tenant, project or pack is restored. A later runtime may add reasons, so treat an unknown one as a reason not yet named. A `cleared` endpoint carries this or `waiting`, never both. Absent from older servers, which send neither.

packEnvProblem.description: `ready` only: the pack service runs on the values it was last given, because the newest can't be given to it (a required one was removed, say, or a secret can't be given), or didn't start (`pack-env-update-failed`). Gone once they can, or do. For a name that can't be given, `GET /v1/deployments/{deploymentId}/pack-env` names it. Absent from older servers.

imageDigest.description: Idempotency key. Extracted from `imageRef` after the `@`.

indexHash.description: sha256 of the canonicalised `/app/index.json` inside the image.

signerPublicKey.description: Base64 of the raw Ed25519 public key bytes (32 bytes → 44 chars).

signature.description: Base64 of the raw Ed25519 signature (64 bytes → 88 chars).

publishedAt.description: Issuer-supplied timestamp inside the signed envelope.

activatedAt.description: Server-side ledger timestamp — when the register call succeeded.

projectId.description: The project the deploy named, which its primitives were registered into. Absent for a tenant-wide deploy (the tenant's Default project).

promotedFromDeploymentId.description: When this deployment was made by promoting another into the next environment of its order: the deployment it was promoted from. Absent for one deployed directly.

packId.description: The pack's id, from the image's index. Absent from a runtime that doesn't keep it.

type.description: `tool`, `agent`, `provider` or `pack`; a later runtime may add kinds, so treat an unknown one as a need not yet named.

name.description: The secret's or env value's name; for a model key, the key's secret name, or `any provider` when none is registered.

kind.description: `secret`, `env`, `model-key` or `pack-env`; a later runtime may add kinds, so treat an unknown one as a value not yet named.

foundAt.description: Where a run finds it, when it is set: the project, else its org, else the tenant.

problem.description: Why it isn't ready; absent when it is. One of a fixed list; a later runtime may add problems, so treat an unknown one as a reason not yet named. `missing`: set nowhere a run looks. `secret-not-yet`: a pack env name set only as a secret, which isn't given into a pack service's environment yet. `ambiguous`: a pack env name set both as a secret and as a plain value. `revoked`: a tool's secret revoked where it's recorded, or a model key revoked where a run looks first (a run refuses rather than read a wider one). `no-provider`: an agent that runs on any provider (it names none, or names one that isn't registered), with no provider registered in the tenant, so a run has none to call.

data.description: Every value the deployment needs in the project: each tool's secrets and env values (in the deployment's order), then each model key by provider, then the pack service's env.

toProjectId.description: The next environment of the deployment's order.

reason.description: Why, kept in the `deployment-promoted` audit record.

makeLive.description: Make every agent version the promotion carries live in the target project, each through its scope's gate. The answer's `live` reports each. An error answered after some carried agents were already pinned lists those in `error.details.live`, in `live`'s shape.

toProjectId.description: The next environment of the deployment's order.

carried.description: Carried with the build: an edit of a version it ships. Absent for one it ships.

version.description: Absent for guardrails, which have no version.
Absent for guardrails, which have no version.

kind.description: `agent` or `flow`; a later runtime may add kinds, so treat an unknown one as an item not yet named.

from.description: The version its chain of edits starts from.

policy.description: The gate policy that applied; null when none did.

approvalId.description: The approval a `pending-approval` pin waits on.

pinned.description: Live now (`true`), or waiting on a gate — an approval, or a check it failed (`false`, with `gate`).

created.description: `true`: the promotion made this deployment (`201`). `false`: the target had this build already (`200`), and only the versions it lacked were carried.

leftBehind.description: Edits of the build's agents and flows that stay behind; absent when none.

live.description: Each carried agent pinned live in the target; present only when `makeLive` was asked.

position.description: Its place in the order, from 0 (the first, which takes builds).

values.description: Each value with a problem in the target; empty when every one is ready.

envName.description: The env this runtime serves, which a run in the target reads its values under: a value is set there (`--env=<envName>` with `--scope=project:<id>`). Absent when the runtime names none, and each value is then listed unread.

leftBehind.description: Edits of the build's agents and flows that would stay behind; absent when none.

indexHash.description: sha256 of the image's `/app/index.json`, byte for byte — covered by the signature. The server reads the file from the image, checks it hashes to this, and registers what it declares.

signerPublicKey.description: PEM-encoded Ed25519 public key (`-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----\n…`). Parsed to raw bytes for verification.

signature.description: Base64 of the Ed25519 signature over canonicalise({ imageDigest, artifactVersion, indexHash, tenantId, publishedAt }) with sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8.

publishedAt.description: Issuer-supplied ISO-8601 timestamp — covered by the signature.

projectId.description: The project to deploy into, one per client: its agents, flows, tools and guardrails are registered there, and its secret sync writes there. It takes admin on that project (a key limited to another project is refused). Absent: a tenant-wide deploy, into the tenant's Default project. An id that already lives in another project is `409` (`tool-project-mismatch` and the like): each client gets its own pack, whose ids carry its own pack id. Not covered by the signature, which attests the image.

The project on every page of a list asked for with `?projectId=`, an empty one too: it holds only that environment's deployments. Absent from a runtime before Kindgi 0.1.9, which ignores `projectId` and lists them all.

packId.description: The pack on every page of a list asked for with `?packId=`, an empty one too: it holds only that pack's deployments. Absent from a runtime before Kindgi 0.1.9, which ignores `packId` and lists them all.

secrets.description: Zero or more secret entries. Each entry MUST set exactly one of `ref` (validate-only) or `value` (write new version).

ref.description: Opaque reference to an existing secret record — validated via `SecretBinding.get`; no bytes cross the wire.

value.description: Plaintext secret value written via `SecretBinding.set` with `writeMode: add-version`. The response returns only the framework-generated reference.

ref.description: Opaque reference — either echoed from the request (`{ name, ref }` entries) or freshly minted (`secret:<envName>/<name>#<version>` for `{ name, value }` entries).

EvidenceKind.description: Compliance-relevant event class. Open set: evidence is a classifier lens over the audit stream, and a deployment can mark any audit-event kind exportable. `examples` lists the built-in kinds; clients must tolerate kinds they do not know.

ComplianceEvidence.description: One evidence record — matches `@kindgi/specs/compliance-evidence.schema.json` (`payload` is a versioned document opaque to the wire schema).

projectId.description: The project the underlying audit event belongs to. Absent for tenant-level events (e.g. authz decisions).

kind.description: Compliance-relevant event class. Open set: evidence is a classifier lens over the audit stream, and a deployment can mark any audit-event kind exportable. `examples` lists the built-in kinds; clients must tolerate kinds they do not know.

payload.description: Kind-specific payload document. Always carries `version` for on-read migration; other fields vary by kind.

ExportComplianceEvidenceFilter.description: Optional filter narrowing the export set. Composition is AND — every populated field must match. Absent / empty filter exports every record for the tenant.

kind.description: Compliance-relevant event class. Open set: evidence is a classifier lens over the audit stream, and a deployment can mark any audit-event kind exportable. `examples` lists the built-in kinds; clients must tolerate kinds they do not know.

ExportComplianceEvidenceBody.description: Optional: no body exports every exportable kind, signed with the active key.

signingKeyId.description: Optional: sign with this key, one of `GET /v1/export-signing-keys`. Leave it out to sign with the deployment's active key. A key the deployment doesn't sign with is `404 signing-key-not-found`.

filter.description: Optional filter narrowing the export set. Composition is AND — every populated field must match. Absent / empty filter exports every record for the tenant.

kind.description: Compliance-relevant event class. Open set: evidence is a classifier lens over the audit stream, and a deployment can mark any audit-event kind exportable. `examples` lists the built-in kinds; clients must tolerate kinds they do not know.

SignedComplianceEvidenceBundle.description: Signed compliance evidence. Body: `{ bundleSchemaVersion, tenantId, filter, records, recordCount, exportedAt }`.

kind.description: Which export this is: `audit-bundle`, `provenance` or `compliance`. Absent from older servers.

bundle.description: Base64 of the exact bytes that were signed: the body, as sorted-key JSON with no whitespace. Verify these bytes; nothing needs re-serializing.

algorithm.description: The signing key's algorithm. `ecdsa-p256-sha256` signatures are IEEE P1363 `r‖s`. A verifier refuses an algorithm it doesn't know.

signingKeyId.description: The key that signed it: one of `GET /v1/export-signing-keys`.

signature.description: Base64 of the 64-byte signature over the `bundle` bytes: Ed25519's, or ECDSA P-256's as IEEE P1363 `r‖s`.

publicKey.description: The signing key's public half, PEM SPKI. On its own it only proves the bytes weren't changed; check it against `GET /v1/export-signing-keys` (or a key you pinned) to know who signed them.

exportedAt.description: When it was signed: the same instant as the signed body's `exportedAt`.

CreateResourceResult.description: Shared 201 response body for platform-hierarchy create endpoints — the freshly-assigned id of the created row.

orgId.description: `null` explicitly re-assigns the team out of any org (cross-org).

ProjectRole.description: Role on a project, as read. `member` is only read, on a role given before it was retired: it grants what `viewer` does, and writes refuse it.

AssignableProjectRole.description: A role to give on a project: `owner`, `admin`, `editor` or `viewer`, each including the ones after it. `member` is refused (400): give `viewer`.

TeamProjectRole.description: A team's role on a project, held by every member of the team: `admin` includes `editor`, which includes `viewer`. A team never owns a project.

TeamProjectGrant.description: A team's role on a project.

grantedAt.description: When the team was given the role. Absent from a runtime that does not record it, or for a grant from before 0.1.6.

AccessPrincipal.description: Whom access is held by: a person, or a service account.

ProjectAccessDirect.description: The principal's own role on the project. `joinedAt` when a membership stands behind it: only then do the membership routes change or remove it.

ProjectAccessTeam.description: A team's grant on the project, held by every member of the team.

ProjectAccessOrgAdmin.description: An admin of the project's org (directly or through a team): admin on the project.

ProjectAccessTenantAdmin.description: A tenant admin: admin on every project.

ProjectAccess.description: Someone with access to the project, their effective role, and every way in.

displayName.description: A person's name, or a service account's.

primaryEmail.description: A person's email: shown to the project's admins only.

role.description: The effective role: the highest any way in gives.

via.description: Every way in, the highest role first.

productionSince.description: When the project was put in production; absent while it isn't. A run in a project in production is a production run, and a run anywhere else is staging.

production.description: `true` puts the project in production; `false` takes it out.

productionSince.description: When the project went into production; `null` while it isn't in production.

orgId.description: `null` explicitly re-assigns the project out of any org (cross-org).

AddProjectMembershipBody.description: Exactly one of `userId` and `email` names the person.

email.description: The person's email, as the tenant has it.

productionAllowed.description: Whether the tenant may put projects in production. Absent from a runtime that doesn't gate production.

productionNext.description: Where to go to be allowed to put projects in production, for example a billing page. Only while `productionAllowed` is `false`, and only when the runtime names one.

state.description: On a runtime serving many tenants: `closing` (readable and exportable for its window, nothing changes) or `suspended` (the same, until restored). `closing` wins. Absent: active.

TenantPatch.description: A new name, a new slug, or both; a field left out stays as it is. The id stays, so whatever names the tenant by its id keeps working.

slug.description: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, unique across tenants. The console's addresses carry it, so links with the old one stop opening the tenant; nothing else is keyed by it.

TenantLimits.description: The tenant's limits that are set. A limit that isn't set is absent, and isn't enforced.

apiRequestsPerMinute.description: API requests a minute. Past it: 429 `rate-limit-exceeded`.

webhookReceivesPerMinute.description: Webhook deliveries received a minute, across the tenant's triggers. Past it: 429.

runsAtOnce.description: Runs executing at once. Past it, a new run waits as `pending`.

runsPending.description: Runs waiting as `pending`. Past it, a new run is refused with 429.

toolCallsInFlight.description: Tool calls in flight to the tenant's pack services. Past it, a call waits for a slot.

approvalsPending.description: Approvals waiting for a decision. Past it, the step that asks fails, naming the limit.

projectsInProduction.description: Projects in production at once. Past it, putting another project in production is refused with 403 `production-limit-reached`. Lowering it takes no project out of production.

EgressAddresses.description: The IP addresses this deployment's calls to other sites come from, for a site that admits only known addresses. They're the same for every tenant on the deployment, so admitting them admits every tenant's calls: a site still checks its own credentials. They say where calls come from, not where they go. Absent when the deployment publishes none. An empty list: none of that kind.

server.description: Where the server's own calls come from, such as its calls to MCP servers and model providers, and its webhook deliveries.

deployments.description: Where calls made by the code deployed to it come from.

allowed.description: `true` allows the tenant to put projects in production; `false` stops it.

TenantLimitsInUse.description: How much of each limit that counts something the tenant uses now, whether the limit is set or not: on `GET …/limits` only, and only from a runtime that counts it. A limit can be lowered below it: nothing is taken back, and the next one waits until the count is under the limit.

TenantConfigKind.description: Slot for a tenant config entry (tenant-scoped). `env` and `config` both address `EnvBinding`; `secret` addresses `SecretBinding`. Prefer `/v1/env/*` + `/v1/secrets/*` for new callers.

value.description: Entry value. For `kind: "secret"` this is ALWAYS `[redacted]` on this admin surface; use the `/v1/secrets/*` routes and `SecretBinding.resolve` on the dispatch path to read plaintext.

sensitive.description: When `true`, the write is routed to `SecretBinding` regardless of `kind`. `kind: "secret"` implies `sensitive: true`.

ifRevision.description: Optimistic-concurrency guard — the write fails with `tenant-config-revision-conflict` (409) unless the stored revision matches. Omit for last-write-wins.

ScopeKind.description: Discriminator for the ?scopeKind + ?scopeId + ?inherit triplet. Tenant carries no id (implicit from session); org/project require scopeId.

Scope.description: Discriminated Scope primitive (Tenant / Org / Project). Source of truth: `Scope` in `@kindgi/platform`.

recoverableUntil.description: A hard revoke left a copy your secret manager can still recover (for example Azure Key Vault's soft delete, when the vault doesn't allow a purge or the runtime isn't permitted to purge): when the secret manager purges it on its own. Setting the same name again before then can keep that copy, its values disabled, until the name is hard-revoked again. Absent on a soft revoke, and when a hard revoke left nothing recoverable.

hasMore.description: Whether there's another page. Absent from older servers: there is one when `nextCursor` is set.
Whether there's another page. Absent from older servers: there is one when `nextCursor` is set.
Whether there's another page. Absent from older servers: there is one when `nextCursor` is set.

name.description: A new secret name: 1 to 255 ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter, digit or `_`, with any `.` between two non-`.` characters. The server holds a newly-created name to this shape (`create-new`, or an `add-version` of a name not yet stored); a name already stored outside this shape still reads, rotates and takes new versions.

appEnvFile.description: Under `kindgi dev` only: write the app's own env file (the last of `dev.envFiles`, `.env.local` by default) instead of Kindgi's `.kindgi/secrets.env`, for a value the app reads too, such as a webhook signing secret. A runtime with a secrets store refuses it with `bad-input`.

recoverableUntil.description: A hard revoke left a copy your secret manager can still recover (for example Azure Key Vault's soft delete, when the vault doesn't allow a purge or the runtime isn't permitted to purge): when the secret manager purges it on its own. Setting the same name again before then can keep that copy, its values disabled, until the name is hard-revoked again. Absent on a soft revoke, and when a hard revoke left nothing recoverable.

TriggerStatus.description: Lifecycle status. Only `active` triggers fire. Tombstoned rows are excluded from every read path.

ScheduleRecord.description: A schedule: what it runs (a flow at a version, or an agent), when (a cron expression in a timezone), as whom (its owner), and what it does after a gap or while a run is still going.

scheduleId.description: Domain-friendly alias for `triggerId` — the trigger id (a UUID). Use interchangeably in admin URLs.

flowId.description: A schedule that runs a flow: the flow, at `flowVersion`.

agentId.description: A schedule that runs an agent: the agent, at `agentVersion`, else its version live for the schedule's project (else the latest), as a run that names none.

improve.description: A schedule that starts Improve runs: on this agent, for this scope, when enough answers have been marked wrong since its last Improve run (`input`: the threshold, the monthly cap and the Improve options).

projectId.description: The schedule's project: its runs are this project's.

owner.description: Who its runs act as. A person: a personal trigger, which only they or a project admin change. A service account: a shared trigger. Only a take-over (`POST …/owner`) changes it. Checked again at every fire.

cronExpression.description: 5- or 6-field cron expression (croner-compatible). 6-field enables second precision.

input.description: Static input handed to the run on every fire. Absent → `{}`.

catchUp.description: After a gap (the runtime was down, or a fire is later than `startingDeadlineSeconds`): `latest` runs once, for the latest missed occurrence, and its fire says how many it missed; `skip` drops the missed occurrences. Never a run per missed occurrence. A tenant's suspension isn't caught up either way: once the tenant is restored, a schedule that's on fires next at its first occurrence after the restore.

overlap.description: When an occurrence comes while the previous run of this schedule is still running: `skip` records the fire as skipped; `allow` starts another run.

startingDeadlineSeconds.description: How late a fire may start and still count as on time; past it, `catchUp` applies.

statusReason.description: Why the runtime paused it: repeated fires that were refused (the owner lost access) or failed. Skipped fires (an overlap, an erasure in progress) never count.

toolsAllowedUnattended.description: The tools whose calls in this schedule's runs don't wait for a person's yes, though a tool asks for one in a run no person started (`needsApprovalWhenUnattended`). Absent: none. Each tool by its id, with no wildcard or pattern, and only tools this trigger's flow or agent calls. It lifts only that wait: the tenant's approval rules, the agent's own rules, the permission check (as the trigger's owner) and the tool's own limits all still apply.

nextFireAt.description: Wall-clock time of the next scheduled fire. `null` on paused rows if the cron scheduler never re-armed.

upcoming.description: The next occurrences, when the request asked for them (`?upcoming=N`).

displayName.description: The owner's name at the time of the response: the person's display name, or the service account's name. Absent when it can't be read (no directory, a removed account) and from a runtime before Kindgi 0.1.6: show the id then.

isProjectAccount.description: Set when the owner is the trigger's project's own service account (`runAsProject`): the trigger is shared, and runs as the project. Show it as "This project". Absent otherwise.

ScheduleFire.description: One fire of a schedule (an occurrence, or a `run-now`) and what came of it. `pending` while its run is being started.

scheduledFor.description: The occurrence it is for; absent on a `run-now` fire.

outcome.description: `skipped-overlap`: the previous fire's run was still going (`overlap: skip`). `skipped-erasure`: the person the fire acts for is being erased, so no new run starts for them until the erasure completes. `skipped`, as `detail` says: what an improve schedule waits for wasn't there (its threshold, or its monthly cap); the target's project is suspended (`project-suspended`), so no run or pass started; its run or pass hadn't started when its tenant was suspended, and the restore concluded it (`tenant-suspended`); or its tenant was suspended or closing as its run started (`tenant-suspended`, `tenant-closing`). None of the skipped outcomes counts toward the auto-pause; `refused` and `failed` do, unless `countsTowardPause` is `false`. A skip for a suspension or a close (`project-suspended`, `tenant-suspended`, `tenant-closing`) doesn't reset the auto-pause's count of fires in a row either.

passId.description: The improvement pass it started (an improve schedule).

detail.description: Why it was refused, skipped or failed.

countsTowardPause.description: Whether this fire counted toward the trigger's auto-pause (5 in a row by default). `false` for a refusal for a limit, such as the tenant's runs pending (`detail` starts `rate-limited:`): the limit passes, and the trigger isn't at fault. Absent from a runtime that doesn't say: `refused` and `failed` fires counted, and the others didn't.

missedCount.description: Occurrences this fire stood in for after a gap (`catchUp: latest`).

RegisterScheduleBody.description: Name what it runs: `flowId` with `flowVersion`, `agentId` (with an optional `agentVersion`), or `improve` (improvement passes). Registering needs `write` on the project and `execute` on what it runs (`publish` on the agent for `improve`); its runs act as the caller.

agentId.description: Run an agent (instead of a flow): at `agentVersion`, else its live version.

improve.description: Start an improvement pass instead of a run (instead of `flowId` or `agentId`). Its `config.input` is the pass options; registering needs `publish` on the agent.

projectId.description: The schedule's project. Absent → the tenant's default project.

runAsServiceAccountId.description: A service account the schedule's runs act as (its owner), named by id, instead of the caller. Needs `act_as` on that account — a tenant admin holds it — and the account must itself hold the access the schedule's target needs. With an authorization store, that's checked when the account is named, and again when the schedule's target changes: an account that can't is refused (`409 trigger-owner-cannot-run-target`). Not a project's own account (409 `service-account-project-owned`: name it with `runAsProject`). Absent: the caller owns it.

runAsProject.description: `true`: the schedule's runs act as its project's own service account, made the first time with the `editor` role on the project, so it's shared. It runs only what the project's editors can. With an authorization store, that's checked when it's named, and again when the schedule's target changes: if it can't run the target, the request is refused (`409 trigger-owner-cannot-run-target`). Takes `admin` on the schedule's project (without an authorization store, a tenant-admin key), not `act_as`. Not with `runAsServiceAccountId`, and not without a project (400). A runtime that can't make the account answers 501 `trigger-operation-unsupported`. `false` or absent: as `runAsServiceAccountId` says.

input.description: What each run gets. An agent schedule's runs take the agent payload, `{ userMessage, parameters? }`, so it needs `userMessage`; a flow's take the flow's input. An improve schedule's is `ImproveScheduleInput`, kept with its defaults applied.

toolsAllowedUnattended.description: The tools whose calls in this schedule's runs needn't wait for a person's yes, though a tool asks for one in a run no person started (`needsApprovalWhenUnattended`). Naming it, `[]` included, takes `admin` on the schedule's project. Each tool by its id, with no wildcard or pattern, and only tools this trigger's flow or agent calls. It lifts only that wait: the tenant's approval rules, the agent's own rules, the permission check (as the trigger's owner) and the tool's own limits all still apply.

PatchScheduleBody.description: Change what it runs (the target fields, as at registration, which also needs `execute` on the new target), when, or its policies.

agentId.description: Run an agent (instead of a flow): at `agentVersion`, else its live version.

improve.description: Start an improvement pass instead of a run (instead of `flowId` or `agentId`). Its `config.input` is the pass options; registering needs `publish` on the agent.

input.description: What each run gets. An agent schedule's runs take the agent payload, `{ userMessage, parameters? }`, so it needs `userMessage`; a flow's take the flow's input. An improve schedule's is `ImproveScheduleInput`, kept with its defaults applied.

label.description: `null` clears the label; omit to leave unchanged.

toolsAllowedUnattended.description: Replaces the schedule's list; `[]` clears it, and absent keeps it. Naming it takes `admin` on the schedule's project. A change of what it runs (another flow or agent) while the list isn't empty must name it again, as it is or `[]`; a new version alone keeps it. Each tool by its id, with no wildcard or pattern, and only tools this trigger's flow or agent calls. It lifts only that wait: the tenant's approval rules, the agent's own rules, the permission check (as the trigger's owner) and the tool's own limits all still apply.

unregistered.description: `true` iff this call tombstoned the row; `false` on idempotent re-invocation.

WebhookSignature.description: How a webhook trigger's sender signs. `hmac-sha256`: an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body under the secret's UTF-8 bytes, in `header`, `hex` or `base64`, after an optional `prefix` (GitHub and Drupal's Webhooks module: `X-Hub-Signature-256`, hex, `sha256=`; WooCommerce: `X-WC-Webhook-Signature`, base64; Shopify: `X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256`, base64). No timestamp is signed, so only the trigger's dedupe catches a replay. `standard-webhooks`: the Standard Webhooks format (`webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature: v1,<base64>` over `{id}.{timestamp}.{body}`, a `whsec_` secret), refused past `toleranceSeconds` (default 300) from the receiver's clock; it dedupes on its `webhook-id`.

header.description: The header that carries the signature (matched case-insensitively).

prefix.description: Stripped from the header's value before decoding (e.g. `sha256=`).

WebhookTriggerRecord.description: A webhook trigger: a signed request to its `receiveUrl` starts a run of its flow, as its owner. The signing secret is never on it, only its name.

webhookId.description: The routable id in the receive URL. Route-minted (a random UUID); unique per tenant. Not a secret: the signature is what a request is checked by.

receiveUrl.description: Where the sender posts: `{public URL}/v1/hooks/{tenantId}/{webhookId}`. Absent when the deployment has no public URL configured (`KINDGI_PUBLIC_URL`); it's never taken from a request's `Host`.

projectId.description: The trigger's project: its runs are this project's.

owner.description: Who its runs act as. A person: a personal trigger, which only they or a project admin change. A service account: a shared trigger. Only a take-over (`POST …/owner`) changes it. Checked again at every delivery.

input.description: The flow's input on every delivery, in place of the event. Absent: the event (the body, parsed as JSON for a JSON content type, else its text).

hmacSecretName.description: The signing secret, by name (written with `POST /v1/secrets`, or made by `generateSecret`). Read in the env the deployment serves, at `hmacSecretScope`.

hmacSecretScope.description: Where the signing secret is read, recorded when the trigger was registered (or its secret named again). `null`: none usable, so no delivery verifies until an admin names it again. Absent on triggers registered before it was recorded: read at the tenant, as before.

signingSecret.description: Only in the answer to a register with `generateSecret`: the new signing secret, shown this once, to paste into the sender. It's stored as `hmacSecretName` in the trigger's own scope; no later read shows it.

deliveryIdHeader.description: The header whose value, with the body, is a delivery's dedupe key (WooCommerce: `X-WC-Webhook-Delivery-ID`, which is per second, not per event, so the body counts too). Absent: deliveries aren't deduped (`standard-webhooks` dedupes on its own `webhook-id`).

rateLimitPerMinute.description: Accepted deliveries a minute (default 600); past it, `429`.

statusReason.description: Why the runtime paused it (repeated refused or failed starts; a sender's failed proofs never count), when it did.

suppressedRefusals.description: Refusals and skipped deliveries this minute past the 20 recorded in its history, which only counted.

toolsAllowedUnattended.description: The tools whose calls in this trigger's runs don't wait for a person's yes, though a tool asks for one in a run no person started (`needsApprovalWhenUnattended`). Absent: none. Each tool by its id, with no wildcard or pattern, and only tools this trigger's flow or agent calls. It lifts only that wait: the tenant's approval rules, the agent's own rules, the permission check (as the trigger's owner) and the tool's own limits all still apply.

WebhookFire.description: One delivery to a webhook trigger and what came of it. A fire keeps the delivery's event only until its run starts; then only the run has it.

outcome.description: `pending` while its run starts. `skipped`: no run started, and the event was dropped: the trigger was paused (`paused`); its project was suspended after the delivery was taken, before its run started (`project-suspended`); its run hadn't started when its tenant was suspended, and the restore concluded it (`tenant-suspended`); or its tenant was suspended or closing as its run started (`tenant-suspended`, `tenant-closing`). `refused`: `detail` says why. `failed`: the run couldn't start.

detail.description: Why it was refused, skipped or failed: `signature-missing`, `signature-invalid`, `stale`, `secret-unavailable`, `unregistered`, `paused`, `rate-limited`, `body-too-large`, `body-not-json`, `body-too-deep`, or the owner's lost access. A skip for a suspension or a close names `project-suspended`, `tenant-suspended` or `tenant-closing` in it.

countsTowardPause.description: Whether this fire counted toward the trigger's auto-pause (5 in a row by default). `false` for a refusal for a limit, such as the tenant's runs pending (`detail` starts `rate-limited:`): the limit passes, and the trigger isn't at fault. Absent from a runtime that doesn't say: `refused` and `failed` fires counted, and the others didn't.

duplicates.description: Later deliveries with the same dedupe key, which started nothing.

WaitTokenAccepted.description: The runtime has the answer. It says nothing about the run: who holds a wait token's link isn't a run reader.

WebhookReceipt.description: What the receiver did with a delivery.

fireId.description: The fire recorded (or, with `duplicate`, the earlier one).

duplicate.description: An earlier fire holds this delivery's dedupe key: nothing new started.

skipped.description: No run started, and the event was dropped. `paused`: the trigger is paused, and a `skipped` fire was recorded. `tenant-suspended`, `project-suspended`: the trigger's tenant or project is suspended, and nothing was recorded.

received.description: A WooCommerce save-time ping: answered, nothing started.

projectId.description: The trigger's project; absent: the tenant's Default project.

hmacSecretName.description: The signing secret, by name: written first with `POST /v1/secrets`, and read at the first of the trigger's project, its org and the tenant that has it and that you administer (`hmacSecretScope`); or the name `generateSecret` stores a new one under. Never a model provider's key. For WooCommerce, use letters and digits only (it HTML-decodes the secret before signing). Under `kindgi dev`, `generateSecret` writes it to an env file, so the name is capital letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit (`secret-name-invalid` otherwise).

generateSecret.description: Make a new signing secret, store it as `hmacSecretName` in the trigger's own project (in the env the deployment serves), and return it once as `signingSecret`. Needs only `write` on the project. A name the project already has is refused (`secret-write-conflict`, 409), never overwritten. Letters and digits, or `whsec_…` for `standard-webhooks`.

deliveryIdHeader.description: The header whose value, with the body, dedupes deliveries. Not with `standard-webhooks`, which dedupes on its `webhook-id`.

runAsServiceAccountId.description: A service account the trigger's runs act as (its owner), named by id, instead of the caller. Needs `act_as` on that account — a tenant admin holds it — and the account must itself hold `execute` on the flow. With an authorization store, that's checked when the account is named: an account that can't is refused (`409 trigger-owner-cannot-run-target`). Not a project's own account (409 `service-account-project-owned`: name it with `runAsProject`). Absent: the caller owns it.

runAsProject.description: `true`: the trigger's runs act as its project's own service account, made the first time with the `editor` role on the project, so it's shared. It runs only what the project's editors can. With an authorization store, that's checked when it's named: if it can't run the flow, the request is refused (`409 trigger-owner-cannot-run-target`). Takes `admin` on the trigger's project (without an authorization store, a tenant-admin key), not `act_as`. Not with `runAsServiceAccountId`, and not without a project (400). A runtime that can't make the account answers 501 `trigger-operation-unsupported`. `false` or absent: as `runAsServiceAccountId` says.

toolsAllowedUnattended.description: The tools whose calls in this trigger's runs needn't wait for a person's yes, though a tool asks for one in a run no person started (`needsApprovalWhenUnattended`). Naming it, `[]` included, takes `admin` on the trigger's project. Each tool by its id, with no wildcard or pattern, and only tools this trigger's flow or agent calls. It lifts only that wait: the tenant's approval rules, the agent's own rules, the permission check (as the trigger's owner) and the tool's own limits all still apply.

Replaces the trigger's list; `[]` clears it, and absent keeps it (a new `flowVersion` too). Naming it takes `admin` on the trigger's project, and it's checked against the flow at the version the trigger will run. Each tool by its id, with no wildcard or pattern, and only tools this trigger's flow or agent calls. It lifts only that wait: the tenant's approval rules, the agent's own rules, the permission check (as the trigger's owner) and the tool's own limits all still apply.

TakeTriggerOwnerBody.description: Who the trigger's runs act as from now: for a trigger whose owner left, or to make one shared or personal. Absent, or an empty body: the caller takes it over (today's behaviour). With `runAsServiceAccountId`: that service account becomes the owner. With `runAsProject`: the project's own account does. A take-over keeps the trigger's `toolsAllowedUnattended`: change that with PATCH.

runAsServiceAccountId.description: A service account the trigger's runs act as (its owner), named by id, instead of the caller. Needs `act_as` on that account — a tenant admin holds it — and the account must itself hold what the trigger runs. With an authorization store, that's checked when the account is named: an account that can't is refused (`409 trigger-owner-cannot-run-target`). Not a project's own account (409 `service-account-project-owned`: name it with `runAsProject`).

runAsProject.description: `true`: the trigger's runs act as its project's own service account, made the first time with the `editor` role on the project, so it's shared. It runs only what the project's editors can. With an authorization store, that's checked when it's named: if it can't run what the trigger runs, the request is refused (`409 trigger-owner-cannot-run-target`). Takes `admin` on the trigger's project (without an authorization store, a tenant-admin key), not `act_as`. Not with `runAsServiceAccountId`, and not without a project (400). A runtime that can't make the account answers 501 `trigger-operation-unsupported`. `false` or absent: as `runAsServiceAccountId` says.

MailTriggerMailbox.description: The mailbox a mail trigger reads: its app (`google`: Gmail; `microsoft`: Outlook) and whose it is (`company`: the company's mailbox, through the company's connection of that app; `person`: the trigger owner's own, through their connection).

MailTriggerRecord.description: A mail trigger: each new mail in its mailbox's folder starts a run of its agent or flow, with the mail as the run's input, as its owner. In such a run, every call that changes something, or uses the run's own mailbox, waits for a person's yes unless the trigger lists it (`toolsAllowedUnattended`).

agentId.description: Run an agent (instead of a flow): at `agentVersion`, else its live version.

projectId.description: The trigger's project: its runs are this project's.

owner.description: Who its runs act as, with their connections. A service account owns a shared trigger, on the company's mailbox: one named with `runAsServiceAccountId`, or the project's own (`runAsProject`, `isProjectAccount`). A person owns a personal one: every trigger on a person's mailbox, and one on the company's mailbox registered without either. No edit moves it; only a take-over (`POST …/owner`) does.

folder.description: The Gmail label id, or the Outlook folder id or well-known name, it watches. Absent: the inbox.

pollSeconds.description: How often it looks for new mail, in seconds (default 60).

runsPerHour.description: The most runs its mail starts in an hour (default 60). Past it, a mail's fire is `refused` (`detail` starts `over-limit:`), and that mail doesn't run later.

statusReason.description: Why it isn't polling as it should: `connection-missing` (the mailbox's connection is gone or lapsed; polls go on, and work again once it's back), `owner-refused` (its owner was removed or may no longer run the target; polls go on and read nothing until that changes or an admin takes it over), or why the runtime paused it.

account.description: The mailbox's account at its last poll: the connection's account id and its label (the address). Absent before its first poll.

lastPolledAt.description: When it last polled the mailbox and got an answer.

toolsAllowedUnattended.description: The tools whose calls in this trigger's runs don't wait for a person's yes, though a run a mail started asks for one for every call that changes something or uses its mailbox. Absent: none. Each tool by its id, with no wildcard or pattern, and only tools this trigger's flow or agent calls. It lifts only that wait: the tenant's approval rules, the agent's own rules, the permission check (as the trigger's owner) and the tool's own limits all still apply.

RegisterMailTriggerBodyConfig.description: A new mail trigger's mailbox, folder and pace.

folder.description: The Gmail label id, or the Outlook folder id or well-known name, it watches. Absent: the inbox.

pollSeconds.description: How often it looks for new mail, in seconds (default 60).

runsPerHour.description: The most runs its mail starts in an hour (default 60). Past it, a mail's fire is `refused` (`detail` starts `over-limit:`), and that mail doesn't run later.

PatchMailTriggerBodyConfig.description: A mail trigger's mailbox, folder or pace, to change. An absent field keeps its value.

folder.description: The Gmail label id, or the Outlook folder id or well-known name, it watches from now. Absent: it keeps its folder, unless `mailbox` changes; then it watches the new mailbox's inbox. To watch the inbox again, name it: `INBOX` in Gmail, `inbox` in Outlook.

pollSeconds.description: How often it looks for new mail, in seconds (default 60).

runsPerHour.description: The most runs its mail starts in an hour (default 60). Past it, a mail's fire is `refused` (`detail` starts `over-limit:`), and that mail doesn't run later.

RegisterMailTriggerBody.description: Name what it runs: `flowId` with `flowVersion`, or `agentId` (with an optional `agentVersion`). Its runs' input is the mail, so it takes none. A trigger on a person's mailbox reads the caller's own mail and is theirs: it needs `write` on the project. One on the company's mailbox needs `admin` on the project. Both need `execute` on what it runs.

agentId.description: Run an agent (instead of a flow): at `agentVersion`, else its live version.

projectId.description: The trigger's project. Absent → the tenant's default project.

runAsServiceAccountId.description: On the company's mailbox only: a service account that owns the trigger, so it's shared, named by id instead of the caller. Needs `act_as` on that account, which a tenant admin holds, and the account must itself hold the access the target needs. With an authorization store, that's checked when the account is named, and again when the trigger's target changes: an account that can't is refused (`409 trigger-owner-cannot-run-target`). Not a project's own account (409 `service-account-project-owned`: name it with `runAsProject`). Absent: the caller owns it.

runAsProject.description: On the company's mailbox only. `true`: the trigger's runs act as its project's own service account, made the first time with the `editor` role on the project, so it's shared. It runs only what the project's editors can. With an authorization store, that's checked when it's named, and again when the trigger's target changes: if it can't run the target, the request is refused (`409 trigger-owner-cannot-run-target`). Takes `admin` on the trigger's project, as the company's mailbox does (without an authorization store, a tenant-admin key), not `act_as`. Not with `runAsServiceAccountId`, on a person's mailbox, or without a project (400). A runtime that can't make the account answers 501 `trigger-operation-unsupported`. `false` or absent: as `runAsServiceAccountId` says.

toolsAllowedUnattended.description: The tools whose calls in this trigger's runs needn't wait for a person's yes. Naming it, `[]` included, takes `admin` on the trigger's project. Each tool by its id, with no wildcard or pattern, and only tools this trigger's flow or agent calls. It lifts only that wait: the tenant's approval rules, the agent's own rules, the permission check (as the trigger's owner) and the tool's own limits all still apply.

PatchMailTriggerBody.description: Change what it runs (the target fields, as at registration, which also needs `execute` on the new target), its mailbox (replaced whole), folder, pace or label. A personal trigger's change is its owner's or a project admin's; a shared one's, a project admin's; and the company's mailbox, before or after, takes a project admin. The owner stays.

agentId.description: Run an agent (instead of a flow): at `agentVersion`, else its live version.

toolsAllowedUnattended.description: Replaces the list (`[]` clears it; absent keeps it). Naming it takes `admin` on the trigger's project. A new target (not just a version) or another mailbox while it lists any must name it again, as it is or `[]`. Each tool by its id, with no wildcard or pattern, and only tools this trigger's flow or agent calls. It lifts only that wait: the tenant's approval rules, the agent's own rules, the permission check (as the trigger's owner) and the tool's own limits all still apply.

MailFire.description: One mail a mail trigger found and what came of it. A thread's mail runs one at a time, oldest first.

outcome.description: `pending` while its run starts, or while an earlier mail of its thread waits or that mail's run hasn't finished (`detail` starts `thread-busy:`). `skipped`: no run started, as `detail` says: the mail is from the mailbox's own address (`own-address`), an automatic reply (`auto-submitted`), received before the trigger began watching (`before-since`), found in a mailbox that changed account before it was read (`mailbox-changed`), gone by the time it was read (`not-found`), or already had by an earlier run of its thread (`mail-already-given:`); or the poll started afresh (`cursor-reset:`). `refused`: over the trigger's `runsPerHour` (`over-limit:`), the mailbox's connection missing, lapsed or lacking a scope (`connection-missing:` and why), or the app gave the mail no thread (`no-thread-id`); a refused mail doesn't run later. `failed`: the run couldn't start.

detail.description: Why it was skipped, refused or failed, or why a `pending` fire waits.

countsTowardPause.description: Whether this fire counted toward the trigger's auto-pause (5 in a row by default). `false` for `over-limit:`, `connection-missing:` and `no-thread-id` refusals: the limit passes, connecting again ends a missing connection, and a mail with no thread is the app's doing, not the trigger's. Skips never count.

WebhookEventType.description: An event type an endpoint can subscribe to.

WebhookEndpointFilter.description: Which events reach the endpoint. Every field narrows; absent fields do not. `run.finished` is sent for top-level runs only.

projectId.description: Only runs in this project.

flowIds.description: Only runs of these flows (any version).

includeDryRuns.description: Dry runs are left out unless this is `true`.

WebhookSecretRef.description: A secret by name in the deployment's secrets store, resolved at tenant scope (the same shape as a provider's `secret_ref`). The value is `whsec_` + base64 of at least 24 random bytes (or that base64 alone); the store keeps it, the endpoint keeps only this reference.

secret.description: A new signing secret (`whsec_` + base64 of 32 random bytes). Not stored anywhere: put it in your secrets (`.env` in development, the secrets store in production) and reference it by name.

url.description: Absolute https URL (http only where the deployment allows it, e.g. development). No credentials in the URL. The deployment may refuse private network addresses (`400 webhook-url-refused`).

PatchWebhookEndpointBody.description: Fields to change; absent fields are kept. `filter` is replaced as a whole.

unregistered.description: `true` iff this call unregistered the endpoint; `false` when it was unknown or already unregistered.

ConnectionSecretRef.description: A secret by name in the deployment's secrets store, resolved at tenant scope. The registration keeps only this reference, never the value.

ConnectionOwner.description: Who owns a connection: one member (`kind: member`, with their `userId`), or the company (`kind: company`, the tenant's own account).

ConnectionAccount.description: Whose account a connection is at the app.

id.description: The account's stable id at the app.

label.description: What people see: an email address, a login.

ConnectionState.description: `working`: runs can use it. `needs-reconnecting`: the app no longer accepts it; connect again. `removing`: a disconnect is under way. `removed`: gone.

says.description: In plain words, for the person asked.

changes.description: Whether it changes anything at the app. `false` is read only.

ConnectionEntry.description: An app this server can connect to.

name.description: The app's name as people know it.

owners.description: Who may own a connection to this app.

signIn.description: How a person signs in at the app.

tenant.description: Present when the sign-in happens in a directory of the app's own (Microsoft's tenant, not a Kindgi tenant). A registration's `oauth2.tenant` names it; without `default`, each registration must give its own.

default.description: The directory a registration that names none signs in at.

permissions.description: What a tool may ask for, by permission key (`gmail.send`).

removal.description: How a disconnect withdraws access at the app, and how the app reports a removal made there. `{}` when the app has neither: a disconnect then withdraws nothing at the app, and a removal made there is not reported.

revoke.description: How a disconnect withdraws access at the app: an OAuth revoke, or revoking the GitHub App's installation tokens (the app stays installed).

revokeIsGrantWide.description: Whether the app's revoke withdraws everything the person granted the registration, not only this connection's permissions. Google's does.

notices.description: How the app reports a removal made at the app.

setupGuide.description: The docs page an admin follows to register the app.

tenant.description: The directory the app signs people in at, for an app whose sign-in names one: Microsoft's tenant id or domain for a single-tenant app, `organizations`, `common` or `consumers` for a multi-tenant one. Required when the app's entry has no default, refused for an app without one (`connection-app-invalid`, `details.field` `oauth2.tenant`).

ConnectionApp.description: A tenant's registration of its own client at an app. Secrets are references, never values.

projects.description: The projects whose runs may use its connections. Absent: every project.

redirectUrl.description: Give this to the app as its redirect URL: a GitHub App's Callback URL, with "Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation" ticked.

noticesUrl.description: Give this to the app as the place it reports removals.

CreateConnectionAppBody.description: Give `oauth2` for an app that signs in with OAuth, `githubApp` for a GitHub App.

projects.description: The projects whose runs may use its connections. Leave out for every project.

UpdateConnectionAppBody.description: Fields to change; absent fields are kept. The app itself cannot change.

connectionsRemoved.description: How many live connections the removal took with it.

Connection.description: One owner's account at an app, through a registration, in one env. Never its token.

permissions.description: The entry's permission keys the app granted.

stateReason.description: Why it's in its state: `invalid-grant` (the app withdrew the grant), `no-refresh-token` (the app gave no way to renew it), `token-missing` (its stored token is gone), `store-write-failed` (its token couldn't be stored at the connect), `installation-missing` (the GitHub App was uninstalled from the account), `installation-permissions` (an owner took permissions from the installation), `suspended` (the installation was suspended), `sessions-revoked` (Google revoked the person's sessions), `access-expired` (the app gave no refresh token, and its access token ends within a minute, or has ended). Other values may be added; `state` says what to do.

accessEndsAt.description: When its access token ends, for a connection the app gave no refresh token. From one minute before then, it needs reconnecting (`access-expired`), and reads say so too. Absent for one that renews.

connectedAt.description: When its current grant was stored: the connect, or the last reconnect.

lastUsedAt.description: When a run last used it, to the hour.

withdrawn.description: What a removal did at the app. `at-app`: access was withdrawn there. `app-failed`: the app refused the revoke; the token is gone here all the same. `kept-for-other-connection`: another live connection uses the same grant. `not-supported`: the app has no revoke that would touch only this connection.

ConnectRequest.description: A connect: the owner goes to `connectUrl`, consents at the app, and comes back. A run that needs a connection it lacks waits on one.

permissions.description: The permissions asked for: the ones needed, and the ones already granted.

says.description: What each asks for, in plain words.

reconnects.description: The connection it connects again; the same account is required.

runId.description: The run that waits for it.

name.description: The tool's name for the connection, when a run waits.

startedBy.description: Who started it last: `<kind>:<id>`. Only they may finish it.

missing.description: The permissions the app granted less than asked.

installations.description: A GitHub App's, while it's `pending`: the app's installations the person's GitHub account reaches, when the finish found several and none was picked. They pick one and start again with `installationId`, or install the app on another account with `newInstallation`.

appId.description: Which registration, when the tenant has more than one for the app.

projectId.description: When given, the registration must allow this project.

permissions.description: The entry's permission keys to ask for.

for.description: `me`: the caller's own account (signed in as a person). `company`: the company's account; a tenant admin only.

ConnectRequestInstallation.description: A GitHub App installation the person can reach.

account.description: The account it's on: its login, or the enterprise's slug.

StartConnectBody.description: Optional, and a GitHub App's only: the installation to attach, or a new one. Leave it out for any other app.

installationId.description: The installation to attach: one of the request's `installations`.

newInstallation.description: `true`: go to the app's install page to install it on another account, even when it has installations. Not with `installationId`.

FinishConnectBody.description: What the app sent back to the callback page, each as a string. Only whoever started the request may finish it.

state.description: The one the app sent back.

kind.description: `declined`: the person declined, or granted less than asked (`request.missing`). `pick-installation`: a GitHub App's person reaches several installations and picked none; the request stays `pending` with its `installations`.

reviewerSeat.description: On a server with approvals, for a member who connected: whether they have a reviewer seat, which approving a send from their own account needs.

authorizeUrl.description: The app's consent page, with a fresh sign-in state good for 10 minutes. Send the person there.

WaitingForConnection.description: A connect the run waits for: the person opens `connectUrl`, consents at the app, and the run goes on.

name.description: The tool's name for the connection.

says.description: What each permission asked for allows, in plain words.

reconnects.description: The person connected this app before, and connects it again.

ApprovalApprover.description: The one member who may decide it.

ApprovalConnection.description: The person's account the call would use.

account.description: The account's label at the app: an email address, a login.

RunTreeUsage.description: The model calls of the run tree (this run and every run it started) that the cost ledger had recorded when this run finished: a child run still running then isn't in it. `calls` counts failed calls too. Absent when the runtime records no usage.

FinishedRun.description: A finished top-level run: its identity and outcome, never its input or output. Field names match `GET /v1/runs/{runId}`.

failureMessage.description: Why the run failed or was cancelled; `null` when it completed.

failure.description: A failed run's error, as `GET /v1/runs/{runId}` reads it back: its `code`, and the error's own `details` when it has them. Absent unless the run failed, and from a runtime that doesn't send it yet; read `failureMessage` then.

agent.description: On an agent's run: the agent, the version that ran and the conversation, as `GET /v1/runs/{runId}` shows them (an agent run's `flowId` is `agent.turn`). Absent on a flow's run, and from a runtime before Kindgi 0.1.6.

id.description: Event id, also sent as the `webhook-id` header; the same on every retry.

ImprovementPassFinishedEvent.description: An improvement pass ended (`completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`): one a person started, or one an `improve` schedule did. Its outcome names the proposal it wrote, if it wrote one.

id.description: Event id, also sent as the `webhook-id` header; the same on every retry.

RequestedApproval.description: The approval an `approval.requested` event names. What it is about stays behind sign-in: no `context`, no tool call or run input.

requiredRole.description: The least reviewer role that may decide it.

assignedTo.description: The one reviewer it is assigned to, when it is.

url.description: Its page in the console, when the runtime knows its public address.

ApprovalRequestedEvent.description: An approval was asked for: a reviewer's decision is waiting. Sent once per approval (an escalation is a new approval). `projectId` in the endpoint's filter narrows it to the approval's project.

id.description: Event id, also sent as the `webhook-id` header; the same on every retry.

ImproveScheduleTarget.description: What an improve schedule works on: the agent, and the live scope its passes propose for and count judgments in.

ImproveScheduleInput.description: An improve schedule's `config.input`. Each fire counts the answers marked wrong on the agent's runs in the scope since its last Improve run, as `classWeights` counts them: by default everyone's corrections until a restricted (experts') judge class is named, then experts' only. When there are enough, across enough runs and judges, it starts an Improve run on fresh test cases from those runs; otherwise the fire is `skipped`, saying which count was short. An Improve run that suggests a change asks for the review at once.

budget.description: Each pass's budget (default $5 and 30 candidates), never more than what's left of the month's cap.

threshold.description: Default 5 judgments, across 3 runs, from 2 judges.

monthlyCapUsd.description: The most its passes may cost in a calendar month (UTC). Default 20.

WebhookEvent.description: The JSON body of every webhook request.

WebhookDeliveryStatus.description: `pending`: waiting for its next attempt. `delivered`: the endpoint answered 2xx. `failed`: every attempt failed, or the endpoint was unregistered first; redeliver queues it again.

lastResponseStatus.description: HTTP status of the last attempt; `null` when it got no response.

LicensePreview.description: This build's own expiry: a preview release stops starting 90 days after it was released, in every mode, unless a production key exempts it. Absent when nothing expires: a build from source, or a production key.

expiresAt.description: From then on, it no longer starts: `releasedAt` plus 90 days.

daysLeft.description: Whole days until then; negative once it has passed.

standing.description: `expiring`: 30 days or fewer left. `expired`: past it: this server runs on, but won't start again; run a newer release.

thumbprint.description: The key's RFC 7638 thumbprint, to compare with the one the site shows.

vouching.description: Whether the site's statements are accepted.

peopleCap.description: At most this many live people from the site.

newPeoplePerDay.description: At most this many new people from the site per day.

audience.description: What the site's statements carry as `aud`: this deployment's public URL, given at enrollment.

origin.description: An https:// origin with no path; http:// only for localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1].

roleMap.description: Default: both default roles may ask, and decide as `standard` reviewers. An allowed role with no entry signs in to read the project only.

UpdateSiteBody.description: The settings to change; the rest stay as they are.
