400.description: Malformed request body, or the body's `projectId` isn't a project id (a UUID). Or `reference-out-of-scope`: the agent or flow isn't registered in the named `projectId`'s project, its org or the tenant (`details.issues`).

401.description: Missing / malformed / expired / revoked bearer token.

403.description: No `execute` on the agent or flow; or, for one more than one project serves run in one of its projects (the one named, else the conversation's, else a project-scoped key's when it is one of them, else its first), no `call` there for an agent (`caller` or `editor`) or `execute` there for a flow (`executor` or `editor`), asked in place of its own `execute` and of `write` on a named project; otherwise, naming a `projectId` without `write` on it; or a turn run as a participant whose memory the caller may not read (`participant-not-allowed`; for a conversation's stored participant, only to a caller who can read the conversation). A turn runs with its participant's memory (the conversation's stored participant, else `input.participantId`), so running as one takes being them (a person, by their user id) or `write` on the turn's project, as reading their memory does. A turn into a conversation with no participant takes having opened it (the caller `?openedBy=me` names) or `write` on its project (on its agent, for a conversation from before projects): `permission-denied`, with `details.resource` the conversation, to a caller who can read it.

404.description: Agent or flow not found; or `projectId` names no project of this tenant (`project-not-found`); or `input.conversationId` names no conversation of this tenant (`conversation-not-found`), answered before any turn starts, with `options.wait: false` too. A caller who can't read the conversation gets the same answer, byte for byte, in place of the 409 for a turn naming another project, of the 403 for a turn into it they may not add (a conversation with no participant, or `participant-not-allowed` for its stored participant), or of the 409 for a closed conversation they may not add a turn to.

409.description: Idempotency-Key was reused with a different body; or `projectId` names a project other than `input.conversationId`'s (`conversation-project-mismatch`, with `details.projectId` and `details.conversationProjectId`): a conversation belongs to one project, so name its own or omit `projectId`; or an erasure of the turn's person (its conversation or its `participantId`) is in progress (`erasure-in-progress`): no new turn starts for them until it completes; or the run's project is suspended (`project-suspended`): no run starts in it until it's restored; or `input.conversationId` names a closed conversation (`conversation-closed`, with `details.conversationId`): it takes no new turns, so start a new one. It's answered before a run is made, with `options.wait: false` too, and only once the caller may add the turn: the 404 and 403 rules come first.

413.description: The request body is over the API's limit (`request-too-large`; `details.maxBytes` says how much).

429.description: A limit of the tenant's (set by the runtime's operator): past its limit on runs waiting to start, `rate-limit-exceeded` with `details.limit: 'runs-pending'`, with the limit in `details.runsPending`; a turn whose gate asked for an approval past its limit on approvals waiting for a decision, `approvals-pending-limit` (`details.approvalsPending`), when the call waits for the run (with `options.wait: false`, the call answers 202 and the run fails with that code). On a server with budgets kept per tenant (Kindgi Cloud), also `rate-limit-exceeded` when work the agent's turn needed was refused, because this tenant's work of that kind took `details.budgetMs` in the last 60 seconds: `details.limit` names the budget, `template-render-time` (rendering instructions templates) or `schema-compile-time` (compiling schemas). The turn's run failed with this error (`details.runId`); `Retry-After` says when to start the turn again.

500.description: Server error (unmapped domain code or framework crash).

post.description: One primitive, discriminated subject (`agent` XOR `flow`). When the deployment issues public run tokens, the response carries `publicAccessToken`: a read-only token for this run (15 minutes by default) to hand to a browser, which follows the run with it on `GET /v1/runs/{runId}/progress` and its stream.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Caller-supplied idempotency key, scoped to the caller: the same key from someone else in the tenant is their own request (from 0.1.5). Retries with the same key return the original response byte-identical (per `docs/API-ROUTE-CONVENTIONS.md` §3.1). A retry sent while the first request still runs is answered `409 idempotency-key-in-flight` with `Retry-After`, on a runtime whose store holds keys (from 0.1.5); retry after it, and you get the first request's answer. An answer that carries a secret (a new API key or public run token, a session token, a generated signing secret) isn't kept: a retry gets `409 idempotency-key-replay-withheld`, with the first request's status and when it succeeded (from 0.1.5).

post.summary: Answer a run's wait for another system

200.description: The run after the answer: running again, finished, or waiting at its next wait (`waitingFor`).

400.description: `bad-input`: no `waitpointId`, or a field the body doesn't take. `wait-token-output-invalid` (`details.issues`): the value doesn't fit the tool's output schema, and the wait stays open.

post.description: Answers a run paused on a tool call until another system answers (a pack tool that declares `pauses`; its waitpoint id starts with `pause:`, as the run's `waitingFor.tokens` lists it), as that system would through the wait token's link, and resumes the run in the same request. `value` is the tool's output, checked against its output schema; absent, `{}`. Answering stands in for the other system, and the run acts on the answer, so it needs `write` on the run's project and `execute` on the agent or flow it runs, as starting it does. The same answer again is accepted again, even after the run has ended; a different one to a wait that's over is `409 wait-token-closed`. Every other waitpoint belongs to an approval or to the runtime itself, and is `422 run-resume-not-supported`: a run waiting for an approval continues when a reviewer decides it (`POST /v1/approvals/{approvalId}/complete`).

Under `kindgi dev`, `promotion-superseded` also when a pack file the version's data blocks go into changed since the version was made, or the block left the pack; the message names the file. Or `registry-read-only`: under `kindgi dev`, a scope narrower than the whole tenant, since the pack's files serve every scope.

429.description: `approvals-pending-limit`: the gate wants an approval, and the tenant's approvals waiting for a decision are at its limit (set by the runtime's operator). Nothing is recorded.

501.description: `promotion-gate-unsupported`: a gate policy applies, and the deployment can't record a gated promotion.

post.description:
Pins `version` live for `scope`: runs in that scope that don't name a version use it, from the next run. Open conversations keep their version. The version must be registered and active. Every promotion is recorded, with who asked and why. Needs `promote` on the agent.

With a gate policy for the scope (`GET …/gate-policy`), the promotion is checked first against the comparison named by `evalRunId`: `201` promoted; `202` the gate passed and the policy wants a reviewer's approval (a HITL approval, subject `agent-promotion`; the live version moves once it's approved, if nothing changed meanwhile); `422 gate-failed` with `details.promotionId`, `details.policy` and every check in `details.checks`. A refused promotion is recorded too.

A pin in place skips the gate: when the scope has no live version of its own and already serves exactly `version` (from a scope above, or as the latest), pinning it there changes nothing any run gets, so it is promoted (`201`) with one passing `pinInPlace` check, no comparison and no approval, its reason starting `pin-in-place`. It is re-checked as it is written; if the scope moved meanwhile, `409 promotion-superseded`: check again.

Under `kindgi dev`, nothing is pinned, since the pack's files are what runs: making a version live writes the data blocks it changes into the pack's own files (each block's new version and content, and a prompt's template into its template file), and the dev server reloads them. Only for the whole tenant, which the pack's files serve. If one of those files changed since the version was made (the changed block's file holds another version than the one its proposal changed, or another block's file a version not older), or the block left the pack, `409 promotion-superseded`, and the message names the file; an approval's decision settles it `superseded` the same way.

post.description: The runtime looks for better values for the version's tunable settings (keys its settings blocks' schemas mark `x-kindgi-tunable`) on the test set, within the budget, and writes its best candidate as an improvement proposal, which waits for a reviewer when requested. It answers at once with the pass, `running`. The pass works in one project, as an improve schedule does: `projectId`, else the scope's project, else (a tenant or org scope) the agent version's. The test set must be one that project reaches, and the pass's eval runs run there; its proposal's version is made where the agent's versions are. The body is the start body of `POST /v1/proposals/improve`, resolved and reach-checked the same way: an unknown or inactive `fromVersion` (or the version serving the scope) answers `404 agent-version-not-found`, and a test set or scope the pass's project doesn't reach answers `400 reference-out-of-scope`, exactly as `improve` would. `estimatedCostUsd` is `min(budget.maxCostUsd, the replay count times the version's mean cost over its recent completed runs)` — clamped to the budget cap — and is absent when the version has no cost history; `basis` gives the unclamped inputs: the replay count, and that mean when there is one. post.description: Body is a full `ProviderMetadata`. Server validates shape: provider-level `id` + `region` non-empty; `models[]` non-empty with unique `name` per entry; per-model `contextWindow` positive integer; per-model `features` against the closed enum; per-model `cost` non-negative; optional per-model `p95LatencyMs` / `maxOutputTokens` well-shaped; optional `labels` within their limits — same rules as `@kindgi/capabilities.createProviderRegistry`. Secrets (API keys, endpoints) are NOT part of the wire shape; deployments store them inside the binding. When the runtime has the adapter the body names, that adapter checks the registration first (its `adapter_config`, the metadata and the presence of `secret_ref`; static: no network, no secret read): a problem refuses it with `422 provider-config-invalid`. A model provider's key is used by its provider only: a `secret_ref` naming a secret that a tool, an MCP endpoint or a webhook endpoint already uses is refused (`409 provider-key-in-use`), and from then on the name is refused to tools and endpoints.

post.description: Body is a full `MCPEndpoint` plus the scope to register it in (`scopeKind` + `scopeId`); authorization checks that scope. Server validates the closed transport enum + the `config.transport` matches `transport` guardrail + per-variant required fields (`command` for stdio; `url` for http-sse / streamable-http), and refuses unknown fields. `secretRef` names a secret in the deployment's store — plaintext secrets never cross the wire — and never a model provider's key (`400 provider-key-refused`). Where each secret it names is read is recorded on it now (`secretScopes`): the first of its own scope, its project's org and the tenant that has the secret and that the caller administers, else the broadest they administer; the runtime reads it there only. A deployment with `KINDGI_TENANT_HOST_ACCESS=deployed` (the default outside development) refuses a `stdio` endpoint, which would run a command on the server's host: `403 host-access-denied`.

post.description: Publishes a `judged` eval suite version whose cases are copies of judged runs of one agent (optionally one version) or flow, newest first, at most 1000. Each case holds the run's input, what the turn read (`context`), the judged output, and each item's judgments summed up: yes and no counts, the weight behind yes and behind all judgments (an unclassified judgment counts 1), and the reasons. `judgeClassIds` counts only judgments of those classes; `minJudgments` leaves out runs with fewer; `segments` keeps only runs started in that segment path or below it. Needs `admin` on the project.

parameters.description: EvalSuiteId — stable string chosen by the caller (e.g. `acme.drafting-accuracy`).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Caller-supplied idempotency key, scoped to the caller: the same key from someone else in the tenant is their own request (from 0.1.5). Retries with the same key return the original response byte-identical (per `docs/API-ROUTE-CONVENTIONS.md` §3.1). A retry sent while the first request still runs is answered `409 idempotency-key-in-flight` with `Retry-After`, on a runtime whose store holds keys (from 0.1.5); retry after it, and you get the first request's answer. An answer that carries a secret (a new API key or public run token, a session token, a generated signing secret) isn't kept: a retry gets `409 idempotency-key-replay-withheld`, with the first request's status and when it succeeded (from 0.1.5).

The deployment may check the configuration (OIDC discovery, SAML metadata): `422 identity-provider-invalid` says what failed. The answer carries the stored provider when the deployment returns it, with `signIn`: what to give the identity provider.

get.description: Public: nobody is signed in yet. With `email`, the ways in for that email's domain: the identity providers of the one tenant the domain is verified for (an unverified domain offers none), then any the deployment offers everyone it has added (`owner: deployment`, "Continue with Google"); without, an empty list: sign-in is email first, so nothing is offered before an email. `methods` says which ways in the deployment allows: identity providers, an API token (`POST /v1/auth/token-sign-in`), and an emailed sign-in link (`emailLink`, with a captcha site key when it needs one); `identityProviders` and `apiToken` both `false` when nobody can sign in to the console. Always mounted. The answer depends only on the domain: two people at the same domain get the same answer, whether or not either has an account. Lookups with an email are rate-limited per client (`429 rate-limit-exceeded`, with `Retry-After`); a read without one, the same for everyone, isn't counted.

200.description: Signed in: the session cookie is set.

400.description: Signed in by a session, not an API token (`token-sign-in-needs-an-api-token`).

post.description: The API token in `Authorization` is exchanged once for a browser session in the session cookie (HttpOnly; the same as a sign-in with an identity provider), so the browser never keeps the token. Only a person's full key opens a session: a service account's key, or a narrowed one (a `member` role, or one project), is refused `403 token-sign-in-not-allowed`. The session ends after its lifetime, when the key expires if sooner, or when the key is revoked: each request on it reads the key, and one revoked or gone answers `401 auth-revoked`. `403 token-sign-in-off` when the deployment doesn't allow it, or can't read its API keys to check such a session (always mounted, so a console gets that answer); `400 token-sign-in-needs-an-api-token` when the request is already signed in by a session. `403 second-factor-required` in a workspace that requires a second factor at sign-in, which a token can't give.

post.description: Requires a session token (`kgi_sk_*`); bearer tokens are managed via `/v1/tokens`. The session token rotates: the new session keeps the person, scopes and expiry, and the provider is not called. OAuth 2.1 BCP refresh-token rotation: the OLD session token is invalidated (marked rotated) — reusing it after refresh returns `401 refresh-token-invalid` so compliant clients can retry with the fresh token instead of prompting a re-auth. A browser session (the session cookie) is not refreshed: `400 cookie-session-not-refreshable`, so a new token never reaches page scripts; it ends at its TTL. Nor is a session limited to a project or a role: `400 limited-session-not-refreshable`; get a new one where you got this one.

When `image-unverifiable` comes from a failed registry read, `details.cause` names why: `image-not-found`, `image-file-not-found`, `image-registry-unreachable`, `image-registry-unauthorized`, `image-unreadable` (a layer that isn't a readable archive), or `image-limit-exceeded`, with the bound in `details.limit` (`manifest`, `file`, `layer`, `read` or `unpack`: the image's own, so the same image is refused again). The tenant's hour of image reads passes, so it answers `429`. A tool that declares or sends a model provider's key, or a secret under the reserved `kindgi.` prefix, is one such issue (`path` `/secrets/<name>`): a tool never gets a model provider's key or one of Kindgi's own secrets. An agent's `output.schema`, or a flow's loop, fanout branch or subgraph `outputSchema` or its `output.schema`, that doesn't compile is one too (`path` where it sits, such as `/output/schema` or `/nodes/<i>/branches/<k>/outputSchema`), as `defineAgent` and the flow loader refuse it: every turn or run would. A tool whose `metadata` has a key under `kindgi.` (the runtime's own) is a `validation-failed` detail at `/metadata/<key>`. Or `reference-out-of-scope`: an agent or flow names a tool, agent, flow, guardrail or data block that neither the deployment brings nor its project reaches (`details.issues`, at `/agents/<i>/…` or `/flows/<i>/…`); nothing is registered.

Or, on a runtime serving many tenants (`KINDGI_TENANCY=multi`), where each tenant deploys only its own images: `image-not-allowed`, the image is outside the tenant's repository (`details.imagePrefix`, its own), or `image-prefix-unset`, the tenant has no repository set yet; both are checked before any registry read, and never on a runtime serving one tenant. Or `tool-project-mismatch`, `agent-project-mismatch`, `flow-project-mismatch` or `block-project-mismatch`: one of the image's tools, agents, flows or data blocks belongs to another project (`details.primitive`, `details.id`; the message doesn't name the project); nothing was deployed, even when it was unchanged. Or `block-already-registered`: the runtime holds one of the pack's data block versions with other content, and a version never changes; or holds versions of the pack's blocks unregistered, by hand or by the rollback of a deploy that failed after publishing them, and a deploy never reinstates one (`details.primitive` is `block`, `details.id` is `<id>@<version>`, the first such block); the message says to give it a new version, or names each unregistered one with the command that reinstates it; nothing was deployed. Or `tool-already-registered`: the runtime holds one of the pack's tool versions, active or unregistered, with another definition, and a version never changes (`details.primitive` is `tool`, `details.id` is `<id>@<version>`, `details.fields` the fields of its definition that differ: the manifest's top-level fields, and `modulePath` for where its code lives in the pack). A new image of the same tool isn't another definition: its image and artifact version aren't compared. The message says to give the tool a new version; nothing was deployed. Or `tool-kind-mismatch`: one of the image's tools has the id of an MCP endpoint's tool (`details.endpointId`; `details.primitive`, `details.id`), whose active versions are all the endpoint's; nothing was deployed. Or `project-suspended`: the project the deploy goes into (the named one, or the Default for a tenant-wide deploy) is suspended, and nothing deploys into it until it's restored. Or `environment-takes-promotions`: the project the deploy goes into is a later environment of an environment order, which takes builds only by promotion from the one before it; deploy into the order's first environment and promote the build from there (`details.firstProjectId`, when you can read that project; `details.position`, the project's place from 0). Nothing is written. Or `registry-read-only`: this registry takes no writes (under `kindgi dev`, the pack's files are the source); the message says what to do instead.

Or `details.limit: "tenant-unpack-hour"`, on a server that bounds each tenant's image reads (Kindgi Cloud): this tenant's image reads unpacked as much as they may in an hour. post.description: Atomic transaction: check the signing key against the tenant's trust list (the `signingKeyRegistry` binding), verify the Ed25519 signature over the canonical envelope, read the image's `/app/index.json` and verify it hashes to the signed `indexHash` and names the signed `artifactVersion` (`ImageRegistryBinding`), validate every tool / guardrail / agent / flow / data block it declares (the image's index is what registers; the request carries none), upsert into the corresponding registries (in the body's `projectId`, one project per client, else the tenant's Default project), then record the deployment. The pack's data blocks (the index's `blocks`) are published first, as `POST /v1/blocks` publishes a version: a version the runtime holds with the same content is kept, and the agents' block ranges pin over the runtime's versions and the pack's, the newest in range. Its tools are checked the same way before anything is written: a tool version the runtime holds is kept only with the same definition (`409 tool-already-registered`). A runtime that does this lists `deploy-publishes-pack-blocks` in `info["x-kindgi-capabilities"]` of `/v1/openapi.json`. Where each tool's secrets are read is recorded on its version (`RecordedSecretScope`); one set nowhere yet is read where this deployment's secrets sync writes (`POST /v1/deployments/{deploymentId}/secrets`), the scope this route needs `admin` on. All-or-nothing rollback on any failure. Idempotency: same `imageDigest` re-submitted returns 200 with the existing record (no new version bump). `Idempotency-Key` also applies at the HTTP layer.

delete.description: A tombstone, not an erase: from then on the org is gone from get and list, and its slug is free for a new org. Its projects and teams stay, without an org; when one of those projects has the slug of a project that has none, nothing is deleted: `409 slug-conflict` names the slugs (rename or move those projects first). When the org is the parent of an environment order, nothing is deleted either: `409 org-has-environment-order` names the order (a tenant admin clears it first). In the Kindgi runtime, the org's own secrets and secret mappings are deleted with it, for good, and its own environments and MCP endpoints are unregistered. A retention policy on the `org` domain purges the org's row. Idempotent: deleting an unknown or already-deleted org returns 204.

Every request that doesn't prove its sender (an unknown tenant or id, a missing, wrong or stale signature, a secret that can't be read) is `401 webhook-refused`, with the reason only in the trigger's history and the access audit; the URL isn't a secret, the signature is. A suspended tenant or project takes a signed one without keeping it: `202` with `skipped`, nothing recorded or started, and the event isn't kept, so a sender that can redeliver by hand (GitHub) can resend it once it's restored. post.description: A wait token's link: a pack tool that declares `pauses` hands it to the system that will answer, and the run waits for that answer. No sign-in, and a bearer token, if sent, is never read: the token in the path is the credential, and it answers one wait of one run, nothing else. The body is the answer itself, the tool's output, as JSON; an empty body is `{}`. It's checked against the tool's output schema. The same answer again (by its canonical JSON) is accepted again, even after the run has ended, so a sender may retry. An answer that comes before the run reaches its wait is held for it, and dropped if the run never waits on this token (the tool answered at once, or its step was retried); the link then answers `409 wait-token-closed`, `unused`. The answer comes back at once, and the run resumes behind it. The link stops working when the wait ends: the run is cancelled, its time passes, or the tool answered without waiting. The answer is data from outside, never instructions.

200.description: The person, in the tenant again.

post.description: For one of the site's people removed in Kindgi (`POST /v1/identity/users/{userId}/unregister`) while the site still knows them: they're in the tenant again, the same person, with their history, and their next sign-in through the site is theirs again. Their grants come back with that sign-in, from the site's role map then; their API keys and sessions stay gone. Refused, with nothing changed (`409 site-person-restore-refused`, `details.reason`): `not-removed` for someone in the tenant whose site still knows them; `left` when their site said they left it, removed in Kindgi too or not: a site forgets a person who leaves, and signs them in as a new person if they come back; `linked-elsewhere` when they also sign in another way (through another site, or the tenant's own sign-in), which letting them back in would open too: add them again instead, as a new person. A paused site's people can be let back in; an unregistered site's can't. Tenant admins only. Mounted when the deployment's site binding can let people back in.

post.summary: A site posts its public key with its enrollment code

200.description: The site's id and its statements' audience.

400.description: A malformed body, or a public key that isn't an Ed25519 JWK with a `kid`, or has a private part (`site-key-invalid`); it's checked before the code.

401.description: The code was refused (`site-enrollment-refused`).

413.description: The body is over 4096 bytes (`site-request-too-large`).

429.description: Too many failures from this client.

post.description: Public: the code is the credential. The site keeps its private key; Kindgi stores the public one, and answers the site's id (its statements' `iss`) and the audience (their `aud`). A wrong, used or expired code, or one for a paused or unregistered site, gets one answer: `401 site-enrollment-refused`. Failures are limited per client (`429 rate-limit-exceeded`, with `Retry-After`). The body is at most 4096 bytes.

post.summary: A site signs one of its people in

400.description: A malformed body, or a statement that isn't a compact JWS.

401.description: The statement was refused (`site-sign-in-refused`, `details.reason`).

413.description: The body is over 4096 bytes (`site-request-too-large`).

429.description: Too many requests from this client or for this site.

post.description: Public: the statement is the credential. A registered site's statement that a person is signed in there, exchanged for a session limited to the site's project: it reads nothing above the project, mints no keys, isn't refreshed, and ends early when the site is paused or unregistered, or one of its keys revoked. The person is the one the site created for that `sub` (a first statement creates them; never matched by email), with the grants the site's role map gives their roles. Every refusal is `401 site-sign-in-refused`, with `details.reason`. A statement whose signature wasn't verified gets `not-verified` alone, whatever was wrong (the site, the key, the signature, the format), since its sender has proved nothing; after a verified signature: `site-paused`, `site-not-vouching`, `wrong-audience`, `expired`, `issued-in-the-future`, `too-long-lived`, `replayed`, `role-not-allowed`, `person-removed` or `people-cap`. Rate-limited per client and per site (`429 rate-limit-exceeded`, with `Retry-After`). The body is at most 4096 bytes.
